topics: Basic concepts: scarcity, choice, scale of preference and opportunity cost
Economic systems
Tools of analysis: tables, graphs, mean, median and mode

Theory of supply: law of supply, determinants, shifts and movements
Price determination, equilibrium, price control and elasticity

Agriculture in the Nigerian economy
Industrialisation, location of industries and business organisations
Natural resources and the petroleum industry in Nigeria
Population: theories, census and structure
International trade: comparative advantage, balance of payments, terms of trade, exchange rates
International economic organisations
Labour market: wages, unemployment and trade unions
Business organisations
Distributive trade

questions.q: Which of the following best defines the concept of scarcity in Economics?
o: A temporary shortage of food items caused by bad weather
The limitation of resources relative to unlimited human wants
A situation where commodities are completely unavailable in the market
The deliberate hoarding of goods by wicked merchants to cause inflation
questions.e: Scarcity means that human wants are endless, but the resources available to satisfy them are limited. It does not mean total absence, but rather inadequate supply relative to demand.
questions.p: Scarcity mean say human want no get limit, but the resources wey we get to satisfy them small pass wetin we need. E no mean say the thing no dey at all o.

questions.q: Mr. Okoro has ₦50,000 and must choose between buying a generator for his shop or paying for his child's school fees. He decides to pay the school fees. The generator he left behind represents his:
o: Scale of preference
Money cost
Opportunity cost
Real cost
questions.e: Opportunity cost is the real cost of making a choice, measured in terms of the next best alternative forgone. The generator is the next best alternative he sacrificed.
questions.p: Opportunity cost na the value of that second best option wey person come drop because e choose another one. Na the generator wey e no buy be im opportunity cost.

questions.q: Why is the study of Economics described as the science of choice?
o: Because resources are unlimited and free for everyone
Because the government dictates what every citizen must produce
Because individuals are naturally greedy and selfish
Because resources are scarce, forcing individuals to decide what to forego
questions.e: Because resources are scarce and wants are unlimited, rational individuals and societies must constantly make choices. Economics studies how these choices are made.
questions.p: Because resources small and want plenty, human beings must choose wetin dem go do first. Economics na the study of how we dey make these wise choices.

questions.q: A rational consumer arranges her needs in descending order of importance starting with the most pressing. This arrangement is known as:
o: A scale of preference
A budget line
An opportunity cost table
A demand schedule
questions.e: A scale of preference is a list of unsatisfied wants arranged in order of their relative importance. It helps the consumer make optimal choices under scarcity.
questions.p: Scale of preference na the list of things wey person want to buy, arrange from the most important one to the least important one.

questions.q: Which of the following is considered a free good in economic terms?
o: Borehole water sold in Jerry cans in a crowded city
Sunlight harnessed by solar panels
Fertilizer distributed freely by the Ministry of Agriculture
Unpolluted air in the atmosphere
questions.e: A free good is a gift of nature available in unlimited quantities, requiring no cost to obtain. Atmospheric air is free, whereas fertilizer and borehole water require human effort and resources to provide.
questions.p: Free good na gift from nature wey plenty well well and person no dey pay money to get am, like ordinary air wey we dey breathe.

questions.q: The fundamental economic problem facing both developed and developing nations is:
o: Corruption and bad governance
Scarcity of economic resources
Excessive population growth
Inflation and unemployment
questions.e: Scarcity is the universal economic problem that affects every society regardless of its level of development. Every country has limited resources to satisfy unlimited wants.
questions.p: The main wahala wey rich and poor countries dey face na scarcity. No country get everything wey im citizens need.

questions.q: An economic good is different from a free good because an economic good:
o: Cannot be touched or seen physically
Is provided solely by the federal government
Commands a price and is limited in supply
Is consumed only by wealthy individuals
questions.e: Economic goods are scarce relative to demand and therefore command a price in the market. Free goods are unlimited and have a zero price.
questions.p: Economic good na the one wey scarce and person must pay money before e get am, unlike free good wey dey free of charge.

questions.q: Chioma had three options for her Saturday afternoon: sleeping (valued at ₦500), reading a novel (valued at ₦1,200), and attending a birthday party (valued at ₦2,000). She chose to attend the birthday party. What is her opportunity cost?
questions.e: Opportunity cost is the value of the *next best* alternative forgone, not the sum of all alternatives. Since the party is her first choice, her next best alternative is reading the novel valued at ₦1,200.
questions.p: Opportunity cost na just the value of that very next best option wey you drop. Since party na number one, reading novel wey worth ₦1,200 na im be the opportunity cost.

questions.q: Why does opportunity cost increase as an economy produces more of one good and less of another?
o: Because consumers change their tastes and preferences randomly
Because resources are specialized and not equally adaptable to alternative uses
Because the government increases taxes on production
Because all resources are equally efficient in the production of all goods
questions.e: Resources are not equally efficient in all uses (they are specialized). As we shift resources from one industry to another, we must give up increasingly larger amounts of the other good.
questions.p: Resources no be jack-of-all-trades; some workers or machines better for one work pass another. As you dey shift them go another work, you go dey lose more of the other product.

questions.q: The concept of scale of preference is important to a consumer primarily because it:
o: Enables the consumer to maximize satisfaction within a limited budget
Guarantees that the consumer will become a millionaire
Ensures that all human wants are fully satisfied
Eliminates scarcity permanently from the household
questions.e: A scale of preference guides a consumer to spend limited income on the most urgent needs first, thereby achieving maximum satisfaction (utility) despite scarcity.
questions.p: Scale of preference dey help person use im small money buy the most important things first so that im belle go full well well.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes 'choice' in economic analysis?
o: Buying goods only when merchants announce a massive price slash
The government's decision on which factories to privatize
Selecting one alternative while ignoring all other available goods forever
The process of prioritizing needs and selecting the most preferred option due to scarcity
questions.e: Because we cannot have everything due to scarcity, we must make choices by selecting our most preferred alternatives based on our scale of preference.
questions.p: Choice na when you select the exact thing wey you want most from the plenty options wey dey ground, because your pocket no carry everything.

questions.q: Which of the following economic systems is primarily characterized by private ownership of the means of production and the operation of the price mechanism?
o: Traditional economy
Command economy
Capitalist economy
Socialist economy
questions.e: Capitalism relies on private individuals owning property and resources, using market prices to guide production. Other systems rely heavily on government control or customs.
questions.p: Na capitalism be system wey private people dey own business and property, and na market price dey direct how things dey produce. Government no too put mouth for inside.

questions.q: A major advantage of a socialist economic system over a capitalist system is that socialism places greater emphasis on:
o: Consumer exploitation through high markups
Unrestricted freedom of enterprise
Maximization of private profits
Equitable distribution of national wealth
questions.e: Socialism aims to reduce massive wealth disparities by letting the state control major resources and provide welfare. Profit maximization is the core goal of capitalism.
questions.p: Socialism dey make sure say government share money and wealth well well among everybody so poverty no go too plenty. E dey differ from capitalism wey dey find only profit.

questions.q: In a mixed economy, the public sector and the private sector are expected to:
o: Complement each other in the production of goods and services
Eliminate the profit motive entirely from society
Compete directly in all economic activities without regulation
Operate independently with zero interaction
questions.e: A mixed economy combines state intervention with private enterprise. Both sectors work together to solve society's economic problems.
questions.p: For mixed economy, government and private people dey join hand work together to produce goods and services. Dem dey complement each other to help citizens.

questions.q: Which of the following countries' economic framework closely reflects a centrally planned or socialist system historically?
o: Federal Republic of Nigeria
United Kingdom
Democratic People's Republic of Korea (North Korea)
United States of America
questions.e: North Korea operates a strict command or socialist economy where the state controls almost all economic decisions. Nigeria, the US, and the UK are mixed or capitalist economies.
questions.p: North Korea na example of country wey government dey control almost everything wey concern business and production. Nigeria and US na mixed and capitalist systems.

questions.q: The fundamental economic problem of resource allocation in a capitalist economy is primarily solved through:
o: Customs and ancestral traditions
The forces of demand and supply
Government rationing boards
Central planning committees
questions.e: Capitalism uses the price mechanism, driven by demand and supply, to determine what to produce, how to produce, and for whom to produce.
questions.p: Under capitalism, na demand and supply price system dey solve the question of how to share scarce resources. Wetine people want naim market go provide.

questions.q: What is the primary motive for production in a purely capitalist economic system?
o: Profit maximization by private individuals
Preservation of cultural heritage
Philanthropic service to humanity
State directives and quota fulfillment
questions.e: Private entrepreneurs invest capital in a capitalist system specifically to earn profits. Philanthropy and quotas belong to other systems.
questions.p: The main reason why people dey open business for capitalist system na to make profit. Na money business be for dem.

questions.q: A common criticism leveled against a socialist economy is that it often results in:
o: Excessive consumer sovereignty
Inefficiency and lack of innovation due to absence of competition
Severe unemployment arising from private sector downsizing
Uncontrollable inflation caused by private monopolies
questions.e: State monopolies in socialism lack profit-driven competition, which can lead to poor service quality and slow innovation. Private monopolies belong to capitalism.
questions.p: Because government dey control everything for socialism, inefficiency dey enter body sometimes because competition no too dey to make people sit up.

questions.q: Consider an economy where the government owns heavy industries and public utilities, while retail trade and agriculture are left to private individuals. This economic structure is best described as:
o: A traditional subsistence economy
A pure capitalist economy
A pure socialist economy
A mixed economy
questions.e: When both the government (public sector) and private individuals own and run economic activities, it is a mixed economy. Nigeria is a practical example of this.
questions.p: If government hold some big business like electricity, and private people hold market and farming, dat one na mixed economy. Both sides dey play active role.

questions.q: In a command or socialist economy, the three central economic problems (what to produce, how to produce, and for whom to produce) are primarily solved by:
o: Market forces of supply and demand
The price mechanism
A central planning authority
Consumer preferences alone
questions.e: Command economies do not rely on market prices; instead, a central government agency decides what goods are made and distributed.
questions.p: For command economy, na government body go sit down plan everything about wetine dem go produce and how dem go share am, instead of market price.

questions.q: Which of the following features is uniquely associated with capitalism and absent in a strict socialist economy?
o: Employment of labor for wages
The existence of social stratification based on wealth
Provision of public goods by the state
Freedom of enterprise and private ownership of capital
questions.e: Freedom of private enterprise and individual ownership of capital are the defining pillars of capitalism. Socialism restricts private ownership of major capital.
questions.p: Na only for capitalism you go see total freedom for private people to open any business and own heavy capital. Socialism no allow private people control major industries.

questions.q: In a mixed economic system, the government typically intervenes through regulatory agencies to:
o: Take over all retail shops and farms in the country
Prevent private monopolies from exploiting consumers
Ensure that no private individual makes any profit
Abolish the use of money as a medium of exchange
questions.e: Government intervention in mixed economies includes price controls and antitrust laws to protect consumers from unfair business practices.
questions.p: Government dey put regulatory agencies inside mixed economy so that greedy business people no go cheat poor consumers anyhow with high prices.

questions.q: Suppose a nation transitions from a centrally planned economy to a free market economy. Which of the following policy actions is most consistent with this transition?
o: Deregulating prices and privatizing state-owned enterprises
Enforcing strict production quotas through central boards
Eliminating private property rights entirely
Nationalizing all private banks and factories
questions.e: Moving toward a free market requires privatization (selling state assets to private owners) and deregulation (letting prices float via market forces).
questions.p: If country wan change from government-controlled system to free market, dem must sell government companies to private people (privatization) and allow market price work.

questions.q: Which of the following economic tools is best suited for showing the trend of inflation rates in Nigeria over a ten-year period?
o: A pie chart
A frequency polygon
A line graph
A bar chart
questions.e: A line graph is specifically designed to show changes and trends over continuous time periods. It connects data points chronologically, making it ideal for tracking economic variables like inflation over years.
questions.p: Na line graph dem dey use to show how something dey change over time, like inflation rate for Nigeria for ten years.

questions.q: Given the set of monthly profits (in thousands of Naira) for five smallholder farms: 12, 15, 12, 20, 25. What is the modal profit?
questions.e: The mode is the value that appears most frequently in a given data set. In this set, 12 appears twice while the other numbers appear only once, so 12 is the mode.
questions.p: Mode na that number wey show pass for inside the list. Na 12 show two times, so naim be the mode.

questions.q: In a frequency distribution table showing the income of workers, what does the 'cumulative frequency' column represent?
o: The average income of workers in each class
The percentage of workers earning above the mean income
The running total of frequencies from the lowest class upward
The difference between the highest and lowest incomes
questions.e: Cumulative frequency is calculated by adding the frequency of each class interval successively to the sum of the frequencies of all previous classes, starting from the lowest.
questions.p: Cumulative frequency na when you dey add the frequencies join body as you dey go up from bottom to top.

questions.q: If the scores of six students in an Economics test are 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, and 90, find their median score.
questions.e: Since the data is already arranged in ascending order with an even number of observations (6), the median is the average of the two middle numbers: (60 + 70) / 2 = 65.
questions.p: Since the number of students even, you go take the two middle numbers, add dem together, then divide by two. E give you 65.

questions.q: A consumer purchases quantities of yam tubers represented by the set: 3, 7, 5, 3, 9, 3, 8. What is the arithmetic mean?
questions.e: The arithmetic mean is calculated by summing all the values and dividing by the total number of items. Sum = 3+7+5+3+9+3+8 = 38. Total items = 7. Mean = 38 / 7 = 5.43, which rounds to 5.4.
questions.p: To find mean, you add all the yam numbers together and divide by how many dem be. Total na 38, divide by 7, e come give you 5.4.

questions.q: Which of the following graphical representations is most appropriate for displaying budget allocation percentages of a state government?
o: Pie chart
Ogive
Scatter plot
Histogram
questions.e: A pie chart is a circular statistical graphic divided into slices to illustrate numerical proportions, making it ideal for showing percentage components of a whole like a budget.
questions.p: Pie chart fine well-well to show percentage of budget because e be like round cake wey dem slice according to proportion.

questions.q: In a distribution of market prices, the mean price is ₦50 and the median price is ₦45. What is the likely nature of this distribution?
o: Normally distributed
Positively skewed
Negatively skewed
Symmetrically distributed
questions.e: When the mean is greater than the median (50 > 45), the distribution is typically pulled to the right by extremely high values, indicating positive skewness.
questions.p: When mean pass median, e mean say the distribution get positive skewness because high values dey drag am go right.

questions.q: Find the median of the following wage distribution: ₦1000 appears 4 times, ₦2000 appears 5 times, and ₦3000 appears 3 times.
questions.e: Total frequency = 4 + 5 + 3 = 12 (an even number). The median position is half of 12, which falls between the 6th and 7th observations. Writing out the ordered values, both the 6th and 7th positions hold the wage ₦2000.
questions.p: Total frequency na 12. Middle position na 6th and 7th person. When you arrange dem, both 6th and 7th person dey collect ₦2,000.

questions.q: Why is a histogram preferred over a simple bar chart when representing grouped continuous data such as daily wages of factory workers?
o: Bars in a histogram have spaces between them to show separation.
Simple bar charts cannot use numbers on the vertical axis.
Histograms have no gaps between bars, reflecting continuous scales.
Histograms use lines instead of rectangles.
questions.e: Continuous data has no gaps between class boundaries. A histogram reflects this by having adjacent bars touch each other, unlike bar charts which have spaces between discrete categories.
questions.p: Histograms no dey get space for middle of the bars because continuous data no get break. Na why bar touch each other.

questions.q: The mean of five numbers is 12. If a sixth number, 24, is added to the set, what is the new mean?
questions.e: Original sum = 5 * 12 = 60. New sum after adding 24 = 60 + 24 = 84. New total number of items = 6. New mean = 84 / 6 = 14.
questions.p: First five numbers total na 60. When you add 24 join, e come be 84. Divide 84 by 6 numbers, e go give you 14.

questions.q: If the lower quartile (Q1) of a distribution of farm yields is 20 kg and the upper quartile (Q3) is 50 kg, calculate the interquartile range.
o: 35 kg
30 kg
70 kg
15 kg
questions.e: The interquartile range is calculated as the difference between the upper quartile and the lower quartile (Q3 - Q1). Therefore, 50 - 20 = 30 kg.
questions.p: Interquartile range na Upper Quartile minus Lower Quartile. Na 50 minus 20, e come give you 30 kg.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the core principle of the law of demand in economics?
o: As consumer income increases, market demand always decreases
As the price of a substitute falls, demand for the good increases
As price decreases, quantity demanded increases holding other factors constant
As price increases, quantity demanded increases holding other factors constant
questions.e: The law of demand states that there is an inverse relationship between price and quantity demanded, meaning lower prices encourage higher purchases when other things remain equal.
questions.p: Law of demand talk say as price dey come down, na so people go wan buy plenty of am, if other things remain constant.

questions.q: An increase in the price of Milo will most likely cause
o: a rightward shift in the demand curve for Milo
an upward movement along the demand curve for Milo
a leftward shift in the demand curve for peak milk
a downward movement along the demand curve for peak milk
questions.e: A change in the price of a good itself causes a movement along its existing demand curve. An increase in price leads to a contraction, represented by an upward movement along the curve.
questions.p: Na only when price of the item itself change e dey cause movement on top the same demand curve. If price go up, you go move go up for the curve.

questions.q: If Mr. Ade's demand for garri increases from 5 bags to 8 bags per month following a 10 percent drop in his salary, garri is classified as
o: an inferior good
a Giffen good
a normal good
a luxury good
questions.e: An inferior good is one for which demand increases when consumer income falls, and decreases when consumer income rises.
questions.p: If person salary drop but e come buy plenty of that thing, that item na inferior good be that.

questions.q: Which of the following scenarios will cause a rightward shift in the demand curve for petrol in Nigeria?
o: An increase in public awareness about fuel economy
A substantial decrease in the price of petrol
An increase in transport fare expectations due to a national holiday
A sudden fall in the number of vehicle owners
questions.e: Expectation of higher transport fares or scarcity in the future increases current demand, causing a rightward shift in the demand curve.
questions.p: If people dey expect say transport fare go cost tomorrow, dem go rush buy petrol today, and dat one go shift demand curve go right side.

questions.q: The downward slope of the demand curve is primarily explained by all of the following EXCEPT
o: the law of diminishing marginal utility
the income effect of a price change
the substitution effect of a price change
the direct relationship between price and supply
questions.e: The direct relationship between price and supply explains the supply curve, not the downward slope of the demand curve.
questions.p: Na supply curve get direct relationship between price and quantity, so option D no join to explain why demand curve dey slope down.

questions.q: An item whose demand decreases as consumer income increases is known as
o: a normal good
a substitute good
a complementary good
an inferior good
questions.e: Inferior goods have a negative income elasticity of demand, meaning demand drops as buyers become richer.
questions.p: Inferior good na the type of item wey once person money increase, e go stop to dey buy am.

questions.q: If the price of Yamaha motorcycles increases, what happens to the demand for Boxer motorcycles, assuming they are substitutes?
o: Demand for Boxer motorcycles increases
Supply of Boxer motorcycles increases
Demand for Boxer motorcycles decreases
Quantity demanded of Boxer motorcycles decreases
questions.e: When two goods are substitutes, an increase in the price of one leads to an increase in the demand for the other as consumers switch.
questions.p: If Yamaha price go high, people go run leave am come buy Boxer, so demand for Boxer go increase.

questions.q: A shift to the left of the demand curve for yam in a local market in Ibadan can be caused by
o: an increase in consumer population in Ibadan
a fall in the price of cassava flour (elubo), a substitute
an increase in the income of yam consumers
a rise in the price of yam
questions.e: A fall in the price of a substitute (elubo) makes consumers buy less yam and more elubo at every price, shifting the yam demand curve to the left.
questions.p: If elubo price come cheap, people go reduce the yam wey dem dey buy because dem go turn to elubo, making yam demand shift left.

questions.q: Which of the following factors is NOT a determinant of demand?
o: Tastes and preferences of consumers
Price of the commodity itself
Prices of related goods
Cost of raw materials used in production
questions.e: The cost of raw materials is a determinant of supply, not demand.
questions.p: Cost of raw materials na wahala for producer side, na supply factor be that, not demand.

questions.q: A movement from a lower point to a higher point along the same demand curve is called
o: a decrease in demand
an extension of demand
a contraction of demand
an increase in demand
questions.e: A contraction of demand refers to a decrease in quantity demanded caused by an increase in the price of the commodity, shown as an upward movement along the curve.
questions.p: As price go up and quantity wey people dey buy reduce on top the same curve, na contraction of demand be that.

questions.q: Market demand is derived by
o: horizontally summing all individual demand curves in the market
averaging the prices charged by all sellers
subtracting consumer surplus from total revenue
multiplying individual demand by the number of producers
questions.e: Market demand is the total quantity demanded by all consumers at each price, obtained by adding up individual demand quantities horizontally.
questions.p: Market demand na to join all individual demand together horizontally make you know wetock everybody dey buy for market.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the law of supply in economics?
o: As price increases, quantity supplied decreases, holding all other variables fixed
As the cost of production falls, the quantity supplied of that good decreases
As price increases, quantity supplied increases, assuming other factors remain constant
As income rises, the supply of a normal commodity shifts to the left
questions.e: The law of supply states that there is a direct relationship between price and quantity supplied, ceteris paribus. Higher prices create an incentive for producers to supply more.
questions.p: Law of supply talk say as price dey go up, the amount wey sellers wan sell dey also go up, if other things remain constant.

questions.q: An upward movement along a single supply curve for yam in Bodija market is caused by
o: an expectation of a future fall in yam prices
a rise in the market price of yam
a technological breakthrough in yam harvesting
an increase in the subsidy given to yam farmers
questions.e: A movement along a supply curve is caused solely by a change in the price of the commodity itself. Other factors cause shifts of the entire curve.
questions.p: Na only change for the price of yam dey cause movement for the same supply line. Other things dey shift the whole line.

questions.q: If the price of crude oil increases, leading to higher costs for petrol, what will happen to the supply curve of transportation services that rely heavily on petrol?
o: It will become perfectly elastic
It will remain completely unchanged
It will shift to the right
It will shift to the left
questions.e: An increase in the price of a key input (petrol) raises production costs, making it less profitable to supply transportation services at any given price, shifting supply to the left.
questions.p: If petrol price go up, cost of transport go high, and dis one go make transport owners reduce supply, so the line go shift go left.

questions.q: Which of the following factors will cause a rightward shift in the supply curve of locally made Ankara fabric?
o: A severe drought affecting cotton farms
A heavy excise tax imposed on textile manufacturers
An increase in the wages paid to textile workers
The introduction of modern, high-speed weaving machines
questions.e: Improvements in technology reduce production costs and increase efficiency, allowing producers to supply more at every given price, which shifts the supply curve to the right.
questions.p: If machines wey fast and fine enter work, production go easy and cheap, so sellers go fit supply more Ankara for every price.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs of commodities represents joint supply?
o: Beef and leather
Tea and coffee
Margarine and butter
Garri and yam flour
questions.e: Joint supply occurs when two or more goods are derived from the same production process, such as leather and beef obtained from cattle.
questions.p: Joint supply mean say two things come out from one production process, like how we dey get beef and leather from cow.

questions.q: An increase in the price of beans will most likely cause the supply curve of maize to
o: shift to the right if they are in joint supply
shift to the left if they are in competitive supply
remain unaffected because they are unrelated
shift to the right if they are in competitive supply
questions.e: Beans and maize are often grown on the same farmland, making them substitutes in production (competitive supply). A higher price for beans entices farmers to reallocate land to beans, reducing the supply of maize (shift to the left).
questions.p: If beans price high, farmers go prefer plant beans instead of maize, so the supply line for maize go shift go left because dem be competitors for land.

questions.q: If the government grants a tax rebate (subsidy) to manufacturers of cement in Nigeria, the immediate effect on the supply of cement is that the supply curve will
o: shift inward to the left
become vertical
shift outward to the right
contract along the curve
questions.e: Subsidies reduce the cost of production for manufacturers. Lower costs encourage greater output at every price level, represented by a rightward (outward) shift of the supply curve.
questions.p: When government dash factory owners subsidy, cost of production go reduce, and dis one go make dem produce and supply more cement, shifting the curve go right.

questions.q: A perfectly inelastic supply curve is represented on a graph as
o: an upward-sloping curve at a 45-degree angle
a downward-sloping curve
a vertical straight line
a horizontal straight line
questions.e: A perfectly inelastic supply has a price elasticity of zero, meaning quantity supplied is fixed regardless of price changes, which is depicted graphically as a vertical straight line.
questions.p: When supply no gree change at all even if price high or low, the line must stand straight like pole, wey mean vertical line.

questions.q: Suppose the supply function for bags of rice is given as Qs = 100 + 4P, where P is the price in thousands of naira. What is the quantity supplied when the price is ₦50,000?
o: 300 bags
400 bags
200 bags
500 bags
questions.e: Substitute P = 50 into the supply function: Qs = 100 + 4(50) = 100 + 200 = 300 bags.
questions.p: Put 50 inside the formula for P: Qs = 100 + 4 times 50, which give you 100 plus 200, equal to 300 bags.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines 'competitive supply'?
o: Two goods produced together from the same raw material
Goods that must be consumed together to satisfy a want
The rivalry among sellers to capture a larger market share
Alternative goods that can be produced using the same scarce factors of production
questions.e: Competitive supply refers to goods that share the same productive resources; producing more of one means using resources that could have produced the other.
questions.p: Competitive supply happen when producer fit use same land or machine make either this one or that one, so dem dey compete for production factor.

questions.q: An expectation by cocoa farmers that the international price of cocoa will skyrocket next month will most likely cause the current supply curve of cocoa to
o: remain completely stationary
shift to the left immediately
shift to the right immediately
become perfectly elastic
questions.e: If farmers expect prices to rise significantly next month, they will withhold current stocks to sell later at higher prices, causing the current supply curve to shift to the left.
questions.p: If farmers hear say cocoa price go sweet well well next month, dem go hide the ones wey dem get now so dem go sell am later, and dis one go make current supply shift go left.

questions.q: Which of the following factors will cause a rightward shift in the demand curve for garri in a typical Nigerian market?
o: A decrease in the price of yam flour (elubo)
An increase in the production cost of garri
A successful government campaign advising against garri consumption
An increase in consumer disposable income
questions.e: An increase in consumer income raises purchasing power, allowing buyers to purchase more garri at every given price. This shifts the entire demand curve to the right. Other options either reduce demand or affect supply.
questions.p: If people money increase, dem go fit buy more garri for any price wey dey market, and dat one go make demand curve shift go right side. Na only income increase dey cause this one.

questions.q: If the price of a basket of tomatoes increases from ₦4,000 to ₦6,000, and as a result, the quantity supplied increases from 100 baskets to 150 baskets, what is the price elasticity of supply?
questions.e: Elasticity of supply is percentage change in quantity supplied divided by percentage change in price. Percentage change in quantity is (50/100) * 100 = 50%. Percentage change in price is (2000/4000) * 100 = 50%. Thus, 50% / 50% = 1.0.
questions.p: To calculate supply elasticity, divide percentage change for quantity by percentage change for price. Quantity change na 50%, price change na also 50%. When you divide 50 by 50, you go get 1.0 exact.

questions.q: At the equilibrium price in a free market:
o: Total revenue of producers is at its minimum
Quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied
There is neither a shortage nor a surplus of the commodity
Government intervention is compulsory to maintain stability
questions.e: Market equilibrium occurs precisely where the quantity demanded equals the quantity supplied. At this intersection point, there is no excess demand (shortage) and no excess supply (surplus).
questions.p: Equilibrium price na that point where wetin buyers wan buy equal the one sellers wan sell. Dem no dey get excess goods or shortage for market again.

questions.q: A maximum price legislation (price ceiling) is often imposed by the government to:
o: Eliminate black market activities permanently
Protect low-income consumers from exorbitant prices of essential goods
Protect the profit margins of commercial farmers
Discourage the consumption of locally produced luxury items
questions.e: A price ceiling is set below the equilibrium price to make essential commodities affordable for low-income earners. However, it often leads to excess demand and shortages, creating queues or black markets.
questions.p: Government dey put maximum price so poor people fit afford important things like food or rent. E dey help consumers make price no too high, even though e fit cause shortage sometimes.

questions.q: If the demand for petrol is perfectly inelastic, a 10% increase in its price will result in:
o: No change in the quantity demanded
A 10% decrease in quantity demanded
A 5% decrease in quantity demanded
An infinite decrease in quantity demanded
questions.e: A perfectly inelastic demand has a price elasticity coefficient of zero. This means changes in price have absolute zero effect on the quantity demanded by consumers.
questions.p: If demand dey perfectly inelastic, e mean say whether price costly or cheap, people must buy the same quantity. Price increase by 10%, quantity demanded no go move at all (0%).

questions.q: An increase in the supply of beans, with demand remaining constant, will lead to:
o: A higher equilibrium price and a lower equilibrium quantity
A lower equilibrium price and a higher equilibrium quantity
Both a higher equilibrium price and quantity
Both a lower equilibrium price and quantity
questions.e: An outward shift in the supply curve creates a temporary surplus at the old price, forcing sellers to lower their prices. As prices drop, consumers buy more, resulting in a lower equilibrium price and higher equilibrium quantity.

questions.q: Given the demand function Q = 50 - 2P, where Q is quantity demanded and P is price, calculate the quantity demanded when the price is ₦15.
questions.e: Substitute P = 15 into the equation: Q = 50 - 2(15). This gives Q = 50 - 30, which equals 20.
questions.p: Just put 15 inside place of P for the equation. You go get Q = 50 minus 2 times 15. Two times 15 na 30, and 50 minus 30 na 20 straight.

questions.q: Which of the following commodities is most likely to have a price elasticity of demand greater than one (elastic)?
o: Electricity for domestic use
Brand-new sports cars
Life-saving prescription drugs
Common salt
questions.e: Luxury items like brand-new sports cars have many substitutes and are not necessities, making consumers very sensitive to price changes (elastic demand). Necessities like salt and medicines are inelastic.
questions.p: Sports car na luxury item, e no be something wey person must die if e no buy am. If price increase small, people go stop to buy am, so demand dey elastic.

questions.q: A minimum price (price floor) fixed above the equilibrium price usually results in:
o: An increase in consumer surplus
Excess demand or shortage
Clearing of the market at the old price
Excess supply or surplus
questions.e: A price floor set above the equilibrium encourages producers to supply more while discouraging consumers from buying as much. This disequilibrium generates a surplus (excess supply) in the market.
questions.p: When government say make price no fall pass one particular high level (price floor), producers go rush produce plenty goods, but buyers no go fit buy all. Na surplus market go con jam.

questions.q: If the cross-elasticity of demand between product X and product Y is positive, it implies that the two goods are:
o: Substitutes
Unrelated goods
Complements
Inferior goods
questions.e: A positive cross-elasticity means an increase in the price of product Y leads to an increase in the quantity demanded of product X. This is the hallmark of substitute goods (e.g., butter and margarine).
questions.p: If cross-elasticity positive, e mean say if price of one good naik up, people go run go buy the other one instead. E show clearly say the two things na substitutes like butter and margarine.

questions.q: Total revenue reaches its maximum point when the price elasticity of demand is:
o: Zero
Unity (equal to 1)
Infinity
Less than 1
questions.e: When price elasticity of demand is unitary (1.0), a percentage change in price is matched by an exact equal percentage change in quantity demanded, keeping total revenue at its peak.
questions.p: Total revenue dey highest point when price elasticity na unitary, meaning e equal to 1. For this point, any further price movement for up or down go reduce total money wey seller dey make.

questions.q: An inferior good is one for which demand:
o: Falls as consumer income increases
Rises as consumer income increases
Rises proportionately with the price of the good
Remains completely unchanged when income changes
questions.e: By definition, an inferior good has a negative income elasticity of demand. As people become richer, they switch from inferior goods to better alternatives.
questions.p: Inferior good na that thing wey people dey consume because dem no get money. Once their income improve, dem go stop to buy am and switch to better quality things.

questions.q: Which of the following factors of production is primarily responsible for bearing business risks and coordinating other inputs in a bakery in Onitsha?
o: Capital
Land
Entrepreneurship
Labour
questions.e: The entrepreneur is the ultimate risk-bearer who combines land, labour, and capital to produce goods and services. In a bakery, the business owner or entrepreneur coordinates these factors and takes the financial risk.
questions.p: Na entrepreneur be the person wey dey carry the risk of the business and dey join land, labour and capital together. Naim make bread baking business for Onitsha take dey run smoothly.

questions.q: A factory producing leather shoes in Aba notices that as it adds more workers to a fixed size workshop, output initially increases rapidly, then grows at a slower rate, and finally begins to fall. This illustrates the
o: quantity theory of money
law of demand and supply
law of comparative advantage
principle of diminishing marginal returns
questions.e: The law of diminishing marginal returns states that as successive units of a variable factor are added to a fixed factor, the marginal output will eventually decrease. This explains why adding too many workers to a fixed workshop eventually reduces total output.
questions.p: Dis one na law of diminishing marginal returns. E dey show say if you keep adding workers to small shop wey no dey expand, the extra work wey each person dey add go start to dey reduce small small.

questions.q: An advantage of division of labour in a large palm oil processing mill in Benin is that it
o: increases the monotony of work for operators
leads to an over-reliance on manual tools
makes workers easily replaceable without training
enhances the acquisition of special skills by workers
questions.e: Division of labour breaks production into smaller, specific tasks, allowing workers to concentrate on one task and become highly skilled at it. This specialization increases overall efficiency and productivity.
questions.p: When person dey do one particular work every time for palm oil mill, e go come sabi the work well well. Dat specialization dey help worker acquire special skill sharp sharp.

questions.q: If total product increases from 100 units to 135 units when the number of labourers increases from 4 to 5, what is the marginal product of the 5th labourer?
o: 135 units
35 units
43 units
25 units
questions.e: Marginal Product (MP) is the change in total product divided by the change in the variable factor. MP = 135 - 100 = 35 units.
questions.p: To find marginal product, just minus the old total product from the new total product. E come be 135 minus 100, wey give us 35 units.

questions.q: A disadvantage commonly associated with the specialization of labour in a modern manufacturing firm is
o: increase in the interdependence among production units
reduction in the time wasted moving between tasks
higher output per head due to expert handling
lower cost of production per unit of output
questions.e: When tasks are divided, each section depends heavily on the previous one. If one department or worker stops working due to a strike or breakdown, the entire production line grinds to a halt, showing interdependence.
questions.p: If everybody dey do different small part of work, wahala go come if one person slow down. The whole company go jam because everybody dey depend on each other work.

questions.q: Given that the fixed cost of a sachet water factory is N50,000 and the variable cost for producing 10,000 sachets is N150,000, what is the average total cost?
o: N10 per sachet
N25 per sachet
N20 per sachet
N15 per sachet
questions.e: Average Total Cost (ATC) is Total Cost divided by Total Output. Total Cost = Fixed Cost + Variable Cost = 50,000 + 150,000 = N200,000. ATC = 200,000 / 10,000 = N20 per sachet.
questions.p: First find total cost by adding fixed cost and variable cost together (50k + 150k = 200k). Then divide am by the total 10,000 sachets to get N20 per sachet.

questions.q: Which of the following is classified as working capital in a modern transport business operating in Lagos?
o: The minibuses used for transport
The administrative office building
The spare tyres and engine oil in stock
The long-term bank loans obtained
questions.e: Working capital refers to circulating capital, which includes raw materials, cash, and short-term operational items like fuel, spare tyres, and engine oil used up during daily business operations.
questions.p: Working capital na those things wey dey finish quick quick for daily business, like engine oil, fuel, and spare tyres wey transport bus dey use every day.

questions.q: The stage of production where the Marginal Product (MP) is zero corresponds to the point where the
o: Average Product (AP) is at its minimum
Total Product (TP) is at its maximum
Total Product (TP) starts to rise rapidly
Average Product (AP) equals zero
questions.e: When Marginal Product is zero, adding another unit of the variable factor does not change the total product. This corresponds precisely to the peak of the Total Product curve, after which TP begins to fall.
questions.p: When marginal product reach zero, it means the extra person wey you add no add anything again to the work. Dat time, total product don high reach peak level.

questions.q: Geographical mobility of labour in Nigeria is often severely hindered by
o: differences in state-of-origin policies and language barriers
uniform national minimum wage laws
the availability of modern telecommunications
free movement protocols under regional trade agreements
questions.e: Geographical mobility refers to the ease with which workers can move from one location to another for employment. In Nigeria, language barriers, cultural differences, and state-of-origin sentiments often discourage people from relocating.
questions.p: Make person pack go work another state for Nigeria dey hard sometimes because of language, culture, and all those state-of-origin wahala.

questions.q: Which of the following best exemplifies fixed capital for a commercial poultry farmer in Ibadan?
o: Veterinary drugs used for treatment
Day-old chicks bought for rearing
bags of poultry feeds in the warehouse
The automated feeding troughs and battery cages
questions.e: Fixed capital consists of durable assets used in production over a long period, such as machinery, buildings, and equipment. Automated feeding troughs and battery cages are long-lasting equipment, unlike feeds or chicks.
questions.p: Fixed capital na those long-lasting property like battery cages and feeding machines wey farmer go use for many years before dem spoil.

questions.q: Which of the following costs must a bakery in Aba continue to pay even if it completely stops baking bread for a month due to machine maintenance?
o: Factory rent
Electricity consumed during baking
Packaging materials
Cost of flour and sugar
questions.e: Factory rent is a fixed cost because it does not change with the level of output and must be paid even when production is zero. Flour, sugar, packaging, and baking electricity are variable costs that become zero when production stops.
questions.p: Na factory rent be fixed cost, e mean say whether dem bake bread or not, dem must pay am. Na only variable cost like flour and sugar dey stop when production stop.

questions.q: If a pure water producing firm in Ibadan experiences an increase in its total output from 1,000 bags to 1,200 bags, and its total cost rises from ₦50,000 to ₦58,000, what is the marginal cost of the extra production?
o: ₦100 per bag
₦80 per bag
₦40 per bag
₦50 per bag
questions.e: Marginal cost is the change in total cost divided by the change in total output. Change in cost is ₦58,000 - ₦50,000 = ₦8,000, and change in output is 1,200 - 1,000 = 200 bags. Therefore, marginal cost = ₦8,000 / 200 = ₦40 per bag.
questions.p: To find marginal cost, you go minus old total cost from new total cost, then divide am by change in output. E go give you ₦8,000 divide by 200 bags, wey be ₦40 per bag.

questions.q: What happens to the average fixed cost (AFC) of a shoe-making enterprise in Onitsha as it increases its output of shoes?
o: It first falls then rises
It falls continuously
It increases continuously
It remains constant throughout
questions.e: Average fixed cost is total fixed cost divided by output. As output increases, the fixed cost is spread over a larger number of units, causing the AFC curve to fall continuously.
questions.p: As production dey increase, the fixed cost dey spread on top plenty items, make the average fixed cost dey come down small small.

questions.q: Which cost curve typically has a U-shape because of the operation of the law of variable proportions (diminishing returns)?
o: Total fixed cost curve
Total cost curve
Average fixed cost curve
Average variable cost curve
questions.e: The average variable cost curve is U-shaped due to increasing returns to variable factors at first and then diminishing returns later. Average fixed cost slopes downward continuously, while total cost and total fixed cost curves do not have a U-shape.
questions.p: Na average variable cost curve dey get U-shape because of how efficiency take change from better to worse as worker or material plenty pass normal level.

questions.q: The short-run total cost of producing 50 pieces of Ankara fabric is ₦75,000, and the total fixed cost is ₦25,000. What is the average total cost?
questions.e: Average total cost is total cost divided by total output. Therefore, ₦75,000 / 50 pieces = ₦1,500 per piece.
questions.p: Average total cost na just total cost divide by total quantity. Just divide ₦75,000 by 50 pieces, you go get ₦1,500.

questions.q: Why does the marginal cost curve intersect both the average variable cost curve and the average total cost curve at their lowest points?
o: Because fixed costs are constant at all levels of output
Because marginal cost always rises faster than average cost
Because marginal cost equals average cost at their minimums
Because total revenue is maximized at that exact point
questions.e: When marginal cost is below average cost, average cost falls. When marginal cost is above average cost, average cost rises. Therefore, where marginal cost equals average cost, the average cost is neither rising nor falling, which is its minimum point.
questions.p: If marginal cost dey down, e dey drag average cost down. If e pass am, e dey push am up, so na where dem meet equal be the lowest point for average cost.

questions.q: A pure monopoly firm producing yams in a Benue market discovers that its total revenue increases from ₦200,000 to ₦230,000 when sales increase from 400 tubers to 500 tubers. What is the marginal revenue of the extra tubers?
o: ₦300 per tuber
₦230 per tuber
₦500 per tuber
₦200 per tuber
questions.e: Marginal revenue is the change in total revenue divided by the change in quantity sold. Change in revenue is ₦230,000 - ₦200,000 = ₦30,000, and change in quantity is 500 - 400 = 100 tubers. Marginal revenue = ₦30,000 / 100 = ₦300 per tuber.
questions.p: Marginal revenue na the extra money wey you get from selling extra goods. Minus old revenue from new revenue, then divide by change in tubers, you go get ₦300.

questions.q: If a soap manufacturer in Lagos sells 200 bars of soap at a uniform price of ₦300 per bar, what is the average revenue and total revenue respectively?
questions.e: Average revenue is total revenue divided by output, which is always equal to the price, hence ₦300. Total revenue is price multiplied by quantity (₦300 * 200 = ₦60,000).
questions.p: Average revenue na the price per one, wey be ₦300. Total revenue na price times quantity, wey give ₦60,000.

questions.q: In the long run, all costs of production for an enterprise are considered to be:
o: Marginal costs
Sunk costs
Variable costs
Fixed costs
questions.e: In the long run, there are no fixed inputs or fixed costs because all factors of production, including plant size and machinery, can be varied. Therefore, all costs become variable in the long run.
questions.p: For long run, nothing like fixed cost again because owner fit change factory size, machine, and everything. So all cost turn to variable cost.

questions.q: A firm selling leather bags in Kano calculates that its total revenue function is given as TR = 500Q - 2Q^2, where Q is quantity. What is the marginal revenue function for this firm?
o: MR = 500Q - 4Q
questions.e: Marginal revenue is the first derivative of the total revenue function with respect to quantity (Q). Differentiating TR = 500Q - 2Q^2 gives MR = 500 - 4Q.
questions.p: To get marginal revenue from total revenue equation, you differentiate am with respect to Q. When you differentiate 500Q - 2Q^2, you go get 500 - 4Q.

questions.q: Suppose a table-water factory operating in Port Harcourt faces a total cost function of TC = 10,000 + 50Q + 2Q^2. What is its total fixed cost?
questions.e: In the total cost equation TC = 10,000 + 50Q + 2Q^2, the term 10,000 is independent of output (Q) and represents the total fixed cost. The other terms containing Q are variable costs.
questions.p: Inside the cost equation, any number wey no carry Q na the fixed cost because e no depend on how many water you produce. Na 10,000 be that.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a key characteristic of a perfectly competitive market in Nigeria?
o: There are very few large firms dominating the supply.
Products sold by different sellers are highly differentiated through branding.
Entry into and exit from the industry are heavily restricted by government licenses.
Individual buyers and sellers have no control over the market price.
questions.e: In perfect competition, firms and consumers are price takers because no single economic agent is large enough to influence the market price. Product homogeneity and free entry and exit are also core features.
questions.p: For perfect competition, nobody get power to fix price for market, whether buyer or seller. Dem all dey follow the market price wey demand and supply bring.

questions.q: Under pure monopoly, the demand curve facing the monopolist is generally:
o: downward-sloping from left to right
horizontal at the prevailing market price
perfectly inelastic at all price levels
perfectly elastic
questions.e: A monopolist is the sole supplier of a product with no close substitutes, so the firm's demand curve is the same as the industry demand curve, which slopes downward.
questions.p: Monopolist na him be the only person wey dey sell that product, so him demand curve dey slope downward from left go right.

questions.q: An oligopolistic market structure is primarily characterized by:
o: complete absence of non-price competition like advertising
thousands of independent farmers selling identical yams
mutual interdependence among a small number of large rival firms
a single firm controlling the entire national output
questions.e: Oligopoly features a few dominant firms whose pricing and output decisions are strategically interdependent, meaning one firm's action directly affects its rivals.
questions.p: For oligopoly, small number of big companies dey compete, and wetin one company do must affect the other onessef. Dem dey eye themselves well well.

questions.q: Why is the marginal revenue (MR) curve of a monopolist always below its average revenue (AR) or demand curve?
o: Because total revenue rises at a constant, unchanging rate as output expands.
Because the monopolist can sell infinite quantities at a constant price.
Because average revenue decreases as total output remains strictly constant.
Because the monopolist must lower its price to sell an extra unit of output.
questions.e: To sell an additional unit, a monopolist must reduce the price for all units sold. Consequently, the addition to total revenue (marginal revenue) is less than the price (average revenue) of the extra unit.
questions.p: To sell extra one, monopolist must reduce price for all of them. That one make the money wey he gain from the extra one (marginal revenue) dey come down pass the price itself.

questions.q: Which of the following industries in Nigeria most closely approximates an oligopoly?
o: The market for pure water packaged in nylon bags by hundreds of small operators
The telecommunications market dominated by MTN, Airtel, Globacom, and 9mobile
The market for locally roasted corn by roadside hawkers
The Nigerian National Petroleum Company sole importation of crude fuel
questions.e: The Nigerian telecommunications sector is shared among a few major service providers, making it a classic textbook example of an oligopoly.
questions.p: Telecommunications market for Nigeria na good example of oligopoly because na only few major network providers dey share the whole country.

questions.q: In the long run, a firm operating under perfect competition earns:
o: abnormal or supernormal profits due to high barriers to entry
only normal profits because free entry and exit eliminate excess gains
substantial economic losses because total costs always exceed total revenue
monopoly rents protected by patent rights
questions.e: In the long run, freedom of entry and exit ensures that any supernormal profits attract new firms, driving price down to minimum average cost where only normal profit is made.
questions.p: For long run, if people dey make excess profit, new people go enter market until everybody just dey make normal profit. No extra gain again.

questions.q: Price discrimination is most successfully practiced by a monopolist when:
o: markets can be effectively separated and price elasticities differ between them
the product is completely standardized and sold in an open auction
consumers can easily resell the product among themselves in different markets
transportation costs between different consumer groups are extremely high
questions.e: Price discrimination requires market segregation to prevent arbitrage (reselling) and varying price elasticities of demand among consumer groups to charge different prices profitably.
questions.p: To fit do price discrimination, monopolist must fit separate customers make dem no fit resell am among themselves, and people elasticity must不同.

questions.q: A firm under monopolistic competition differs from a monopolist primarily because the former:
o: faces a perfectly elastic demand curve
produces a homogenous product identical to all other rivals
has no competitors whatsoever in the industry
sells differentiated products and faces easy entry and exit
questions.e: Monopolistic competition combines elements of monopoly (product differentiation giving some price-setting power) and competition (many firms, easy entry and exit).
questions.p: Monopolistic competition dey sell product wey get small difference (like different soap brands), and anybody fit enter market anyhow unlike pure monopoly.

questions.q: The main economic objection to a pure monopoly is that it typically results in:
o: unnecessary duplication of advertisements and wasteful packaging costs
excessive output and extremely low market prices for consumers
an inefficient allocation of resources where price exceeds marginal cost
constant price wars among rival firms trying to capture market share
questions.e: A monopolist restricts output and charges a price higher than marginal cost (P > MC), creating deadweight loss and allocative inefficiency compared to a competitive market.
questions.p: Monopoly bad for economy because dem dey reduce output and sell high price wey pass marginal cost, make resources no distribute well.

questions.q: What is the primary feature of the 'kinked demand curve' model often used to explain price rigidity in oligopoly?
o: Competitors match price cuts immediately but ignore price increases by a rival firm.
Competitors match price increases immediately but ignore price cuts by a rival firm.
All firms in the industry agree on a single uniform price through a formal cartel.
Demand is completely inelastic regardless of any changes in the prevailing price.
questions.e: In the kinked demand curve model, rivals ignore price hikes (making demand elastic above the current price) but match price cuts (making demand inelastic below it), causing price stickiness.
questions.p: For kinked demand curve, if one company increase price, others go leave am. But if he reduce price, everybody go follow am reduce their own. That one make price stiff.

questions.q: Which of the following conditions ensures profit maximization for any firm regardless of its market structure?
o: Total Revenue equals Total Cost
Price equals Average Variable Cost
Average Revenue equals Average Cost
Marginal Revenue equals Marginal Cost
questions.e: The fundamental rule for profit maximization across all market structures (perfect competition, monopoly, oligopoly, etc.) is where Marginal Revenue equals Marginal Cost (MR = MC).
questions.p: Anywhere you dey, whether monopoly abi perfect competition, once Marginal Revenue (MR) equal Marginal Cost (MC), na there profit highest.

questions.q: An agreement among independent oligopolistic firms to collude and fix prices or output levels is commonly referred to as a:
o: subsidiary
holding company
cartel
merger
questions.e: A cartel is a formal organization of independent producers that collude to restrict output and fix prices, acting collectively like a single monopolist (e.g., OPEC).
questions.p: When companies join hand make dem fix price together like say na one person own am, we dey call that kind association cartel.

questions.q: National income measured at current market prices is known as:
o: Disposable national income
Nominal national income
Net national product
Real national income
questions.e: Nominal national income is the total monetary value of all final goods and services produced within an economy, measured at current year prices without adjusting for inflation. When adjusted for inflation, it becomes real national income.
questions.p: Nominal national income na the total money value of all goods and services wey dem produce for inside country using current market price without removing inflation.

questions.q: Which of the following is added to Gross Domestic Product (GDP) to arrive at Gross National Product (GNP)?
o: Indirect taxes minus subsidies
Depreciation or capital consumption allowance
Net income from abroad
Government transfer payments
questions.e: GNP measures the total output produced by the citizens of a country, both at home and abroad. Therefore, net factor income from abroad is added to the domestic output (GDP) to get GNP.
questions.p: To convert GDP to GNP, you must add net income wey citizens dey bring enter house from foreign land join domestic production.

questions.q: In an economy, if Gross National Product is ₦450 billion, depreciation is ₦50 billion, and indirect taxes minus subsidies is ₦30 billion, what is the Net National Product at factor cost (National Income)?
o: ₦420 billion
₦400 billion
₦480 billion
₦370 billion
questions.e: NNP at market prices = GNP minus depreciation = 450 - 50 = 400 billion. NNP at factor cost (National Income) = NNP at market prices minus indirect taxes plus subsidies = 400 - 30 = 370 billion.
questions.p: First remove depreciation from GNP to get NNP market price (450 - 50 = 400). Then remove indirect taxes to reach factor cost, which give us 370 billion.

questions.q: The main problem of double counting in the measurement of national income using the output method is avoided by using:
o: Market prices
Value added at each stage of production
Factor costs
Transfer payments
questions.e: The value-added approach calculates only the net increase in value at each stage of production, thereby preventing the same item or raw material from being counted more than once.
questions.p: To avoid counting the same item plenty times, economist dey use value-added method to sum up only the extra value wey dem put at every stage of production.

questions.q: Which of the following is excluded when calculating national income by the income approach?
o: Unemployment benefits and pensions
Wages and salaries of civil servants
Profits of manufacturing companies
Rent paid on commercial buildings
questions.e: Transfer payments like unemployment benefits and pensions are excluded from national income calculations because no current productive service is rendered in exchange for them.
questions.p: Government transfer payments like pension and unemployment money no dey count for national income because nobody work for am currently.

questions.q: Net Domestic Product (NDP) differs from Gross Domestic Product (GDP) by:
o: Direct taxes
Net factor income from abroad
Subsidies
Capital consumption allowance
questions.e: Gross figures include depreciation, while net figures exclude it. Therefore, subtracting depreciation (capital consumption allowance) from GDP gives NDP.
questions.p: The only difference between GDP and NDP na depreciation. If you remove depreciation from gross, you go get net.

questions.q: If the population of a country is 20 million and its real GDP is ₦100 billion, the per capita real GDP is:
questions.e: Per capita real GDP is calculated by dividing real GDP by the total population. That is ₦100,000,000,000 divided by 20,000,000, which equals ₦5,000.
questions.p: Per capita income na to divide total real GDP by the number of people for the country. 100 billion Naira divide by 20 million people give us 5,000 Naira per head.

questions.q: The expenditure approach to measuring national income sums up:
o: Wages, rent, interest, and profit
Consumption, investment, government purchases, and net exports
Primary, secondary, and tertiary sector outputs
Gross output minus intermediate consumption
questions.e: The expenditure approach measures national income as the sum of final expenditures by households (C), businesses (I), government (G), and net foreign sector (X - M).
questions.p: Expenditure method na to add all the money wey people, companies, government, and foreign buyers spend on final goods and services (C + I + G + X-M).

questions.q: Why is per capita income often considered an unreliable indicator of economic welfare in developing countries?
o: It accounts for inflation too accurately
It measures only the agricultural sector
It does not reflect income inequality and distribution
It includes income earned abroad
questions.e: Per capita income is an average figure that hides disparities; a high per capita income can exist alongside severe poverty if wealth is concentrated in the hands of a few.
questions.p: Per capita income na just average number, e no dey show how wealth spread. If two people get plenty money and ninety-eight people poor, average go high but poverty still dey.

questions.q: Disposable personal income is best defined as:
o: National income plus transfer payments
Personal income minus personal taxes and non-tax payments
Gross national product minus depreciation
Total national income minus personal income taxes
questions.e: Disposable personal income is the actual amount of money households have left for spending and saving after paying personal income taxes and settling non-tax obligations.
questions.p: Disposable income na the exact money wey workers remain with to chop or save after government don remove tax and other compulsory payments from their salary.

questions.q: National income measured at factor cost is equal to national income at market prices:
o: Plus subsidies minus indirect taxes
Plus net income from abroad
Plus indirect taxes minus subsidies
Plus depreciation
questions.e: Market prices include indirect taxes and exclude subsidies. To get factor cost from market prices, we must subtract indirect taxes and add back subsidies.
questions.p: To change market price to factor cost, you must remove indirect tax wey government add and add back any subsidy wey dem give.

questions.q: Which of the following activities is NOT included in the calculation of Gross Domestic Product?
o: A teacher receiving a monthly salary from a public school
A housewife cooking meals for her own family members
A tailor sewing clothes for paying customers
A commercial bus driver earning transport fares
questions.e: GDP only accounts for market transactions where goods and services are exchanged for money. Household chores done for oneself or family have no recorded market value and are excluded.
questions.p: GDP no dey count work wey person do for inside house for free, like cooking for family, because money no change hand for market.

questions.q: Which of the following properties of money is most responsible for overcoming the double coincidence of wants inherent in barter?
o: Store of value
Portability
Divisibility
Medium of exchange
questions.e: Money serves primarily as a medium of exchange, which removes the need for two people to want what each other has. This direct acceptability solves the major headache of the barter system.
questions.p: Na medium of exchange be the main thing wey dey help us buy wetyn we want without stress of finding person wey get wetyn you need and also want wetyn you get.

questions.q: When money is used to express the value of different goods and services in a common unit like the Nigerian Naira, it is performing the function of a
o: Standard for deferred payment
Medium of exchange
Unit of account
Store of value
questions.e: A unit of account, or measure of value, allows prices of diverse commodities to be quoted in a uniform monetary denomination, easing comparison and accounting.
questions.p: As money dey help us measure price of yam, garri and cloth for one common Naira value, e dey act as unit of account.

questions.q: According to the Keynesian liquidity preference theory, the demand for money for speculative motive is primarily determined by
o: The general price level
The level of current income
The frequency of salary payments
The prevailing rate of interest
questions.e: Speculative demand for money is inversely related to the interest rate. When interest rates are high, people hold bonds instead of cash, and vice versa.
questions.p: Speculative demand dey depend on interest rate. If interest rate high, people go buy bonds instead of holding idle cash for house.

questions.q: If the total money supply in an economy is ₦50,000,000, the aggregate output is 2,000,000 units, and the average price level is ₦40, what is the velocity of circulation of money according to the Fisher quantity theory equation (MV = PT)?
questions.p: We apply MV = PT formula. 50 million times V equal to 40 times 2 million, wey be 80 million. When you divide 80 million by 50 million, you go get 1.6.

questions.q: Cost-push inflation in Nigeria can be triggered by an increase in which of the following factors?
o: Import tariffs on raw industrial materials
Commercial bank lending rates to SMEs
Consumer confidence and spending
Government expenditure on infrastructure
questions.e: Cost-push inflation occurs when the cost of production rises, such as higher import tariffs on raw materials, forcing producers to raise prices.
questions.p: Cost-push inflation dey happen when wahala like high import duty on raw materials make production cost cost well well, come force sellers make dem increase price.

questions.q: During a period of severe inflation, creditors generally
o: Gain because interest rates automatically drop
Remain unaffected due to fixed nominal contracts
Lose because the purchasing power of repaid money has fallen
Gain because they receive more valuable money
questions.e: Creditors lend money with high purchasing power and are repaid later with money that has lower purchasing power due to rising prices.
questions.p: Person wey lend money (creditor) go lose during inflation because the money wey debtor pay back go fit buy fewer things pass before.

questions.q: Which of the following groups of people is likely to benefit most during a period of unanticipated inflation?
o: Pensioners living on fixed incomes
Commercial banks holding long-term bonds
Workers whose wages are adjusted sluggishly
Debtors who borrowed at fixed interest rates
questions.e: Debtors benefit because they pay back their loans with currency that has depreciated in real value, meaning they effectively repay with cheaper money.
questions.p: Debtors dey happy pass during inflation because dem go pay back their debt with money wey value don drop.

questions.q: Deflation is best defined as a sustained decrease in the general price level accompanied by
o: An increase in export volumes
A contraction in aggregate economic activity
An expansion in the money supply
An increase in the level of employment
questions.e: Deflation is often associated with falling output, decreased consumer demand, and rising unemployment, representing a general economic downturn.
questions.p: Deflation no be only when price fall, e dey follow economic recession where business slow down and unemployment dey increase.

questions.q: The transaction demand for money is primarily a function of
o: The speculative behavior of investors
The exchange rate of the currency
The level of national income
The rate of inflation
questions.e: People demand money for daily transactions mainly based on how much income they earn. Higher income generally leads to higher transaction demand for money.
questions.p: Transaction demand for money mean the cash wey you need for daily transport and food, and na how much money you dey earn (income) dey determine am.

questions.q: If the Central Bank of Nigeria increases the cash reserve ratio (CRR) of commercial banks, the expected immediate effect on the money supply is that it will
o: Decrease because banks' ability to create credit is restricted
Increase because interest rates will fall
Remain unchanged because only currency in circulation matters
Increase because banks have more reserves
questions.e: Raising the cash reserve ratio forces banks to keep more cash with the Central Bank, reducing the amount available for lending and contracting the money supply.
questions.p: If CBN increase cash reserve ratio, banks go keep more money for Central Bank and reduce the one dem dey give loan, so money supply go reduce.

questions.q: Demand-pull inflation is commonly described as a situation of
o: Too much production chasing too little demand
Too many goods chasing too few goods
Too much money chasing too few goods
Too few workers chasing too many jobs
questions.e: Demand-pull inflation happens when aggregate demand outpaces aggregate supply, summarized as 'too much money chasing too few goods'.
questions.p: Demand-pull inflation na when plenty money dey pursuit small goods for market, making price to begin shoot up.

questions.q: Suppose the velocity of money is constant at 4, real GDP grows by 3 percent, and the money supply increases by 8 percent. According to the monetarist approach, what is the approximate inflation rate?
o: 3 percent
5 percent
4 percent
8 percent
questions.e: Using growth rates: % change in M + % change in V = % change in P + % change in Real GDP. Here, 8% + 0% = Inflation (%) + 3%. Thus, Inflation = 8% - 3% = 5%.
questions.p: We use percentage form of quantity theory: Money growth (8%) plus velocity growth (0%) equal to inflation plus output growth (3%). If you minus 3 from 8, inflation na 5%.

questions.q: Which of the following institutions is primarily responsible for formulating monetary policy and regulating commercial banks in Nigeria?
o: First Bank of Nigeria PLC
The Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation
The Nigerian Stock Exchange
The Central Bank of Nigeria
questions.e: The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) is the apex monetary authority responsible for monetary policy formulation and banking regulation. Commercial banks operate under its supervision, while the other options have different statutory mandates.
questions.p: Na Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) be the apex bank wey dey control monetary policy and supervise commercial banks. Na im work be that, no be commercial bank or stock exchange.

questions.q: A financial market where long-term securities such as bonds and equities are traded is known as the
o: capital market
money market
bullion market
foreign exchange market
questions.e: The capital market specializes in the mobilization and trading of long-term financial instruments like shares, stocks, and bonds. The money market deals with short-term funds instead.
questions.p: Capital market na where dem dey trade long-term securities like shares and bonds. Money market na for short-term money.

questions.q: Which of the following instruments is NOT traded in the money market?
o: Ordinary shares
Treasury bills
Commercial papers
Call money
questions.e: Ordinary shares represent ownership in a company and are traded in the capital market, not the money market. Treasury bills, commercial papers, and call money are typical short-term money market instruments.
questions.p: Ordinary shares na capital market instrument, no be money market. Treasury bills and commercial papers na short-term money market things.

questions.q: When the Central Bank of Nigeria desires to curb inflation, it will most likely
o: lower the bank rate to encourage borrowing
increase the monetary policy rate
reduce the cash reserve ratio of commercial banks
buy government securities in the open market
questions.e: To curb inflation, the CBN adopts a contractionary monetary policy by raising interest rates like the Monetary Policy Rate (MPR). This makes borrowing expensive, reduces money supply, and cools down aggregate demand.
questions.p: To fight inflation, CBN go increase interest rates like Monetary Policy Rate make borrowing cost high. When borrowing reduce, money for circulation go reduce.

questions.q: The primary function of commercial banks in an economy is to
o: mint currency notes and coins
regulate the activities of microfinance banks
accept deposits and grant loans
fix the official foreign exchange rate
questions.e: Commercial banks act as financial intermediaries whose core business is mobilizing surplus funds through deposits and lending them to deficit units. Minting currency is strictly the function of the Central Bank.
questions.p: Primary work of commercial bank na to collect deposits from people and give out loans. Na CBN dey mint money, no be commercial bank.

questions.q: Open market operations (OMO) conducted by the Central Bank involve the
o: issuance of legal tender currency to the general public
direct control of lending rates charged by commercial banks
provision of bailout funds to distressed financial institutions
buying and selling of government securities to influence liquidity
questions.e: Open market operations refer to the deliberate buying and selling of government securities by the central bank in the open market to regulate money supply and commercial bank liquidity.
