questions.p: Open market operations mean say CBN dey buy or sell government securities to control how much money dey enter economy.

questions.q: Which of the following bodies is responsible for regulating operations and trading activities in the Nigerian capital market?
o: Federal Inland Revenue Service
Asset Management Corporation of Nigeria
Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation
Securities and Exchange Commission
questions.e: The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is the apex regulatory agency for the Nigerian capital market, ensuring investor protection and market integrity. The Nigerian Stock Exchange is the platform, while SEC is the regulator.
questions.p: Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) na the main regulator for Nigerian capital market to protect investors and stop fraud.

questions.q: The discount house in a financial system primarily acts as an intermediary between
o: importers and exporters of goods
the central bank and commercial banks
foreign governments and local banks
retail investors and stockbrokers
questions.e: Discount houses specialize in dealing with short-term government paper, acting as intermediaries between the central bank and commercial banks to facilitate liquidity management.
questions.p: Discount house dey stand as middleman between central bank and commercial banks, especially when dem wan manage short-term funds.

questions.q: An increase in the cash reserve ratio (CRR) by the Central Bank will result in
o: a reduction in the ability of commercial banks to create credit
an automatic fall in the general price level
an expansion in the lending capacity of commercial banks
an increase in the volume of money in circulation
questions.e: A higher cash reserve ratio means commercial banks must keep a larger fraction of their deposits with the CBN, leaving them with less cash to lend out, thereby reducing credit creation.
questions.p: If CBN increase cash reserve ratio, banks go keep more money with CBN and get less money to give out as loan. Credit creation go drop.

questions.q: Which of the following is a liability on the balance sheet of a commercial bank?
o: Treasury bills held by the bank
Loans granted to customers
Customer deposits
Cash reserves kept in the vault
questions.e: Customer deposits represent money that the bank owes to its customers, making them a liability. Loans and vault cash are assets because they generate income or are owned by the bank.
questions.p: Customer deposits na liability for bank because na money wey people keep with dem and bank must pay back. Loans and cash na bank assets.

questions.q: The lender of last resort function of the Central Bank means that the bank
o: controls the foreign exchange reserves of the country
provides emergency financial assistance to solvent but illiquid commercial banks
purchases all unsold shares during a public share issue
finances the annual budget deficit of the federal government
questions.e: As the lender of last resort, the Central Bank steps in to provide temporary emergency loans to commercial banks experiencing severe liquidity crunches to prevent a systemic banking collapse.
questions.p: As lender of last resort, CBN go help give emergency money to commercial banks wey get liquidity problem so say bank no go crash.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a progressive tax system?
o: A tax where the rate decreases as the taxpayer's income increases
A tax levied only on luxury goods purchased by high-income earners
A tax where the rate increases as the income of the taxpayer increases
A tax where everyone pays the same fixed percentage of their income
questions.e: A progressive tax takes a larger percentage of income from high-income earners than from low-income earners. This helps to redistribute wealth and reduce income inequality in the economy.
questions.p: Progressive tax mean say as your money dey increase, the percentage tax wey dem go chop from your pocket dey increase too. E dey help government share wealth well well make poor man pikin breathe.

questions.q: When government expenditure exceeds government revenue in a fiscal year, the resulting economic situation is known as a
o: deficit budget
balanced budget
recessionary budget
surplus budget
questions.e: A deficit budget occurs when government spending is higher than its total revenue collected from taxes and other sources. To finance this gap, the government often borrows money.
questions.p: If government spend pass the money wey enter their hand for one year, na deficit budget be that. Dem go come go find where to borrow money to cover the remaining gap.

questions.q: Which of the following is a direct tax?
o: Excise duty
Value Added Tax
Customs duty
Personal income tax
questions.e: A direct tax is levied directly on the income or property of an individual or organization, and the burden cannot be shifted to someone else. Personal income tax is a classic example of a direct tax.
questions.p: Direct tax na the one wey dem go direct take from your salary or property, and you no fit transfer the load give another person. Personal income tax na perfect example.

questions.q: An incidence of taxation refers to
o: the legal responsibility of paying tax to the tax authority
the final burden or ultimate resting place of the tax burden
the process of calculating tax rebates for manufacturers
the reduction of tax rates to encourage foreign investments
questions.e: Tax incidence is the economic analysis of who ultimately bears the burden of a tax. Even though a seller legally pays a tax, the burden may be shifted to the consumer through higher prices.
questions.p: Incidence of taxation mean the person wey suffer the tax load for end of the day. Even if na seller pay am for counter, na consumer dey carry the actual weight through high price.

questions.q: Which of the following measures can a government adopt to control inflation during a budget cycle?
o: Presenting a deficit budget to stimulate aggregate demand
Printing more currency notes to fund capital projects
Removing all forms of taxation on imported goods
Implementing a surplus budget by cutting public spending and raising taxes
questions.e: A surplus budget occurs when revenue exceeds expenditure, which reduces money supply in circulation and cools down aggregate demand. This contractionary fiscal policy helps to curb rising inflation.
questions.p: To fight inflation, government fit run surplus budget by reducing their spending and increasing tax. E go reduce money for circulation and calm down price hike.

questions.q: An indirect tax is often described as regressive because
o: it cannot be evaded by consumers under any circumstances
it is levied only on goods produced by small-scale enterprises
it takes a higher percentage of income from low-income earners than high-income earners
it takes a larger absolute amount from the rich than the poor
questions.e: Indirect taxes like VAT apply a flat rate to goods. Since poor people spend a larger share of their income on basic goods, they bear a heavier relative tax burden, making it regressive.
questions.p: Indirect tax dey regressive because rich man and poor man dey pay same amount for item like bread or soap. E dey pain poor man pass because e dey take big chunk of im small money.

questions.q: The macroeconomic objective of public finance that ensures resources are reallocated from private use to public goods such as roads and security is known as the
o: allocation function
distribution function
stabilization function
monetary function
questions.e: The allocation function of public finance deals with how government uses its budget to provide public goods and services that the market mechanism might fail to supply adequately.
questions.p: Allocation function mean how government use budget to provide things like road, security and bridge wey everybody go enjoy because private person no fit easily build am.

questions.q: Which of the following represents a non-tax revenue source for the Nigerian federal government?
o: Company income tax
Licence fees and fines
Petroleum profit tax
Value added tax
questions.e: Licence fees, fines, court fees, and earnings from government investments are classified as non-tax revenues. Taxes like PPT, CIT, and VAT are statutory tax revenues.
questions.p: Money from licence, fines, and government business na non-tax revenue. But things like VAT and company tax na proper tax revenue.

questions.q: A balanced budget multiplier implies that an equal increase in government spending and taxes will result in
o: an increase in national income by the same amount of the change
an infinite expansion of the economy
a decrease in national income equal to the tax increase
no change in national income
questions.e: According to the balanced budget multiplier theorem, when government increases spending and taxes by the exact same amount, national income increases by that same amount because government spending has a multiplier effect while taxes reduce disposable income by a fraction.
questions.p: Balanced budget multiplier talk say if government increase spending and tax by same amount, national income go increase by that exact same amount too.

questions.q: Deadweight loss of taxation refers to
o: the tax evaded by fraudulent business owners
the administrative cost incurred by the tax authority
the total revenue collected by the government from the citizens
the excess burden or net loss of economic welfare created by a tax
questions.e: Deadweight loss is the loss of economic efficiency (surplus) that occurs when taxation causes a distortion in the market, preventing mutually beneficial trades from taking place.
questions.p: Deadweight loss na the waste or economic pain wey tax dey cause because e dey distort market price and stop people from doing business wey for benefit them.

questions.q: Which of the following best distinguishes economic development from economic growth?
o: Growth focuses solely on rising inflation while development focuses on unemployment.
Growth occurs only in developed nations while development occurs in developing nations like Nigeria.
Growth is a quantitative increase in national output, whereas development includes qualitative improvements in living standards.
Growth is measured by the Human Development Index while development is measured by Gross Domestic Product.
questions.e: Economic growth is strictly a quantitative measure of increased total output or GDP. Economic development is broader, incorporating qualitative changes such as poverty reduction, better healthcare, and education.
questions.p: Economic growth just mean say money and goods plenty for country, but economic development mean say life better for everybody inside the country, like better hospital and school.

questions.q: A major challenge confronting national economic planning in Nigeria is:
o: excessive reliance on accurate statistical data
consistent over-funding of the agricultural sector
absence of natural resources to plan for
inadequate reliable data and faulty statistical projections
questions.e: Effective planning requires accurate demographic and economic data. In Nigeria, unreliable census figures and poor record-keeping often lead to faulty projections and failed development plans.
questions.p: Na bad data and fake figures dey scatter national planning for Nigeria. If dem no know the exact number of people or money wey dey ground, planning go hard.

questions.q: If a country's Real GDP increases from 50 billion naira to 55 billion naira over a one-year period while its population remains constant, the rate of economic growth is:
questions.e: Growth rate is calculated as ((New GDP - Old GDP) / Old GDP) * 100. Thus, ((55 - 50) / 50) * 100 = (5 / 50) * 100 = 10.0%.
questions.p: To find the growth rate, minus the old money from the new money, divide am by the old money, then multiply by 100. That na 5 divide by 50 times 100, wey give you 10 percent.

questions.q: Development planning that involves the central government directly setting production targets for all sectors of the economy is known as:
o: indicative planning
imperative planning
rolling planning
project planning
questions.e: Imperative or directive planning involves strict central command where the state dictates targets and resource allocations to all sectors, common in centrally planned economies.
questions.p: Imperative planning mean say na government go direct everything and give command on wetin everybody must produce without shaking.

questions.q: Which of the following indicators is most appropriate for international comparison of standard of living?
o: Per capita real income
Volume of crude oil export
Total national debt stock
Gross Domestic Product at market prices
questions.e: Per capita real income divides the total real national income by the total population, giving a clearer picture of average individual purchasing power across different countries.
questions.p: Per capita real income na the best to use check standard of living because e dey share the total money of the country per head.

questions.q: A type of development plan that covers a short duration, usually one year, and is integrated into the annual budget is called a:
o: rolling plan
annual plan
capital plan
perspective plan
questions.e: An annual plan is a short-term plan that outlines specific targets and expenditures for a single fiscal year, serving as the basis for the government budget.
questions.p: Annual plan na short-term plan wey dey last for just one year and na im government dey use arrange their yearly budget.

questions.q: What is the primary objective of introducing a 'rolling plan' in economic development?
o: To ensure total elimination of foreign loans
To freeze government capital expenditure for five years
To stop all private sector participation in the economy
To provide continuity and flexibility by revising targets yearly based on performance
questions.e: A rolling plan adds a new year to the plan period as each year lapses, allowing planners to review achievements and adjust targets flexibly without starting a completely new multi-year plan.
questions.p: Rolling plan dey give country room make dem dey adjust their target every year based on how market or money be, instead of strict fixed years.

questions.q: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of a developing economy like Nigeria?
o: High per capita income
Low population growth rate
High dependence on primary product exports
Advanced technological base
questions.e: Developing economies typically rely heavily on the export of raw agricultural or mineral commodities, making them vulnerable to international price shocks.
questions.p: Developing country like Nigeria love to dey export raw things like crude oil and cocoa instead of finished goods.

questions.q: In the context of economic development, the Human Development Index (HDI) is a composite measure comprising:
o: life expectancy, education level, and per capita income
total population, landmass, and mineral reserves
tax revenue, government expenditure, and national debt
inflation rate, unemployment rate, and exchange rate
questions.e: The HDI combines three basic dimensions of human development: a long and healthy life (life expectancy), knowledge (education/literacy), and a decent standard of living (per capita GNI).
questions.p: HDI na measure wey dey check three main things: how long person fit live, education level, and how better the person pocket be.

questions.q: A major bottleneck to industrialization and economic development in West Africa is:
o: surplus supply of electricity
excessive abundance of skilled manpower
over-saturation of consumer goods
poor state of infrastructural facilities such as roads and power
questions.e: Inadequate infrastructure, particularly unstable electricity supply and bad road networks, increases production costs and hinders industrial growth in the region.
questions.p: Bad light and bad road na the major headache wey dey stop factories from growing well for West Africa.

questions.q: If a country's population grows at 3.5% per annum while its Gross National Product grows at 2.5% per annum, the consequence for the citizens is:
o: an improvement in their general standard of living
a fall in their standard of living
no change in their economic welfare
an immediate elimination of poverty
questions.e: When population growth rate exceeds GNP growth rate, output per head falls. This implies per capita income is declining, leading to a drop in the standard of living.
questions.p: If population dey grow pass how money dey come in, e mean say the share for person head go reduce, and standard of living go fall.

questions.q: Indicative planning is most commonly associated with which of the following economic systems?
o: Mixed economy
Pure command economy
Subsistence economy
Socialist economy
questions.e: Indicative planning is used in mixed economies where the government uses incentives and guidelines to influence private sector activities rather than enforcing rigid controls.
questions.p: Indicative planning na wetin mixed economy dey use; government go just give guide and support, make private people run business.

questions.q: The primary objective of the Nigerian Agricultural Insurance Scheme (NAIS) is to
o: regulate the market price of food items in urban centers
increase the exportation of cash crops to foreign markets
protect farmers against financial losses from natural disasters
provide free seeds and fertilizers to rural farmers
questions.e: The NAIS was specifically established to minimize the risk of financial loss faced by farmers due to unpredictable natural events like floods or drought. This insurance encourages farmers to invest more in agriculture without fear of total loss.
questions.p: Dem create NAIS mainly to help farmers protect dia money if bad weather or disaster spoil dia farm. E dey give farmers confidence make dem invest well-well for agriculture.

questions.q: Which of the following describes the 'Green Revolution' program introduced in Nigeria during the early 1980s?
o: A campaign to promote the consumption of locally made textiles
A initiative to move farmers from the North to the Southern forests
A policy to increase the use of chemical pesticides in cocoa farming
A strategy to boost food production through modern farming techniques
questions.e: The Green Revolution was a government policy aimed at achieving food self-sufficiency by introducing high-yielding crop varieties, fertilizers, and mechanized farming tools.
questions.p: Green Revolution na plan wey government make to help us grow plenty food. Dem bring better seed, fertilizer, and machine make farming easy and productive.

questions.q: In the Nigerian context, which of these is an example of an agricultural linkage effect?
o: The government increasing the tax on petroleum products
A farmer buying a new tractor from a local assembly plant
A rise in the cost of imported luxury vehicles in Lagos
A decrease in the rainfall pattern affecting crop yield
questions.e: Backward linkage occurs when the agricultural sector creates demand for the outputs of other industries, such as the manufacturing of farm equipment like tractors.
questions.p: Backward linkage dey happen when farming sector need things from other sectors, like when farmer need tractor from factory. So, farming dey make factory work dey move.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major constraint to agricultural productivity in the Nigerian middle-belt?
o: Lack of demand for staple foods in rural areas
Excessive use of modern irrigation technology
High cost of labor and inadequate storage facilities
Too many banks providing interest-free loans to farmers
questions.e: Many Nigerian farmers suffer huge post-harvest losses because they cannot store their surplus crops properly. Additionally, labor cost is rising as youths migrate to cities.
questions.p: Plenty farmers dey lose money because dem no get where to keep dia harvest well. Plus, as young people dey go city, labor come cost and e dey make work hard for farm.

questions.q: If a government agency fixes the price of maize above the equilibrium price, this is a policy of
o: Price floor
Price ceiling
Market liberalization
Subsidy elimination
questions.e: A price floor is a government-imposed minimum price set above the market equilibrium price to protect farmers' income by ensuring they get a guaranteed minimum return.
questions.p: If government set price higher than wetin market say, na 'Price Floor' be that. Dem dey do am so say farmer go fit sell im food get better profit.

questions.q: The shift of labor from the agricultural sector to the industrial sector is a classic indicator of
o: Structural transformation
Economic stagnation
Agricultural revolution
Trade deficit
questions.e: Structural transformation refers to the process where an economy moves from being primarily based on agriculture to one based on industry and services as it develops.
questions.p: As country dey develop, people dey leave farm go work for factory or office. We dey call this 'structural transformation' as the economy change.

questions.q: Which of these is considered a 'cash crop' in the Nigerian economy?
o: Yam
Cocoyam
Cocoa
Cassava
questions.e: Cash crops are those primarily grown for export or sale in the commercial market rather than for immediate subsistence consumption. Cocoa is a leading export crop for Nigeria.
questions.p: Cash crops na crop wey dem dey grow mostly for sell or export, no be just for home food. Cocoa na big example wey Nigeria dey sell outside.

questions.q: The use of land tenure systems in Nigeria often discourages long-term agricultural investment because
o: It makes it impossible to buy land in the rural areas
It promotes collective ownership of all land by the state
It forces every farmer to pay taxes to the federal government
It creates insecurity of land ownership for smallholder farmers
questions.e: Insecure land tenure means farmers do not have permanent rights to the land they cultivate. This discourages them from investing in capital-intensive improvements like irrigation or permanent tree crops.
questions.p: If person no get clear paper for land, e go fear to invest big money there. If dem fit take the land from am anytime, e no go fit plant tree or build better structure.

questions.q: Which of the following is an advantage of the 'Operation Feed the Nation' (OFN) policy?
o: It focused exclusively on the fishing industry in the Niger Delta
It aimed to reduce food imports and encourage local cultivation
It mandated that all civil servants must own a farm
It provided free land to all Nigerians in the cities
questions.e: OFN was launched by the Obasanjo military administration to mobilize Nigerians to engage in farming to reduce dependence on imported food items.
questions.p: Operation Feed the Nation na program to make every Nigerian start to plant something. The main aim na make we stop to dey rely on food from abroad.

questions.q: What is the primary reason why Nigeria still imports food despite its vast arable land?
o: The population growth rate often outpaces the food production growth rate
Nigerians prefer to eat only foreign-made food items
There are no seeds available to be planted in Nigeria
The soil in Nigeria is not suitable for any crop production
questions.e: While Nigeria has land, the speed at which the population increases often exceeds the speed at which agricultural technology and output grow, leading to food gaps.
questions.p: Even though we get big land, the way our population dey increase plenty pass the way we dey produce food. Na why we still dey import food to feed everybody.

questions.q: Which of these is a direct impact of 'Extension Services' on agricultural output?
o: It increases the market price of fertilizer in the open market
It provides information on modern farming techniques to farmers
It imports high-quality tractors from overseas for personal use
It serves as a regulatory body for agricultural labor unions
questions.e: Extension workers act as bridges between researchers and farmers, teaching them new ways to plant, manage pests, and increase yields.
questions.p: Extension workers dey go meet farmers for bush to show dem better ways to plant and harvest. Na knowledge dem dey give farmers to make work better.

questions.q: In the context of the Nigerian economy, a 'subsistence farmer' is one who
o: Specializes only in the production of exportable spices
Uses advanced biotechnology to produce genetically modified crops
Produces mainly for the consumption of his household
Employs over 50 workers on a large mechanized plantation
questions.e: Subsistence farming is a form of farming where nearly all of the crops or livestock raised are used to maintain the farmer and the farmer's family, leaving little to no surplus for sale.
questions.p: Subsistence farmer na person wey dey farm mainly to feed im family. Wetin remain after dem don eat, e fit sell am, but the main goal na home food.

questions.q: Which of the following business organisations is owned by at least two and at most twenty persons whose liability is generally unlimited?
o: Public limited company
Cooperative society
Public corporation
Partnership
questions.e: A partnership is formed by 2 to 20 individuals (or up to 50 for professional practices) who pull resources together and share unlimited liability. Public companies require a minimum of seven members with limited liability. Cooperatives focus on member welfare rather than profit maximisation.
questions.p: Na partnership be business wey two to twenty people dey form, and their liability no get limit if wahala come. Public company and cooperative get different rule and member number.

questions.q: A deliberate policy by the government to encourage the establishment of manufacturing industries in rural areas of Nigeria is primarily aimed at achieving which of the following?
o: Reducing rural-urban migration
Maximising transport costs for firms
Increasing urban migration
Eliminating the petroleum sector
questions.e: Locating industries in rural areas creates jobs and infrastructural development there, which discourages people from moving to overcrowded cities. This balances regional development and curbs rural-urban drift.
questions.p: When government carry industry go village, e dey help create work and light for rural area so people no go pack come Lagos or Abuja anyhow.

questions.q: Which of the following describes a public limited company?
o: It is managed solely by the government without private participation
Shares cannot be transferred without the consent of all directors
Shares are sold freely to the general public through the stock exchange
Membership is restricted to a maximum of fifty shareholders
questions.e: A public limited company (Plc) raises capital by selling its shares openly to the general public via the stock exchange. Private limited companies restrict share transfers and cap membership at fifty.
questions.p: Na public limited company shares people dey buy and sell freely for stock market. Private company own no be so, dem dey restrict transfer.

questions.q: The concentration of manufacturing industries in a particular town or region, leading to shared benefits such as skilled labour and auxiliary services, is known as:
o: Public-private partnership
Localization of industries
Vertical integration
Merger and acquisition
questions.e: Localization (or agglomeration) of industries occurs when many firms in the same or related industries cluster together in an area to enjoy external economies of scale. Vertical integration involves combining different stages of production within one firm.
questions.p: Localization of industry mean say plenty factory pack enter one area so dem fit enjoy similar benefit like skilled workers and good market together.

questions.q: A major disadvantage of sole proprietorship as a form of business organization is:
o: Sharing of profits with numerous shareholders
Legal requirement to publish annual accounts
Difficulty in decision making
Unlimited liability of the owner
questions.e: In a sole proprietorship, the owner's personal assets can be seized to pay off business debts because of unlimited liability. Decision making is actually very fast since there is only one boss.
questions.p: Sole proprietorship get big problem of unlimited liability, meaning if business debt enter red, person personal property fit go down.

questions.q: Which of the following factors is LEAST important when deciding the location of a cement manufacturing factory in Nigeria?
o: Access to a good transport network to the market
Availability of reliable power supply
Proximity to bulky raw materials like limestone
Proximity to a major airport for international courier services
questions.e: Cement is a heavy and bulky product made from limestone, making raw material proximity and transport networks critical. Air courier services are irrelevant for bulk industrial cement distribution.
questions.p: Cement na heavy good, so limestone and road matter pass airport courier service when you wan site factory.

questions.q: A business arrangement where two or more independent companies combine their operations to form a completely new and single enterprise is called a:
o: Consortium
Merger
Cartel
Holding company
questions.e: A merger occurs when two or more separate firms agree to join forces to create a single new corporate entity. A cartel is an agreement among competing firms to control prices or output, while maintaining separate identities.
questions.p: Merger happen when two or three different companies join body become one single company to work together.

questions.q: Import substitution industrialisation strategy in a developing country like Nigeria is primarily designed to:
o: Produce domestically goods that were previously imported
Rely entirely on foreign loans for industrial growth
Discourage local raw material sourcing
Encourage the importation of finished luxury goods
questions.e: Import substitution industrialisation (ISI) aims to reduce foreign dependence by producing previously imported manufactured goods locally. This helps conserve foreign exchange and creates domestic jobs.
questions.p: Import substitution strategy na to produce the things wey we dey normally buy abroad inside Nigeria, so we go save foreign exchange.

questions.q: What is the primary objective of a consumers' cooperative society?
o: To maximize profit for external shareholders
To export agricultural produce to foreign markets
To eliminate middlemen and sell goods to members at affordable prices
To provide cheap loans exclusively to business tycoons
questions.e: Consumers' cooperatives are formed by buyers to purchase goods in bulk directly from manufacturers, cutting out costly middlemen and passing savings to members. Profit maximization for outside investors is not the goal.
questions.p: Consumers cooperative na to cut off middleman so members fit buy food and goods for cheaper price.

questions.q: When a manufacturing firm expands its scale of production by combining different successive stages of production under one management, it is engaging in:
o: Diversification
Horizontal integration
Vertical integration
Conglomerate merger
questions.e: Vertical integration involves a firm taking over stages of production earlier (backward) or later (forward) in the supply chain. Horizontal integration involves firms at the same stage of production joining together.
questions.p: Vertical integration mean say company take charge of different steps of production from raw material to final market under one roof.

questions.q: Which of the following organisations is financed mainly through tax payers' funds and managed by an appointed board for public service rather than profit?
o: Joint stock enterprise
Registered partnership
Private limited company
Public corporation
questions.e: Public corporations (statutory corporations) are established, owned, and funded by the government to provide essential services to the public, prioritising welfare over profit.
questions.p: Public corporation na government own business wey dem establish to give people service like water or light, no be just pure profit.

questions.q: If a manufacturing firm experiences decreasing returns to scale as it expands its plant size indefinitely, this is primarily caused by:
o: Managerial inefficiencies and bureaucratic delays
Lower cost of raw materials
Economies of scale
Excessive availability of skilled labour
questions.e: As a firm becomes excessively large, coordination, communication, and managerial control become difficult, leading to diseconomies of scale and decreasing returns to scale. Lower costs and skilled labour would actually cause economies of scale.
questions.p: When company too big, management wahala, slow communication, and bureaucracy go enter, make efficiency drop down naim be diseconomies of scale.

questions.q: Which of the following is classified as a renewable natural resource in the Nigerian economy?
o: Natural gas
Forest timber
Crude petroleum
Bitumen
questions.e: Forest timber is a renewable resource because trees can be replanted and grown over time. Crude oil, natural gas, and bitumen are non-renewable exhaustible minerals.
questions.p: Na timber be renewable resource because pesin fit plant new trees make dem grow again. Crude oil, gas and bitumen na minerals wey dey finish when you pack dem finish.

questions.q: A major economic challenge directly caused by heavy reliance on crude oil revenue in Nigeria is
o: hyperinflation of agricultural land values
excessive surplus in the balance of visible trade
Dutch Disease syndrome affecting non-oil exports
rapid industrialization of rural communities
questions.e: Dutch Disease occurs when massive revenues from a single natural resource like oil cause the local currency to appreciate, making other local sectors like agriculture and manufacturing uncompetitive.
questions.p: Dutch Disease happen when money from one oil business too plenty, make our money strong pass normal, con carry agriculture and other local goods make dem expensive to export abroad.

questions.q: Natural resources that cannot be replaced once they are extracted and consumed are known as
o: exhaustible resources
flow resources
biological resources
perennial resources
questions.e: Exhaustible or non-renewable resources exist in fixed quantities in the earth's crust and deplete permanently with usage. Flow and biological resources can regenerate naturally.
questions.p: Exhaustible resources mean those things wey once you consume am finish, e no dey come back again. Flow and biological resources dey renew themselves.

questions.q: In the Nigerian petroleum industry, a Joint Venture (JV) arrangement typically involves the
o: exclusive management by indigenous private artisanal refiners
partnership between the state oil company and international oil companies
Federal Government holding 100 percent equity ownership
sole proprietorship of foreign multinational corporations
questions.e: A Joint Venture in the Nigerian oil sector is a contractual partnership where the national oil corporation shares costs and equity with multinational oil companies like Shell or Chevron.
questions.p: Joint Venture na partnership arrangement where government company join hand with big foreign oil companies to share cost and profit together.

questions.q: The process of converting raw crude oil into usable petroleum products such as petrol, diesel, and kerosene is carried out through
o: hydraulic fracturing
subterranean seismic imaging
catalytic hydrogenation
fractional distillation
questions.e: Crude oil is a mixture of various hydrocarbons which are separated into different useful products at different boiling points through fractional distillation in a refinery.
questions.p: Na fractional distillation dem dey use for refinery take separate crude oil into petrol, diesel, kerosene and other things based on dia boiling points.

questions.q: What term describes the economic rent paid by oil mining companies to the Nigerian government for the right to extract crude oil?
o: Petroleum profit tax
Royalty
Value Added Tax
Stamp duty
questions.e: Royalty is a mandatory payment made by extractive companies to the resource owner (the government) based on the volume or value of minerals extracted, distinct from profit taxes.
questions.p: Royalty na the money wey oil company must pay government just because dem carry oil comot from ground, no be profit tax o.

questions.q: A primary objective of establishing public refineries in Nigeria was to
o: export all finished petrochemicals to neighbouring ECOWAS nations
subsidize electricity generation for rural farmers only
eliminate the importation of refined petroleum products
promote small-scale artisanal palm oil production
questions.e: Local refineries were built primarily to process domestic crude oil into finished products locally, thereby reducing dependence on costly imported petroleum products.
questions.p: Dem build refinery for Nigeria make local crude oil turn to petrol inside house, so we no go dey go abroad buy refined fuel again.

questions.q: Gas flaring in the Niger Delta region of Nigeria creates negative externalities primarily because it leads to
o: environmental pollution and loss of economic livelihood
enhanced generation of free electricity for host communities
massive reduction in global crude oil prices
increased fertility of swampy agricultural soils
questions.e: Gas flaring releases toxic pollutants and greenhouse gases, causing environmental degradation, acid rain, and destruction of farming and fishing livelihoods.
questions.p: Gas flaring dey spoil environment, bring acid rain, and scatter fishing and farming work for Niger Delta area.

questions.q: Which of the following mineral resources in Nigeria is predominantly used as a raw material for cement production?
o: Gold
Columbite
Iron ore
Limestone
questions.e: Limestone is the key raw material required for the manufacturing of cement, which is vital for the construction sector in Nigeria.
questions.p: Na limestone dem dey grind use make cement wey builders dey use build house everywhere for Nigeria.

questions.q: The establishment of the Nigerian Content Development and Monitoring Board (NCDMB) is primarily aimed at
o: banning the exportation of crude petroleum completely
increasing foreign expatriate quota in oil firms
promoting local participation and utilization of Nigerian goods and services in the oil sector
transferring total ownership of oil wells to private individuals
questions.e: NCDMB was created to ensure that Nigerian companies, local labor, and locally produced goods take a greater percentage of contracts and value creation in the petroleum industry.
questions.p: NCDMB make sure say na Nigerian companies and local workers get major contracts and work for oil industry instead of giving everything to foreigners.

questions.q: A major challenge facing solid mineral exploitation in Nigeria compared to the petroleum sector is
o: over-reliance on illegal and artisanal mining with low capital investment
complete absence of government regulatory policies
too many multinational corporations dominating gold production
excessive contribution to the federation account
questions.e: Unlike the capital-intensive and structured petroleum sector, the solid minerals sector in Nigeria is heavily plagued by illegal, informal artisanal mining and low formal investment.
questions.p: Unlike oil sector where big money dey, solid minerals sector suffer because na illegal miners and small-small people with small money dey run am.

questions.q: The total number of people living in a defined geographical territory of Nigeria at a specific point in time is best referred to as
o: population census
optimum population
working population
population size
questions.e: Population size refers to the absolute count of individuals residing in a specific area at a given time. A census is merely the official process of collecting this data.
questions.p: Population size mean the total number of people wey dey live for one place at a particular time. Census na just the process wey government take count them.

questions.q: An economy experiences a situation where an increase in its population leads to a decrease in output per head because the natural resources are overstretched. This condition describes
o: population growth
overpopulation
underpopulation
optimum population
questions.e: Overpopulation occurs when the population exceeds the carrying capacity of the available resources, leading to a decline in living standards and output per head.
questions.p: Overpopulation happen when people too plenty pass the resources wey dey ground, make standard of living come drop.

questions.q: Which of the following demographic concepts represents the number of live births per one thousand population in a year?
o: Fertility rate
Birth rate
Mortality rate
Growth rate
questions.e: Crude birth rate is specifically defined as the number of live births per 1,000 members of the population in a given year.
questions.p: Birth rate na the number of pikin wey dem born alive per every one thousand people for inside one year.

questions.q: Thomas Malthus postulated that population increases in a geometrical progression while food production increases in an
o: harmonic progression
exponential progression
algebraic progression
arithmetical progression
questions.e: According to the Malthusian theory, population grows geometrically (1, 2, 4, 8, 16) while food supply grows arithmetically (1, 2, 3, 4, 5).
questions.p: Malthus talk say population dey multiply fast like 1, 2, 4, 8, but food production dey increase slowly like 1, 2, 3, 4.

questions.q: A country has a total population of 50,000,000, a land area of 200,000 square kilometres, and an active working force of 20,000,000. What is the population density of the country?
o: 250 persons/km^2
400 persons/km^2
625 persons/km^2
100 persons/km^2
questions.e: Population density is calculated as Total Population divided by Land Area. That is 50,000,000 / 200,000 = 250 persons per square kilometre.
questions.p: To find population density, divide total population by land area. That na 50 million divide by 200 thousand, wey give us 250 persons per square kilometre.

questions.q: The demographic transition theory suggests that in the second stage of population growth
o: birth rate is high and death rate is high
birth rate falls rapidly while death rate remains constant
birth rate is high and death rate begins to fall rapidly
birth rate is low and death rate is low
questions.e: In stage two of the demographic transition model, improvements in health and sanitation cause death rates to drop sharply while birth rates remain high, leading to rapid population growth.
questions.p: For stage two of demographic transition, better hospital and clean water go make death rate drop sharply, but people go still dey born pikin plenty.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major economic consequence of a high dependency ratio in a developing nation like Nigeria?
o: Increased national savings and investment
Rapid reduction in poverty levels
Increased pressure on public social infrastructure like schools and hospitals
Higher tax revenue for the government
questions.e: A high dependency ratio means a large portion of the population (children and aged) depends on the few working citizens, straining public amenities like education and healthcare.
questions.p: If dependency ratio high, e mean say small working people dey carry plenty pikin and old people, witch dey put heavy pressure on schools and hospitals.

questions.q: The population structure that classifies a country's population by gender and age groups is usually visually represented using a
o: population pyramid
pie chart
Lorenz curve
bar graph
questions.e: A population pyramid is a graphical illustration that shows the distribution of various age groups and sexes in a population.
questions.p: Na population pyramid dem dey use draw how age groups and male and female take spread for inside country population.

questions.q: Optimum population is achieved when
o: the birth rate equals the death rate
per capita income is at its maximum level
the country has the highest possible number of inhabitants
food production is equal to population size
questions.e: Optimum population is the size that yields the maximum output per head (per capita income) given the available resources and technology.
questions.p: Optimum population na that population size where income per head reach highest level because resources balance well with people.

questions.q: Why is an accurate population census considered difficult to conduct in many developing countries?
o: Universal access to modern digital registration
Lack of political interference
Excessive availability of trained personnel
Cultural taboos, deliberate falsification, and poor logistics
questions.e: Census counting faces challenges in developing nations due to bad roads (logistics), people lying for political/ethnic gains, and cultural beliefs.
questions.p: Census dey hard to count for developing countries because of bad road, people wey dey lie about their number because of politics, and some cultural beliefs.

questions.q: If a country records a crude birth rate of 35 per 1000 and a crude death rate of 15 per 1000, what is the natural growth rate of the population expressed as a percentage?
o: 2.0 percent
20.0 percent
50.0 percent
0.5 percent
questions.e: Natural growth rate = Birth rate minus Death rate = 35 - 15 = 20 per 1,000. Expressed as a percentage, (20 / 1,000) * 100 = 2.0 percent.
questions.p: Natural growth rate na birth rate minus death rate, which na 35 minus 15 equal to 20 per thousand. Change am to percentage by dividing by 10, e go give you 2 percent.

questions.q: An ageing population refers to a demographic situation where
o: life expectancy is extremely short
the working class constitutes over 90 percent of the population
the proportion of elderly people in the total population is rising
the proportion of children under 15 years is increasing rapidly
questions.e: An ageing population is characterized by an increasing median age in the population due to declining fertility rates and rising life expectancy.
questions.p: Ageing population mean say old people plenty pass inside the total population because people dey live long and birth rate don reduce.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines the concept of comparative advantage in international trade?
o: The ability of a country to produce a commodity at a lower absolute cost than any trading partner.
The ability of a country to produce a commodity at a lower opportunity cost than its trading partner.
The maintenance of a favorable balance of trade over a continuous fiscal year.
The total elimination of tariffs and import quotas between two friendly nations.
questions.e: Comparative advantage is based on the principle of opportunity cost, meaning a country produces a good at a lower sacrifice of other goods than another country. Absolute cost advantage refers instead to absolute advantage. Trade policies and trade balances are separate concepts.
questions.p: Comparative advantage mean say country dey produce something with lower opportunity cost pass another country. E no mean say dem must get lower absolute cost for everything.

questions.q: Country A uses 4 hours of labor to produce 1 unit of yam and 2 hours for 1 unit of garri. Country B uses 6 hours for 1 unit of yam and 3 hours for 1 unit of garri. Based on this, which of the following statements is correct?
o: Country A has a comparative advantage in the production of yam.
Country B has a comparative advantage in the production of garri.
Both countries have equal opportunity costs, so no mutually beneficial trade can occur.
Country A has a comparative advantage in the production of garri.
questions.e: For Country A, the opportunity cost of 1 yam is 2 garri (4/2), and for garri it is 0.5 yam. For Country B, 1 yam is 2 garri (6/3), and for garri it is 0.5 yam. Since the opportunity costs are identical for both countries, no comparative advantage exists.
questions.p: If you calculate am, both Country A and Country B get the same opportunity cost for yam and garri. Because their costs match, trade no go benefit any of them.

questions.q: An adverse movement in the terms of trade of a developing nation like Nigeria implies that:
o: the value of the national currency has appreciated against major trading currencies.
the volume of exports has exceeded the volume of imports.
foreign reserves have increased significantly due to favorable oil prices.
more units of exports are now required to buy a given quantity of imports.
questions.e: Terms of trade represent the ratio of export prices to import prices. An adverse or worsening terms of trade means export prices are falling relative to import prices, so the country must export more to acquire the same amount of imports.
questions.p: Worse terms of trade mean say export price don fall, so you must export plenty goods before you fit buy small imports from oyinbo country.

questions.q: Which of the following items is recorded on the credit side of a country's balance of payments current account?
o: Payment for shipping services rendered by foreign vessels to domestic importers.
Expenditure by domestic tourists holidaying in Ghana.
Purchase of foreign shares by a local investment bank.
Export of crude petroleum to European refineries.
questions.e: The credit side of the current account records all transactions that bring foreign exchange into the country. Exporting crude petroleum earns foreign revenue, making it a credit item. The other options involve outflows of funds, which are debits.
questions.p: Anytime money enter country because we sell goods outside, na credit. When we export crude oil, money dey come inside Nigeria, so na credit side.

questions.q: A deficit in a country's balance of payments can be corrected through which of the following measures?
o: Devaluing the domestic currency to make exports cheaper.
Relaxing exchange controls to allow free capital flight.
Removing all forms of tariffs on imported finished goods.
Granting subsidies to domestic importers of luxury goods.
questions.e: Devaluing the currency lowers the external price of exports and raises the domestic price of imports, which boosts export earnings and discourages imports, thereby correcting a balance of payments deficit.
questions.p: If country get balance of payments deficit, dem fit devalue their money so that foreign people go buy our goods cheap, and we go stop to dey import plenty foreign things.

questions.q: The official rate at which one currency is exchanged for another in a free market is determined primarily by:
o: the directives issued by the apex commercial bank.
the total volume of gold reserves held by the central government.
the forces of market demand and supply of the currencies.
agreements signed at international trade summits.
questions.e: In a floating exchange rate system, the exchange rate is determined entirely by the market forces of demand and supply for the respective currencies.
questions.p: For free market, na demand and supply of money dey set the exchange rate, no be just wetin central bank talk anyhow.

questions.q: If the exchange rate of the Nigerian Naira (₦) against the US Dollar ($) moves from ₦400/$1 to ₦800/$1, the Naira has experienced:
o: revaluation.
depreciation.
deflation.
appreciation.
questions.e: When it takes more units of the domestic currency (Naira) to buy one unit of a foreign currency (Dollar), the domestic currency has depreciated in value.
questions.p: Before na ₦400 you need to buy one dollar, now na ₦800. E mean say Naira value don fall, we call am depreciation.

questions.q: Country X exports goods worth $500 million, imports goods worth $700 million, receives $50 million in investment income from abroad, and pays $30 million as interest on foreign loans. What is the balance of visible trade?
o: Deficit of $180 million
Surplus of $180 million
Surplus of $200 million
Deficit of $200 million
questions.e: Visible trade (balance of trade) deals strictly with physical goods. Visible exports ($500m) minus visible imports ($700m) equals -$200 million, which is a deficit of $200 million. Investment income and interest are invisible items.
questions.p: Visible trade na just physical goods wey we sell and buy. Export ($500m) minus Import ($700m) give us deficit of $200 million. Investment income no join.

questions.q: Which of the following constitutes an 'invisible' item in the balance of payments accounts?
o: Delivery of cement produced in Sokoto to Niger Republic.
Export of cocoa bags to London.
Freight charges paid to a foreign shipping company.
Import of industrial machinery from Germany.
questions.e: Invisible items refer to services rather than physical goods. Freight charges, tourism, and banking services are services (invisibles), whereas cocoa, machinery, and cement are physical goods (visibles).
questions.p: Invisible trade na services wey you no fit touch with hand, like shipping charges or tourism. Cocoa and machinery na visible goods.

questions.q: A major distinction between terms of trade and balance of payments is that:
o: terms of trade measures price ratios of exports to imports, whereas balance of payments records actual monetary transactions.
terms of trade is calculated by the Ministry of Finance, whereas balance of payments is managed by commercial banks.
terms of trade applies only to developing countries, while balance of payments applies only to developed nations.
balance of payments excludes services, whereas terms of trade includes all international service payments.
questions.e: Terms of trade is a ratio index comparing export prices to import prices. Balance of payments is a comprehensive accounting statement of all monetary transactions between a country and the rest of the world over a period.
questions.p: Terms of trade na ratio of export price to import price, but balance of payments na the real money record of everything wey enter and leave country.

questions.q: Protectionism in international trade is often justified by developing nations on the grounds of:
o: ensuring complete equality in per capita income among trading nations.
preventing infant industries from being crushed by foreign competition.
maximizing the free movement of cheap consumer goods for citizens.
reducing government revenue derived from custom duties and tariffs.
questions.e: Developing countries use protectionist tools like tariffs and quotas to shield new domestic industries ('infant industries') until they are strong enough to compete globally.
questions.p: Government dey protect local industries with tariff so foreign goods no go kill small young companies before dem grow.

questions.q: If a country experiences a sustained surplus on its balance of payments current account over several years, the most direct long-term effect is likely to be:
o: severe depreciation of its domestic currency.
total collapse of its domestic manufacturing sector.
rapid depletion of its foreign exchange reserves.
accumulation of foreign assets and appreciation of its currency.
questions.e: A continuous current account surplus means the country earns more foreign currency than it spends abroad, leading to a buildup of foreign reserves and upward pressure (appreciation) on the domestic currency.
questions.p: If country dey make surplus every year, money plenty for pocket. Foreign reserves go increase, and their money value go appreciate.

questions.q: Which of the following international financial institutions primarily focuses on long-term capital investments for infrastructural development in developing countries?
o: World Bank
Paris Club
London Club
International Monetary Fund
questions.e: The World Bank, specifically through the IBRD and IDA, provides long-term loans and grants for developmental projects and infrastructure. The IMF primarily focuses on short-term balance of payments stabilization.
questions.p: Na World Bank dey give long-term money for project like road and bridge for developing country. IMF na just short-term support for balance of payment.

questions.q: A core objective of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) in promoting regional integration is the:
o: enforcement of a unified tax rate for all registered businesses in the region
gradual elimination of customs duties and non-tariff barriers among member nations
harmonization of member states' national currencies into a single legal tender
establishment of a common military force to police all West African borders
questions.e: ECOWAS was primarily established to promote economic cooperation and integration, starting with the reduction and eventual elimination of tariffs and trade barriers to form a free trade area and customs union.
questions.p: ECOWAS main target na to make trade easy by removing tax and barrier between member countries so goods fit move well.

questions.q: The Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) primarily influences the global oil market by regulating:
o: the global retail price of premium motor spirit
the international freight charges for oil tankers
member countries' crude oil production quotas
subsidy rates applied by oil-importing nations
questions.e: OPEC uses production quotas for its member countries to manage overall supply, which in turn influences international crude oil prices.
questions.p: OPEC dey use production quota to control how much crude oil each member country go pump, and dat one dey help them regulate global price.

questions.q: Which body serves as the principal multilateral institution responsible for setting global trade rules and resolving trade disputes between nations?
o: United Nations Conference on Trade and Development
Economic and Social Council
World Trade Organization
International Chamber of Commerce
questions.e: The World Trade Organization (WTO) oversees the implementation of multilateral trade agreements and provides a platform for settling trade disputes.
questions.p: Na World Trade Organization dey handle global trade rules and settle fight when trade problem happen between countries.

questions.q: The primary mandate of the African Development Bank (AfDB) is to:
o: manage the national debts of heavily indebted poor African countries
mobilize resources for economic and social progress in African nations
regulate the exchange rates of African currencies against the US Dollar
finance commercial banks operating within ECOWAS
questions.e: The AfDB group aims to spur sustainable economic development and social progress in its regional member countries by mobilizing financial resources.
questions.p: AfDB work na to gather money and support economic and social development projects all over African countries.

questions.q: When a member country experiences a severe balance of payments crisis, which international organization is typically approached for short-term macroeconomic stabilization loans?
o: International Monetary Fund
African Development Bank
World Bank
International Finance Corporation
questions.e: The IMF provides financial assistance to countries facing balance of payments difficulties to help them restore macroeconomic stability.
questions.p: If country get severe balance of payment problem, na IMF dem dey run go meet for short-term rescue money.

questions.q: A major challenge hindering the full realization of the ECOWAS protocol on the free movement of persons, goods, and services is the:
o: uniformity of economic policies across all West African countries
strict standardization of national minimum wages in the sub-region
total absence of common borders among member states
proliferation of unauthorized checkpoints and harassment along transport corridors
questions.e: Despite protocols allowing free movement, travelers and traders within ECOWAS often face delays, extortion, and harassment at numerous security checkpoints along major corridors.
questions.p: Even though law say make people move freely, too many checkpoint and illegal tax for road dey slow down trade and movement for West Africa.

questions.q: How does the World Trade Organization (WTO) primarily enforce its trade agreements among member nations?
o: By seizing shipments of goods at international ports
Through a structured dispute settlement mechanism and authorized retaliatory measures
Through the direct imposition of fines paid into the United Nations treasury
By deploying military sanctions against defaulting states
questions.e: The WTO relies on a formal dispute settlement body where panels investigate complaints and can authorize aggrieved nations to apply retaliatory tariffs if rulings are ignored.
questions.p: WTO dey use dispute settlement process to judge trade fights, and dem fit allow country wey win to put counter-tax if the other party refuse to obey.

questions.q: Which of the following describes a structural adjustment program (SAP) frequently associated with International Monetary Fund conditionalities?
o: Nationalization of all foreign-owned manufacturing industries
Massive expansion of public sector employment and salaries
Removal of government subsidies, trade liberalization, and currency devaluation
Fixing of domestic interest rates at near-zero percentages
questions.e: IMF structural adjustment programs typically require fiscal discipline, including subsidy removal, trade opening, and realistic exchange rate determination.
questions.p: IMF condition normally include make government remove subsidy, open market for trade, and allow exchange rate to float.

questions.q: Unlike the World Bank, which concentrates on project-specific financing for development, the International Monetary Fund focuses principally on:
o: building primary healthcare centers across developing nations
financing regional hydroelectric dams and transport networks
funding poverty reduction NGO programs in rural communities
providing short-term financial assistance for macroeconomic imbalances
questions.e: The key distinction is that the World Bank funds specific long-term development projects, whereas the IMF provides short-term support for macroeconomic and balance of payments stability.
questions.p: World Bank dey face long-term project like dam and school, but IMF na just short-term money for macro-economic wahala.

questions.q: Which of the following represents a primary characteristic of a Customs Union, such as those promoted in regional integration frameworks?
o: Abolition of internal tariffs combined with a common external tariff against non-members
Complete merging of all member states' central banks into a single monetary authority
Free movement of labour without any form of documentation across borders
Total ban on the importation of manufactured goods from outside the region
questions.e: A customs union is defined by the removal of tariffs between members plus the adoption of a common external tariff (CET) applied to imports from non-member countries.
questions.p: Customs Union mean say member countries no go charge tax among themselves, and dem go carry one uniform external tax for goods coming from outside.

questions.q: In the context of international trade negotiations under the WTO, what is the core principle of 'Most-Favoured-Nation' (MFN) treatment?
o: Granting special trade privileges exclusively to former colonial powers
Exempting domestic industries entirely from international competition
Treating one's trading partners equally, such that concessions granted to one must be extended to all other WTO members
Imposing higher tariff rates on developing nations compared to developed nations
questions.e: The MFN principle requires WTO members to treat all other members equally; if a country lowers a trade barrier for one trading partner, it must do so for all WTO members.
questions.p: MFN rule mean say make you treat all WTO members equal; if you give special trade favor to one country, you must extend am to all other members too.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the supply of labour in an economy?
o: The total number of hours workers are willing and able to work at a given wage rate
The total output produced by all employed persons in a year
The total number of citizens living within the national boundaries
The total amount of money paid to workers in the formal sector
questions.e: Labour supply refers to the total number of man-hours that workers are willing and able to offer for employment at various wage rates over a given period. It depends on factors like the wage rate, population size, and working age.
questions.p: Na the total number of hours wey workers ready to work for particular wage rate be that. E depend on how much dem dey pay and how many people dey ready work.

questions.q: A situation where university graduates roam the streets of Lagos and Abuja for years without securing formal employment is classified as:
o: Seasonal unemployment
Structural unemployment
Cyclical unemployment
Frictional unemployment
questions.e: Structural unemployment occurs when there is a mismatch between the skills possessed by the workforce and the skills demanded by employers, or when there is a general shortage of jobs for specific qualifications.
questions.p: This one na structural unemployment because the type school wey dem go no match the kind work wey market want, abi job vacancies no dey at all for that sector.

questions.q: Trade unions primarily protect the economic interests of their members through which of the following methods?
o: Imposing direct taxes on manufacturing companies
Fixing the foreign exchange rate of the naira
Granting loans to commercial banks
Collective bargaining with employers
questions.e: Collective bargaining is the core tool used by trade unions to negotiate better wages, improved working conditions, and fringe benefits with employers on behalf of their members.
questions.p: Trade union dey use collective bargaining to carry mouth talk with management make dem increase salary and better working condition for their members.

questions.q: If the government of Nigeria increases the national minimum wage significantly above the market equilibrium wage, the immediate likely economic consequence in the labour market is:
o: Excess supply of labour leading to unemployment
Elimination of all forms of inflation
Excess demand for labour
A reduction in the cost of production for firms
questions.e: A minimum wage set above the equilibrium wage makes labour more expensive for employers, reducing the quantity of labour demanded while increasing the quantity supplied, resulting in unemployment (excess supply).
questions.p: If government increase minimum wage pass market level, employers go reduce workers because money too much to pay, and many people go rush come find work, so unemployment go rise.

questions.q: Unemployment that arises temporarily when workers move from one job to another in search of better prospects is known as:
o: Cyclical unemployment
Frictional unemployment
Disguised unemployment
Residual unemployment
questions.e: Frictional unemployment is the short-term unemployment that occurs when individuals are transitioning between jobs or entering the labour market for the first time while searching for suitable employment.
questions.p: Frictional unemployment na the small time wey person spend dey find another work after e leave the previous one or when e just graduate.

questions.q: Consider a farm in Kano where ten family members work on a small plot of land, but the actual output would remain exactly the same even if three members stopped working. This is an example of:
o: Open unemployment
Cyclical unemployment
Structural unemployment
Disguised unemployment
questions.e: Disguised unemployment occurs when individuals appear to be employed, but their marginal productivity is zero. Removing them from the production process does not reduce total output.
questions.p: Disguised unemployment be say person dey work, but even if e no show for work, the output no go reduce at all because surplus people surplus the job.

questions.q: Which of the following factors will cause a backward-bending individual supply curve for labour?
o: When wages fall to zero
When the substitution effect of a wage increase outweighs the income effect
When the income effect of a wage increase outweighs the substitution effect
When leisure becomes inferior as income rises
questions.e: At very high wage rates, the income effect dominates the substitution effect. Workers prefer to enjoy more leisure time rather than work extra hours because they are already earning enough income.
questions.p: When person salary don high reach, e fit decide say e want rest more instead of working extra hours. That income effect don pass substitution effect, make the supply curve bend backward.

questions.q: In a developing economy like Nigeria, rural-urban migration heavily contributes to urban unemployment primarily because:
o: Job seekers overestimate the probability of securing high-paying formal sector jobs in cities
The cost of living in rural areas is higher than in urban centers
Industries are evenly distributed across all local government areas
Urban areas have surplus fertile land for farming
questions.e: According to models like the Todaro model, rural-urban migration persists because migrants expect high urban wages, even though the actual probability of securing such jobs is low, leading to urban unemployment.
questions.p: People dey run leave village come town because dem think say big money full Lagos or Port Harcourt, even though work no easy to see.

questions.q: If the marginal revenue product (MRP) of labour for a firm in Onitsha is ₦5,000 per day and the prevailing daily wage rate is ₦4,000, the rational profit-maximizing firm should:
o: Shut down operations temporarily
Keep the number of workers constant
Employ more workers
Lay off some workers immediately
questions.e: A firm maximizes profit by hiring workers up to the point where the marginal revenue product equals the wage rate (MRP = Wage). Since MRP (₦5,000) is greater than the wage (₦4,000), hiring more workers adds more to revenue than to cost.
questions.p: Since the extra money wey worker dey bring enter (MRP) pass the salary wey dem dey pay am, company go make profit if dem employ more people.

questions.q: Which of the following economic policies is most effective in combating cyclical unemployment during an economic recession?
o: Contractionary monetary policy
Expansionary fiscal policy
Reduction of government expenditure on infrastructure
Imposition of high tariffs on all imports
questions.e: Cyclical unemployment results from a deficiency in aggregate demand during a recession. Expansionary fiscal policy (increased government spending and tax cuts) boosts aggregate demand, encouraging firms to produce more and hire workers.
questions.p: When recession happen and demand fall make people lose job, government need to use expansionary fiscal policy like building roads to pump money inside economy so companies go employ people back.

questions.q: A situation where a neutral third party is invited to listen to both employers and a trade union and then impose a binding settlement on them is called:
o: Collective bargaining
Arbitration
Mediation
Conciliation
questions.e: Arbitration involves a third party hearing both sides of a dispute and making a decision that is legally binding on both the employers and the trade union. This differs from mediation, where the third party only assists in reaching a voluntary agreement.
questions.p: Arbitration na when independent person judge matter between union and management, and whatever decision e give, both sides must obey am.

questions.q: In a certain rural community in Kebbi State, there is enough borehole water to meet only half of the residents' daily needs, so the community leaders have introduced a rationing system so that everyone gets some water each day. Which basic economic concept does this situation best illustrate?
o: Division of labour
Specialization
Scarcity
Economic growth
questions.e: Scarcity means that resources (like the borehole water) are not enough to meet all the wants of the people, forcing rationing. This is different from choice, which is about deciding among alternatives, though scarcity leads to the need for choice.
questions.p: Scarcity na when resource no reach to cover everybody need, like as the borehole water no reach everybody, dem go ration am. Na because water no plenty reach make dem dey share am small small.

questions.q: Bola receives a weekend allowance of N5,000 and ranks her wants in this order of importance: 1st - a textbook costing N3,500; 2nd - transport top-up costing N2,000; 3rd - snacks costing N1,200; 4th - a movie ticket costing N1,000. She uses her allowance to buy only the textbook, her most preferred want. What is the opportunity cost of her decision?
o: The movie ticket she did not buy
The textbook she eventually bought
The snacks she did not buy
The transport top-up she did not buy
questions.e: Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative that is given up when a choice is made, not everything forgone or the item chosen itself. Since transport top-up is Bola's second most preferred want after the textbook, it is her opportunity cost.
questions.p: Opportunity cost na the next best thing wey person sacrifice when e choose one option. Since transport top-up na the number 2 thing wey Bola rank after textbook, na im be her opportunity cost, no be snacks or movie ticket.

questions.q: A fresh graduate from Ahmadu Bello University receives four job offers with the following annual salaries: Oil company, N3,000,000; Commercial bank, N2,400,000; NGO, N2,100,000; Teaching job, N1,800,000. If he accepts the oil company job, what is the monetary value of his opportunity cost?
questions.e: Opportunity cost is the value of the single next best alternative forgone, not the sum of all other alternatives. Among the three jobs not chosen, the bank job (N2,400,000) is the highest-paying, so it represents the true opportunity cost; adding up all three forgone salaries (N7,300,000) is a common mistake.
questions.p: Opportunity cost na the one best option wey person leave, no be the total of everything wey e no choose. Among the remaining three jobs, bank job (N2,400,000) pay pass, so na im be the real opportunity cost, no be when you add all the three together to get N7,300,000.

questions.q: An economic system is best defined as the:
o: method a country uses to design its national flag
way a society organizes itself to decide what, how and for whom to produce
list of goods a country exports to other nations
process of printing new currency notes
questions.e: An economic system is simply the way a society is organized to solve the basic economic problems of what, how and for whom to produce. It does not relate to flags, printing money, or export lists.
questions.p: Economic system na how society arrange itself to decide wetin to produce, how to produce am, and who go chop am. E no concern flag, money printing or export list.

questions.q: Alhaji Musa owns a private poultry farm in Kano and sells eggs at prices he sets based on demand and supply. At the same time, the Federal Government owns and runs the national railway corporation and sets minimum wage laws that all employers, including Alhaji Musa, must obey. This arrangement best describes a:
o: subsistence economy
pure socialist economy
mixed economy
pure capitalist economy
questions.e: Here, private individuals own businesses and set prices (a capitalist feature), while the government owns some enterprises and regulates the private sector (a socialist feature). This combination of private and public control is exactly what defines a mixed economy.
questions.p: For dis case, private person dey run business and fix price (capitalism side), but government too dey run railway and dey make law wey private business must follow (socialism side). When both dey togeda like dis, na mixed economy be dat.

questions.q: In a centrally planned economy, the government alone fixes production targets for all goods without using market prices as a guide. Suppose planners set the yearly target for garri production far below what consumers actually want to buy. Which outcome is most likely to follow immediately in that economy?
o: A shortage of garri occurs, leading to queues or rationing
Garri prices fall sharply because of oversupply
Private traders quickly increase garri supply to meet demand
Garri becomes abundant and is exported in large quantities
questions.e: Without market prices to signal true demand, planners can easily set output too low, so the quantity available falls short of what people want. This mismatch causes shortages, forcing the use of queues or rationing, a common weakness of command economies.
questions.p: Since dem no dey use market price to guide production, planners fit set garri production too low pass wetin people need. Dis one go cause shortage, so people go dey queue or government go ration am, na common problem for command economy.

questions.q: The weekly savings (in ₦) of five traders in a market in Kano are: 400, 600, 500, 700, and 800. What is the arithmetic mean of their savings?
questions.e: Add all the values: 400+600+500+700+800 = 3000. Divide by the number of traders (5): 3000/5 = 600. So the mean saving is ₦600.
questions.p: Add all di money together: 400+600+500+700+800 = 3000. Divide am by 5 (di number of traders): 3000/5 = 600. So di mean na ₦600.

questions.q: The ages (in years) of eight workers in a company are: 22, 25, 23, 28, 26, 24, 30, and 27. What is the median age of the workers?
questions.e: First arrange the ages in order: 22,23,24,25,26,27,28,30. Since there are 8 (even) values, the median is the average of the 4th and 5th values, which are 25 and 26. So median = (25+26)/2 = 25.5.
questions.p: First arrange di ages from small to big: 22,23,24,25,26,27,28,30. Since na 8 people (even number), median na average of di 4th and 5th number, wey be 25 and 26. So median = (25+26)/2 = 25.5.

questions.q: In a secondary school, Class A has 20 students with an average height of 150 cm, while Class B has 30 students with an average height of 160 cm. If the two classes are combined, what is the mean height of all the students?
o: 156 cm
158 cm
155 cm
152 cm
questions.e: To find the combined mean, first find the total height for each class: Class A = 20 x 150 = 3000 cm, Class B = 30 x 160 = 4800 cm. Add the totals: 3000+4800 = 7800 cm. Divide by the total number of students (20+30=50): 7800/50 = 156 cm. This is a weighted mean, not a simple average of 150 and 160.
questions.p: To find di combined mean, first calculate total height for each class: Class A = 20 x 150 = 3000 cm, Class B = 30 x 160 = 4800 cm. Add dem together: 3000+4800 = 7800 cm. Divide by total number of students (20+30=50): 7800/50 = 156 cm. Na weighted mean be dis, no be simple average of 150 and 160.

questions.q: In demand theory, economists assume that all other factors affecting demand (such as income, taste and prices of related goods) remain unchanged while studying how price affects quantity demanded. This assumption is called
o: Diminishing marginal utility
Law of diminishing returns
Ceteris paribus
Opportunity cost
