questions.e: Ceteris paribus means 'other things being equal'. It allows economists to isolate the effect of price on quantity demanded by holding other determinants constant. Without this assumption, the law of demand could not be clearly stated.
questions.p: Ceteris paribus mean say 'make other things remain the same'. E dey help economist check only how price dey affect quantity wey people wan buy, while e hold other factors steady. Na dis assumption make law of demand dey clear.

questions.q: The demand function for a bag of rice in a market in Onitsha is given as Qd = 60 - 3P, where Qd is quantity demanded in bags and P is price in thousands of naira. What quantity of rice will be demanded when the price is ₦8,000 per bag?
o: 24 bags
36 bags
44 bags
52 bags
questions.e: Substitute P = 8 into Qd = 60 - 3P: Qd = 60 - (3 x 8) = 60 - 24 = 36 bags. This shows how a specific price level determines the exact quantity demanded along the demand curve.
questions.p: Put P = 8 inside Qd = 60 - 3P: Qd = 60 - (3 x 8) = 60 - 24 = 36 bags. Na so you take find the quantity wey people go demand for dat price.

questions.q: Suppose that in the same month, the average income of households in Jos rises, and at the same time the price of cooking gas (a complement to gas cookers) falls sharply. Assuming gas cookers are a normal good, what will most likely happen to the demand curve for gas cookers?
o: There will only be a movement along the same demand curve
It will shift to the right, showing an increase in demand
It will remain unchanged because the two effects cancel out
It will shift to the left, showing a decrease in demand
questions.e: A rise in income increases demand for a normal good, shifting its demand curve rightward. A fall in the price of a complement (cooking gas) also increases demand for gas cookers, shifting the curve further right. Since both forces push in the same direction, the demand curve for gas cookers shifts right, not left or unchanged.
questions.p: When income increase, people go wan buy more normal good like gas cooker, so demand curve go shift go right. Wen price of cooking gas (wey be complement) also drop, e go still make people buy more gas cooker, so curve go shift right again. Since both factors dey push same direction, the demand curve go shift right, e no go cancel out or just move along same curve.

questions.q: A farmer in Benue State lists factors that can affect how much yam he is willing to supply to the market. Which of the following is NOT normally regarded as a determinant of supply of yam?
o: The level of farming technology available to the farmer
The cost of fertilizer and labour used in yam farming
The price of yam itself
The income level of consumers who buy yam
questions.e: Supply depends on price of the good, cost of production and technology, among others. Consumer income affects how much buyers want to buy (demand), not how much sellers want to supply.
questions.p: Supply dey depend on price, cost of production and technology. Consumer income na demand factor, e no dey directly affect how much the farmer go supply.

questions.q: The supply function for crates of eggs in Oja-Oba market is given as Qs = 40 + 5P, where P is the price in naira per crate and Qs is the quantity supplied in crates. If the price of a crate of eggs is ₦30, what is the quantity supplied?
o: 190 crates
200 crates
70 crates
150 crates
questions.e: Substitute P = 30 into Qs = 40 + 5P: Qs = 40 + 5(30) = 40 + 150 = 190. So 190 crates are supplied at that price.
questions.p: Put P = 30 enter the equation Qs = 40 + 5P: Qs = 40 + 150 = 190. So na 190 crates dem go supply.

questions.q: The Federal Government introduces a new per-unit tax that producers of bottled water must pay on every unit produced, while the market price of bottled water remains unchanged. What is the most likely effect on the supply curve of bottled water?
o: The supply curve remains exactly where it was before the tax
There is a movement upward along the existing supply curve
The supply curve shifts to the left because production costs have risen
The supply curve shifts to the right because production has increased
questions.e: A per-unit tax raises the cost of producing each unit regardless of price, so producers are willing to supply less at every price. This is a decrease in supply, shown as a leftward shift of the whole curve, not just a movement along it.
questions.p: Wen gov put tax for every unit wey dem produce, e dey make production cost go up for every price level. So producers go wan supply less for every price, and dat one na leftward shift, no be just movement for the same curve.

questions.q: In a certain market in Onitsha, the demand function for a bag of rice is Qd = 80 - 4P, while the supply function is Qs = -10 + 6P, where Q is quantity in bags and P is price in thousands of naira. What is the equilibrium quantity of rice bags?
o: 44 bags
40 bags
50 bags
36 bags
questions.e: At equilibrium, Qd = Qs, so 80 - 4P = -10 + 6P. Solving gives 90 = 10P, so P = 9. Substitute P = 9 into either equation: Q = 80 - 4(9) = 80 - 36 = 44 bags.
questions.p: For equilibrium, Qd must equal Qs, so 80 - 4P = -10 + 6P. If you solve am, 90 = 10P, P = 9. Put P = 9 back inside any equation, Q = 80 - 36 = 44 bags.

questions.q: In a local market for yam tubers, the demand function is Qd = 100 - 2P and the supply function is Qs = -20 + 3P, where P is price in naira per tuber. Equilibrium price is ₦24 and equilibrium quantity is 52 tubers. If the government fixes a minimum price of ₦30 per tuber to protect yam farmers, what will be the size of the resulting surplus?
o: 20 tubers
10 tubers
40 tubers
30 tubers
questions.e: At P = 30, Qd = 100 - 2(30) = 40, and Qs = -20 + 3(30) = 70. Since the price floor is above equilibrium, suppliers want to sell more than buyers want to buy, creating a surplus = Qs - Qd = 70 - 40 = 30 tubers.
questions.p: When P = 30, Qd = 100 - 60 = 40, and Qs = -20 + 90 = 70. Since minimum price pass equilibrium price, farmers go wan sell pass wetin people wan buy, so surplus = 70 - 40 = 30 tubers.

questions.q: The price of a cup of beans in Kano market falls from ₦200 to ₦160, and as a result, the quantity demanded rises from 50 cups to 70 cups per day. Using the midpoint (arc) method, calculate the price elasticity of demand (ignore the negative sign) and state the type of elasticity it represents.
o: 0.67, inelastic demand
1.5, elastic demand
2.0, elastic demand
1.0, unit elastic demand
questions.e: Percentage change in quantity = (70-50)/((70+50)/2) = 20/60 = 0.333. Percentage change in price = (160-200)/((160+200)/2) = -40/180 = -0.222. Dividing gives elasticity = 0.333/0.222 = 1.5, which is greater than 1, so demand is elastic.
questions.p: Change for quantity = (70-50)/((70+50)/2) = 20/60 = 0.333. Change for price = (160-200)/((160+200)/2) = -40/180 = -0.222. If you divide, elasticity = 0.333/0.222 = 1.5, and since e pass 1, e mean say demand elastic.

questions.q: In economics, the payment made to the factor of production known as land (natural resources) for its contribution to the production process is called
o: Interest
Wages
Rent
Profit
questions.e: Land is the natural factor of production, and the income it earns is called rent. Wages go to labour, interest to capital, and profit to the entrepreneur.
questions.p: Land na the natural resource wey dem dey use for production, and the money wey e dey earn na rent. Wages na for labour, interest na for capital, profit na for entrepreneur.

questions.q: A furniture workshop in Owerri employs 6 carpenters who together produce 180 chairs in one week. Assuming all carpenters are equally skilled, what is the average product per carpenter for the week?
o: 25 chairs
20 chairs
30 chairs
36 chairs
questions.e: Average product = Total product divided by number of workers = 180 chairs divided by 6 carpenters = 30 chairs per carpenter.
questions.p: Average product na total output divide by number of workers: 180 chairs divide by 6 carpenters = 30 chairs per carpenter.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes variable cost of production in a firm, such as a bakery in Jos that buys flour and sugar?
o: A cost that changes directly as the level of output changes
A cost that stays the same no matter how much is produced
A cost that is spread evenly and never changes per unit
A cost that is paid only when the firm closes down completely
questions.e: Variable cost is the cost that rises or falls with the quantity produced, such as raw materials. Fixed cost, not variable cost, stays the same regardless of output.
questions.p: Variable cost na the one wey go up or down as the output change, like raw materials wey dem dey buy. Na fixed cost dey stay same no matter the output.

questions.q: A furniture maker in Benin City produces wooden chairs. When output increases from 40 chairs to 41 chairs, total cost rises from ₦82,000 to ₦84,500. What is the marginal cost of producing the 41st chair?
questions.e: Marginal cost is the change in total cost divided by the change in quantity. Here, (₦84,500 - ₦82,000) / (41 - 40) = ₦2,500.
questions.p: Marginal cost na the change for total cost divide by the change for quantity. So (₦84,500 - ₦82,000) / 1 = ₦2,500.

questions.q: A cassava processing firm in Enugu has a total fixed cost of ₦45,000, which does not change with the level of output. At what level of output will the firm's average fixed cost (AFC) equal exactly ₦150 per unit?
o: 450 units
300 units
150 units
600 units
questions.e: Average fixed cost is total fixed cost divided by quantity, so AFC = TFC/Q. Setting 150 = 45,000/Q and solving gives Q = 45,000/150 = 300 units.
questions.p: Average fixed cost na total fixed cost divide by quantity, so AFC = TFC/Q. If we put 150 = 45,000/Q, we go solve am make Q = 45,000/150 = 300 units.

questions.q: Which of the following is a distinguishing structural feature of a monopoly market, as opposed to perfect competition?
o: Firms are price takers with no control over price
Entry and exit of firms are completely free
There are many firms producing identical products
There is only one firm in the industry producing a product with no close substitute
questions.e: A monopoly exists when a single firm controls the entire supply of a product that has no close substitute, and entry is usually blocked. This is different from perfect competition, where many firms sell identical goods and entry is free.
questions.p: Monopoly na when one company dey control the whole market and nobody fit easily enter the business, plus the product no get close substitute. For perfect competition, na plenty companies dey sell the same type of goods and anybody fit enter.

questions.q: A perfectly competitive firm in Kano sells groundnut oil at the prevailing market price of ₦100 per unit. Its total cost function is TC = 20Q + 2Q^2, where Q is the quantity produced per day. What output level maximizes the firm's profit?
o: 15 units
20 units
25 units
10 units
questions.e: Under perfect competition, profit is maximized where Marginal Cost (MC) equals Price (since P = MR). MC = d(TC)/dQ = 20 + 4Q. Setting 20 + 4Q = 100 gives 4Q = 80, so Q = 20 units.
questions.p: For perfect competition, profit dey maximum when Marginal Cost (MC) equal Price. MC = 20 + 4Q, so if you set am equal to 100, 4Q go be 80, and Q go be 20 units.

questions.q: In Nigeria's cement industry, suppose four leading firms control the following percentages of total market sales: Firm A, 40%; Firm B, 25%; Firm C, 20%; Firm D, 10%, while many small firms share the remaining 5%. What is the four-firm concentration ratio (CR4) of this market, and what type of market structure does this ratio suggest?
o: CR4 = 95%, indicating an oligopoly
CR4 = 100%, indicating a monopoly
CR4 = 85%, indicating an oligopoly
CR4 = 90%, indicating perfect competition
questions.e: The four-firm concentration ratio is found by adding the market shares of the four largest firms: 40% + 25% + 20% + 10% = 95%. A CR4 this high (close to total market control by a few firms) is typical of an oligopoly, not perfect competition or pure monopoly.
questions.p: To find CR4, you just add the market share of the four biggest companies: 40% + 25% + 20% + 10% = 95%. Since few companies dey control almost everything, na oligopoly be dis, no be perfect competition or pure monopoly.

questions.q: Which of the following statements best defines Gross Domestic Product (GDP)?
o: The total income received by a country's citizens after deducting taxes and adding subsidies
The total market value of all final goods and services produced within a country after deducting depreciation of capital
The total market value of all final goods and services produced within the geographical boundaries of a country in a given year, regardless of the nationality of the producers
The total market value of all final goods and services produced by the citizens of a country, whether at home or abroad, in a given year
questions.e: GDP measures the total value of final goods and services produced within a country's borders in a year, no matter who produced them (citizens or foreigners). The other options describe GNP, NNP, and disposable income instead of GDP.
questions.p: GDP na di total value of all final goods and services wey dem produce inside one country border for one year, no matter who produce am (citizen or foreigner). The other options dey describe GNP, NNP or disposable income instead.

questions.q: In a given year, Nigeria's GDP was ₦500 billion. The net factor income from abroad was negative ₦20 billion, meaning foreigners earned more income from activities in Nigeria than Nigerians earned abroad. If capital depreciation for the year was ₦40 billion, what was the Net National Product (NNP) for that year?
o: ₦520 billion
₦480 billion
₦440 billion
₦460 billion
questions.e: First find GNP = GDP + net factor income from abroad = 500 + (-20) = ₦480 billion. Then NNP = GNP - depreciation = 480 - 40 = ₦440 billion.
questions.p: First find GNP = GDP + net factor income from abroad = 500 + (-20) = 480 billion naira. Then minus depreciation make e be NNP = 480 - 40 = 440 billion naira.

questions.q: An economics teacher in Kaduna told her students that when national income is correctly computed using the output, income, and expenditure methods, all three approaches should give the same total value for a given year. Which of the following best explains why this equality holds?
o: Because indirect taxes are automatically added to all three methods before final computation
Because what is spent by one group of economic agents becomes income to another group, which in turn equals the value of output produced
Because national income statisticians always round off figures to the nearest billion naira
Because government deliberately adjusts the three figures to match international standards
questions.e: National income flows in a circle: firms produce output, which is sold for money (expenditure), and that money becomes income for workers and resource owners (income). Because of this circular flow, the output, income, and expenditure methods should, in theory, all add up to the same total.
questions.p: National income dey flow like circle: company produce output, dem sell am for money (expenditure), and dat money come become income for worker and resource owner (income). Because of dis circle flow, output, income and expenditure method suppose give the same total value.

questions.q: Chief Nwosu sold his yams and kept part of the proceeds in a savings account so that he could use the money to pay his daughter's school fees two years later. This use of money is best described as money performing the function of a:
o: Unit of account
Medium of exchange
Standard of deferred payment
Store of value
questions.e: Money acts as a store of value when it is kept aside to be used for spending in the future without losing (much) of its usefulness. Chief Nwosu is saving the money to use later, so this is the store of value function, not buying something now (medium of exchange) or pricing goods (unit of account).
questions.p: Money dey work as store of value when person keep am well-well to use am later, no be to buy something now-now. Since Chief Nwosu kon save the money make e use am two years later, na store of value be dis, no be unit of account or medium of exchange.

questions.q: In an economy, the total money supply is ₦200,000,000 and the velocity of circulation of money is 5. If the total output of goods and services produced in the economy is 2,500,000 units, use the Quantity Theory of Money (MV = PQ) to find the average price level per unit.
questions.e: Using MV = PQ, P = MV/Q = (200,000,000 x 5) / 2,500,000 = 1,000,000,000 / 2,500,000 = ₦400. This is the only value that satisfies the equation with the given figures.
questions.p: Dem use MV=PQ formula: P = MV/Q = (200,000,000 x 5) / 2,500,000 = ₦400. Na di correct answer wey match di figures wey dem give.

questions.q: A commercial bank in Lagos offers a nominal interest rate of 15 percent per annum on fixed deposits, while the prevailing inflation rate in the economy is 9 percent per annum. Using the simple Fisher relationship (Nominal rate = Real rate + Inflation rate), what is the approximate real interest rate earned by a depositor?
questions.e: From the Fisher equation, Real rate = Nominal rate - Inflation rate = 15% - 9% = 6%. This shows the true increase in the depositor's purchasing power after accounting for inflation, which is lower than the nominal rate quoted by the bank.
questions.p: From Fisher equation, Real rate = Nominal rate minus Inflation rate = 15% - 9% = 6%. Na dis one show di real power wey depositor get after dem remove inflation, e dey smaller pass di nominal rate wey bank talk.

questions.q: Which of the following is a money market instrument commonly used by the Nigerian government to raise short-term funds?
o: Debentures
Ordinary shares
Preference shares
Treasury bills
questions.e: Treasury bills are short-term debt securities issued by government and traded in the money market. Debentures, ordinary shares and preference shares are long-term securities traded in the capital market.
questions.p: Treasury bills na short-term paper wey government dey issue for money market. Debentures, ordinary shares and preference shares na long-term things wey dem dey trade for capital market.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes how commercial banks create credit in an economy?
o: Banks lend out a fraction of their deposits while keeping the rest as reserve, thereby expanding the total money supply
Banks print new currency notes to meet customer withdrawal demand
Banks transfer all customer deposits to the Central Bank for safekeeping
Banks exchange foreign currency for local currency on behalf of customers
questions.e: Commercial banks keep only a small fraction of deposits as reserve and lend out the rest. As this lent money is redeposited and relent, the total money supply in the economy expands, a process called credit creation.
questions.p: Commercial banks go keep small part of the money as reserve, then dem go loan out the rest. As dis money dey enter and comot again, e dey increase the total money wey dey circulate - na so credit creation dey work.

questions.q: Public debt can be classified based on the source of borrowing. Which of the following best describes an external public debt?
o: Money borrowed from citizens through the sale of treasury bills
Money owed by government to local contractors for completed projects
Money borrowed from foreign governments and international financial institutions such as the World Bank
Money borrowed by government from the Central Bank of Nigeria
questions.e: External debt is money a government owes to lenders outside the country, such as foreign governments or bodies like the World Bank. Internal debt, on the other hand, is owed to lenders within the country, such as citizens or the central bank.
questions.p: External debt na money wey government borrow from outside country, like foreign government or World Bank. Internal debt na money wey government borrow from inside the country, like citizens or CBN.

questions.q: Mallam Sule's taxable annual income is ₦3,200,000. Under a progressive tax system, the first ₦800,000 of taxable income is taxed at 7%, the next ₦1,000,000 is taxed at 11%, and any amount above ₦1,800,000 is taxed at 15%. Calculate Mallam Sule's total tax payable for the year.
questions.p: Step by step: first 800k dem tax 7% e give 56,000. Next 1,000,000 dem tax 11% e give 110,000. Wetin remain na 1,400,000 (3,200,000 minus 1,800,000), dem tax am 15% e give 210,000. If you add everything you go get 376,000.

questions.q: In a particular fiscal year, the Federal Government of Nigeria budgeted total expenditure of ₦61 billion while total revenue collected was ₦45 billion. To finance the shortfall, the government obtained a loan of ₦10 billion from a development bank, and the remaining balance was financed by drawing down its reserves. How much was drawn from the reserves?
o: ₦16 billion
₦6 billion
₦10 billion
₦4 billion
questions.e: Budget deficit = expenditure - revenue = 61 - 45 = 16 billion. The loan already covers 10 billion of this deficit, so the amount drawn from reserves = 16 - 10 = 6 billion.
questions.p: Budget deficit na wetin dem spend minus wetin dem collect: 61-45=16 billion. Dem don already get loan of 10 billion, so wetin remain wey go come from reserves na 16-10=6 billion.

questions.q: According to Rostow's stages of economic growth theory, which stage describes a society that still depends mainly on traditional methods of farming and production, with low savings and little technological change, and has not yet begun the process of self-sustained growth?
o: Age of high mass consumption
Drive to maturity stage
Take-off stage
Traditional society stage
questions.e: Rostow described the traditional society stage as one where output is limited by old farming methods, low savings, and little science or technology. This is the first and most basic stage before any serious growth begins.
questions.p: Rostow talk say for traditional society stage, people dey use old farming way, savings dey small, and dem never start real growth. Na the first and most basic stage before any serious change.

questions.q: Last year, a certain West African country's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) was ₦120 trillion. This year, it rose to ₦126 trillion. What is the country's economic growth rate for the year?
questions.e: Growth rate = (New GDP - Old GDP) / Old GDP x 100. That is (126 - 120)/120 x 100 = 6/120 x 100 = 5%. So the economy grew by 5% that year.
questions.p: Growth rate = (New GDP - Old GDP) divide by Old GDP, times 100. So na (126-120)/120 x 100 = 5%. The economy grow by 5% for that year.

questions.q: In Nigeria, 'mixed farming' is best described as a system in which a farmer
o: practises only animal husbandry on a ranch
cultivates crops and rears livestock together on the same farm
grows only tree crops for export
plants a single crop across several hectares of land
questions.e: Mixed farming means combining crop production with livestock rearing on the same farm. This helps the farmer use resources like manure and crop residue efficiently. It is common among small-scale farmers in Nigeria.
questions.p: Mixed farming na when farmer dey plant crops and still dey rear animals for the same farm. E help farmer use manure and leftover crops well well. Na common practice for Nigeria small farmers.

questions.q: In a certain year, Nigeria's total Gross Domestic Product (GDP) was valued at ₦200 billion, while the agricultural sector contributed ₦50 billion to this total. What percentage of the GDP did agriculture contribute that year?
questions.e: Percentage contribution = (Agricultural output / Total GDP) x 100 = (50/200) x 100 = 25%. This shows how economists measure a sector's share of national output.
questions.p: Percentage wey agriculture contribute = (50/200) x 100 = 25%. Na so dem dey calculate how much one sector dey contribute to total GDP.

questions.q: Large-scale rural-urban migration of young, able-bodied men in search of white-collar jobs has been a persistent feature of the Nigerian economy. What is the most likely direct economic consequence of this trend on commercial crop farming in rural areas?
o: A rise in the cost of farm labour due to reduced supply of workers
A fall in the cost of farm labour due to oversupply of workers
An automatic increase in farm mechanization funded by migrants
A reduction in the demand for food in urban markets
questions.e: When young workers leave rural areas, the supply of farm labour falls while demand for labour on farms stays roughly the same. By basic supply and demand reasoning, a fall in supply with steady demand pushes up the price (wage) of farm labour, raising production costs for farmers.
questions.p: When young people dey comot from village go city, the number of people wey dey available to work for farm dey reduce. Demand for farm labour no change reach like that, so wetin dey happen be say cost of hiring farm workers go rise, and e go cost farmer more money.

questions.q: Mama Ngozi's bakery buys flour, sugar and other light ingredients, but the baked bread that comes out is bulkier and heavier to transport in large quantities to many customers across town. Based on the theory of industrial location, where would such a bakery most likely be sited to reduce cost?
o: Close to the sugar plantation
Close to the river that supplies water for baking
Close to the flour mill that supplies raw flour
Close to the market where the bread will be sold
questions.e: Industries whose finished products are bulkier or heavier than their raw materials are called weight-gaining industries. They are usually sited near the market to reduce the cost of transporting the heavier finished goods. Bread baking is a good example of this.
questions.p: Industry wey dem dey call weight-gaining dey make product wey heavy pass di raw materials. Dem go rather build near market so dem no go waste money to carry heavy bread go far. Na why bakery dey near market pass raw material source.

questions.q: When a limited liability company is being registered in Nigeria, the document that spells out the internal rules of the company, including how directors are appointed, how meetings are conducted and the rights of shareholders, is known as the:
o: Memorandum of Association
Articles of Association
Certificate of Incorporation
Prospectus
questions.e: The Memorandum of Association defines the company's relationship with the outside world, such as its name, objectives and capital. The Articles of Association, on the other hand, contain the internal rules guiding how the company is run, including directors' duties and shareholders' rights. This makes option B the correct answer.
questions.p: Memorandum of Association dey show how company relate with outside world, like im name and wetin e wan do. Articles of Association na di one wey get di inside rules like how directors go work and how shareholders go get their rights. So na Articles of Association be di answer.

questions.q: A soft-drink company uses large quantities of water (which is heavy and bulky) to produce its finished bottled drinks, which are even heavier and bulkier than the water and sugar used to make them. Applying the principle of weight-gaining and weight-losing industries to decide factory location, where should this company most likely site its bottling plant?
o: Near the market where the drinks will be sold
Near the source of sugar used in production
Near the seaport where sugar is imported
Exactly halfway between the sugar source and the market
questions.e: Because the finished bottled drinks are heavier and bulkier than the raw materials, this is a weight-gaining industry. Weight-gaining industries locate near the market to avoid the high cost of transporting the heavier finished product over long distances. Locating near raw materials or midway would increase transport cost for the bulkier final goods.
questions.p: Since di finished drinks dey heavier pass di raw materials wey dem use make am, na weight-gaining industry be dis. Weight-gaining industries dey site near market so dem no go spend plenty money to carry di heavy finished product go far. If dem build am near sugar source or for middle, e go cost more to transport di heavier product.

questions.q: In which decade did crude oil overtake agricultural products (like cocoa and groundnut) as Nigeria's leading foreign exchange earner?
questions.e: After the Nigerian Civil War, the oil boom of the 1970s pushed crude oil export earnings far above those from agriculture. Before this, agriculture (cocoa, groundnut, palm produce) was Nigeria's main foreign exchange source.
questions.p: After di civil war, na for 1970s crude oil begin bring plenty money pass agriculture. Before that time na agriculture (cocoa, groundnut) dey bring the main foreign exchange.

questions.q: When a country's heavy reliance on crude oil exports causes its currency to appreciate, making other export goods like cocoa or textiles too expensive for foreign buyers, this economic phenomenon is best described as
o: Balance of payments surplus
Import substitution
Dutch Disease
Terms of trade deterioration
questions.e: Dutch Disease occurs when a booming resource sector (like oil) causes currency appreciation, which then hurts other export sectors by making them less price-competitive abroad. This weakens diversification of the economy away from oil.
questions.p: Dutch Disease na wetin dey happen when oil money make naira strong, so e make other exports like cocoa cost too much for foreign buyers. Dis one dey make am hard for economy to depend on something apart from oil.

questions.q: In population studies, what name is given to the official, periodic, and systematic process of counting every person in a country, usually recording details such as age, sex, and occupation, at a specific point in time?
o: Population projection
Census
Sample survey
Vital registration
questions.e: A census is the complete count of all persons in a country at a particular time, including details like age, sex and occupation. A sample survey only covers part of the population, while vital registration tracks births/deaths continuously, not a one-time count.
questions.p: Census na di full and official count of everybody for one kontri, dem go record di age, sex and wetin dem dey do. Sample survey no cover everybody, and vital registration na continuous recording, e no be one-time full count.

questions.q: A town in Delta State has a total population of 80,000. Out of this, 20,000 are children aged 0-14 years and 10,000 are elderly persons aged 65 years and above. The remaining people make up the working-age population. What is the dependency ratio of the town, expressed as a percentage?
questions.e: Working-age population = 80,000 - 20,000 - 10,000 = 50,000. Dependency ratio = (children + elderly) / working-age population x 100 = (20,000 + 10,000) / 50,000 x 100 = 60%. This shows that for every 100 working people, there are 60 dependants to support.
questions.p: Working-age people = 80,000 minus 20,000 minus 10,000 = 50,000. Dependency ratio = (children + old people) divide working-age, multiply by 100 = 30,000/50,000 x 100 = 60%. So na 60 dependants for every 100 working people.

questions.q: A developing country's population is growing at a constant annual rate of 2.5%. Using the simple 'Rule of 70' (Doubling time = 70 / annual growth rate), approximately how many years will it take for the country's population to double in size?
o: 14 years
28 years
35 years
20 years
questions.e: Using the Rule of 70: Doubling time = 70 / 2.5 = 28 years. This rule gives a quick estimate of how long a growing quantity, like population, takes to double at a given constant percentage growth rate. A higher growth rate always means a shorter doubling time.
questions.p: Dem dey use Rule of 70: Doubling time = 70 divide by 2.5 = 28 years. Dis rule na fast way to sabi how long population go take double if di growth rate no change. If growth rate high pass, e go take shorter time to double.

questions.q: In the study of international trade, which statement correctly describes an IMPROVEMENT in a country's terms of trade?
o: The volume of exports falls while the volume of imports rises
The index of import prices rises faster than the index of export prices
The index of export prices rises faster than the index of import prices
Export prices and import prices rise at exactly the same rate
questions.e: Terms of trade compares how fast export prices change relative to import prices. If export prices rise faster than import prices, a country earns more for each unit it sells abroad compared with what it pays for imports, which is an improvement.
questions.p: Terms of trade na how export price dey move compare to import price. If export price dey rise pass import price, kontri go dey gain more for wetin e dey sell compare to wetin e dey buy, so e don improve.

questions.q: A country's export price index is 150 and its import price index is 120, using the same base year of 100. Calculate the country's terms of trade index.
questions.e: Terms of trade index = (Export price index / Import price index) x 100 = (150/120) x 100 = 125. A value above 100 shows the terms of trade are favourable, since export prices have risen more than import prices.
questions.p: Terms of trade = (Export price index divide Import price index) times 100 = (150/120) x 100 = 125. Since e pass 100, e mean say the terms of trade favour the kontri well well.

questions.q: Using 1 unit of labour-time, Country Dara can produce either 1 bag of cloth (using 5 hours) or 1 pair of shoes (using 10 hours). Country Kowa can produce either 1 bag of cloth (using 8 hours) or 1 pair of shoes (using 20 hours). Based on the principle of comparative advantage, which country should specialise in producing shoes?
o: Country Dara, because its opportunity cost of shoes (2 bags of cloth) is lower than Country Kowa's (2.5 bags of cloth)
Country Kowa, because it uses more hours to make shoes, showing greater effort and skill
Both countries equally, since they both take longer to make shoes than cloth
Neither country, because Country Dara is more efficient at making both goods
questions.e: Opportunity cost of 1 pair of shoes in Dara = 10 hours / 5 hours per cloth = 2 bags of cloth. In Kowa, it is 20/8 = 2.5 bags of cloth. Since Dara gives up less cloth to make shoes, Dara has the comparative advantage in shoes, even though Dara is also better at cloth (absolute advantage does not decide specialisation, comparative advantage does).
questions.p: Opportunity cost of one shoe for Dara na 10/5 = 2 bags of cloth, but for Kowa na 20/8 = 2.5 bags of cloth. Since Dara dey sacrifice less cloth make e produce shoe, Dara get comparative advantage for shoe, even though Dara sabi make both goods pass Kowa overall.

questions.q: The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) was formally established in 1975 by the Treaty of Lagos. In which city is the ECOWAS Commission (headquarters) currently located?
o: Accra, Ghana
Abuja, Nigeria
Lome, Togo
Dakar, Senegal
questions.e: ECOWAS was founded in Lagos in 1975, but its permanent headquarters (the ECOWAS Commission) is sited in Abuja, Nigeria. The other cities host other regional bodies or were just meeting venues, not the headquarters.
questions.p: Dem form ECOWAS for Lagos for 1975, but di main headquarters (ECOWAS Commission) dey Abuja, Nigeria. Di oda cities no be where di headquarters dey.

questions.q: The World Bank Group has several affiliate institutions with different functions. Which of these institutions specifically provides interest-free loans and grants to the world's poorest developing countries to support social and economic development?
o: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA)
International Finance Corporation (IFC)
International Development Association (IDA)
questions.e: The IDA is the arm of the World Bank Group that gives interest-free (concessional) loans and grants to the poorest countries. IFC deals with private sector investment, MIGA provides investment insurance, and the IMF is a separate institution dealing with balance of payments issues, not a World Bank affiliate.
questions.p: IDA na di World Bank arm wey dey give free-interest loan and grant to di poorest kontries. IFC dey support private business, MIGA dey insure investment, and IMF na separate body wey dey handle balance of payment wahala.

questions.q: A developing country's currency has depreciated sharply, causing severe balance of payments difficulties. The government approaches the International Monetary Fund (IMF) for emergency financial assistance. Based on typical IMF loan conditionalities designed to restore macroeconomic stability, which policy package would the country most likely be required to adopt?
o: Reduce government spending and allow further currency adjustment to restore competitiveness
Raise import tariffs sharply to protect local industries from foreign competition
Increase fuel and electricity subsidies to protect citizens from hardship
Nationalise all commercial banks to directly control the money supply
questions.e: IMF conditionalities typically require fiscal discipline (cutting government spending/subsidies) and market-driven exchange rate adjustment to correct balance of payments problems. Increasing subsidies, raising tariffs, or nationalising banks would worsen fiscal deficits or distort markets, which goes against IMF's standard stabilisation approach.
questions.p: IMF dey ask kontri to cut government spending and allow di currency adjust well-well so dem fit become competitive again. To increase subsidy, raise tariff, or nationalise banks go only make di budget wahala and market problem worse, na im be why dem no go gree am.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes 'collective bargaining' in the labour market?
o: Negotiation between trade union representatives and employers over wages and working conditions
Individual workers bargaining alone with their employer for higher pay
Government fixing wages without consulting employers or workers
Workers forming cooperative societies to produce and sell goods
questions.e: Collective bargaining means trade union leaders negotiate as a group with employers on behalf of all workers, covering issues like wages and conditions of service. This gives workers stronger bargaining power than if they negotiated alone. Options B, C and D describe different, unrelated actions.
questions.p: Collective bargaining na when union leaders dey negotiate as one group with employer about wages and work condition. E dey give workers better power pass if everybody dey negotiate alone. The other options no match this definition.

questions.q: A textile factory in Aba employs 150 workers at a daily wage of ₦2,500 each. After successful negotiation by the workers' trade union, the daily wage rate is increased by 20%. What is the new total daily wage bill of the factory?
questions.e: New wage = 2,500 + (20% of 2,500) = 2,500 + 500 = ₦3,000 per worker. Total wage bill = 150 workers x ₦3,000 = ₦450,000. The other options either use the old wage or wrong percentage increase.
questions.p: New wage be 2,500 add 20% of am (500), e give 3,000 per worker. Multiply am by 150 workers e give ₦450,000. Other options na wrong calculation or dem use old wage.

questions.q: In a hypothetical labour market, the demand for labour is given by Ld = 800 - 2W, and the supply of labour is given by Ls = -100 + 3W, where W is the daily wage rate in Naira and L is the number of workers. If government fixes a minimum wage of ₦200 per day, which is above the market equilibrium wage, how many workers will be unemployed (excess supply) at this wage?
o: 60 workers
100 workers
300 workers
40 workers
questions.e: At W=200: Ld = 800 - 2(200) = 400, and Ls = -100 + 3(200) = 500. Since supply exceeds demand, unemployment = Ls - Ld = 500 - 400 = 100 workers. This shows how a minimum wage set above equilibrium creates a labour surplus.
questions.p: When W=200: Ld = 800-400=400, Ls = -100+600=500. Since supply pass demand, unemployment = 500-400 = 100 workers. Na so minimum wage wey dey above equilibrium dey cause excess labour.

questions.q: Which of the following arises directly because resources are limited while human wants are unlimited?
o: Specialisation
Taxation
Inflation
Scarcity
questions.e: Scarcity is the direct result of limited resources facing unlimited human wants. It is the root cause of all economic problems.
questions.p: Scarcity na when money or resource small but wetin human beings want plenty pass. Na im cause all di wahala for economics.

questions.q: Tunde has ₦3,000 and lists his wants as: phone recharge card, lunch, a novel, and a haircut, in that order of urgency. If he spends the money starting from the top of the list until it finishes, this arrangement of wants is best described as his:
o: Production possibility
Indifference map
Budget line
Scale of preference
questions.e: Arranging wants in order of importance so the most pressing ones are satisfied first is called a scale of preference. It helps a consumer with limited income decide what to buy first.
questions.p: E arrange im wants starting from di one wey dey pain am pass down to di least one, na wet fibromyalgia dem dey call scale of preference. E dey help person use small money buy di most important things first.

questions.q: A farmer in Benue State has one plot of land which he can use either to plant yam alone, maize alone, or a combination of both. This situation, where resources can be used for alternative purposes, illustrates the problem of:
o: Division of labour
Scarcity only
Economic growth
Choice
questions.e: When a resource has alternative uses, the farmer must choose how to allocate it among competing purposes. This decision-making process is what economists call choice.
questions.p: When one thing fit do different work, person must choose how to use am. Dis kind decision na wet dem dey call choice.

questions.q: Kelechi can use his free afternoon to either repair his bicycle (which he values at ₦1,200) or wash his neighbour's car for ₦2,000, or tutor a student for ₦1,800. If he chooses to tutor the student, what is his opportunity cost?
o: ₦1,800, the value of tutoring
₦3,200, the sum of the two forgone options
₦2,000, the value of washing the car
₦1,200, the value of repairing his bicycle
questions.e: Opportunity cost is the value of the best alternative forgone, not all alternatives added together. Since washing the car (₦2,000) is more valuable than bicycle repair, it is the true opportunity cost of tutoring.
questions.p: Opportunity cost na di value of di best alternative wey person leave. Since to wash neighbour car give ₦2,000 wey high pass, na im be di true opportunity cost.

questions.q: Which of the following situations best illustrates the economic problem of choice arising from scarcity?
o: A trader having limited capital and deciding whether to stock rice or beans for sale
A government building more roads than it needs
A student having enough money to buy all the textbooks on her list
A company producing goods that nobody wants to buy
questions.e: Choice arises when limited resources force a decision among competing alternatives. The trader with limited capital must decide between stocking rice or beans, which is a true scarcity-driven choice.
questions.p: Choice dey happen when small resource make person must select wetin to do. Di trader wey get small money and dey choose whether to buy rice or beans na correct example.

questions.q: A furniture maker in Aba can produce either 20 chairs or 8 tables in a week using the same materials and labour. If he decides to produce 5 tables instead of 8, assuming a straight-line trade-off, what is the opportunity cost, in chairs, of producing those 5 tables?
o: 8 chairs
20 chairs
5 chairs
12.5 chairs
questions.e: Each table costs 20/8 = 2.5 chairs in production. Producing 5 tables therefore costs 5 times 2.5, which equals 12.5 chairs.
questions.p: If one table cost 2.5 chairs, to produce 5 tables mean say you go multiply 5 by 2.5, wey give you 12.5 chairs.

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes scarcity from the economic concept of choice?
o: Scarcity means resources are insufficient, while choice is the act of selecting among alternatives created by that insufficiency
Scarcity refers to unlimited wants, while choice refers to limited resources
Scarcity and choice mean exactly the same thing in Economics
Scarcity only affects poor nations, while choice only affects rich nations
questions.e: Scarcity is the condition of limited resources relative to unlimited wants, and it is this condition that forces choice. Choice is the response or decision-making process that scarcity makes necessary.
questions.p: Scarcity mean say things no enough, while choice na di decision wey person make to select one out of di ones wey dey.

questions.q: A tailor in Onitsha can use one day to sew either 5 native wears or 3 gowns, since both use the same cloth and machine time. If he decides to sew only gowns for the day, what is his opportunity cost?
o: 3 gowns
8 native wears and gowns combined
The cost of cloth only
5 native wears
questions.e: Opportunity cost is the next best alternative given up. Since he chose gowns, what he sacrificed is the 5 native wears he could have sewn instead.
questions.p: Opportunity cost na di next best thing wey person leave. Since di tailor choose gowns, e sacrifice di 5 native wears wey e for fit sew.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why opportunity cost would NOT exist in an economy without scarcity?
o: Without scarcity, prices of goods would simply fall to zero everywhere
Without scarcity, production would increase but opportunity cost would stay constant
Without scarcity, all resources would be free goods and choices would not involve giving up alternatives
Without scarcity, consumers would still rank their wants but choice would remain difficult
questions.e: Opportunity cost only arises because resources are limited, forcing a sacrifice when a choice is made. If nothing were scarce, every want could be satisfied without giving up any other want.
questions.p: Opportunity cost dey happen because resources no reach. If everything plenty for ground, we no go need sacrifice one thing to get anoda.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most important factor that forces every household, firm and government to make economic choices?
o: The existence of money as a medium of exchange
The presence of competition among sellers in the market
The unlimited nature of human wants compared with limited resources
The desire of producers to maximize profit
questions.e: Choice becomes necessary because human wants are unlimited while the resources available to satisfy them are limited. This mismatch, called scarcity, is the root cause of all economic choices.
questions.p: Choice dey necessary because human wants plenty pass di resources wey we get. Dis scarcity na di main reason why we must dey choose wetin we want.

questions.q: A small-scale fish farmer in Delta State has 100 fingerlings and a pond that can hold either catfish alone, yielding ₦80,000 profit, or tilapia alone, yielding ₦95,000 profit, or a mix of both, yielding ₦70,000 profit. If he decides to go for the mixed option because he wants to reduce risk, what is his opportunity cost?
questions.e: Opportunity cost is the value of the best alternative forgone. Since tilapia alone would have given the highest profit of ₦95,000, that is what he sacrifices by choosing the mixed option.
questions.p: Opportunity cost na di value of di best option wey you leave. Since tilapia for give am ₦95,000, na dat money be di cost of im choice.

questions.q: In economics, which of these best distinguishes an economic good from a free good?
o: An economic good has a price because it is scarce, while a free good has no price because it is abundant relative to demand
An economic good is produced by government while a free good is produced by private individuals
An economic good is always imported while a free good is always locally produced
An economic good is tangible while a free good is intangible
questions.e: Economic goods are limited in supply relative to human wants, so they command a price. Free goods, such as sunlight or air, are available in such abundance that no one needs to pay for them.
questions.p: Economic goods get price because dem scarce. Free goods like air plenty well-well, so nobody dey pay for dem.

questions.q: A woman weaving aso-oke in Iseyin has 6 hours of daily working time. Weaving one wrapper takes 2 hours and sells for ₦4,000, while weaving one scarf takes 1 hour and sells for ₦1,500. If she uses all 6 hours to weave only scarves instead of only wrappers, what is her opportunity cost in terms of money, assuming she sells everything she produces?
questions.e: In 6 hours she can make 3 wrappers worth 3 times ₦4,000 equals ₦12,000, or 6 scarves worth 6 times ₦1,500 equals ₦9,000. By choosing scarves, she gives up the ₦12,000 she would have earned from wrappers, which is her opportunity cost.
questions.p: If she weave wrappers, she go make ₦12,000. Because she choose scarves, she lose dat ₦12,000 wey she for make from wrappers.

questions.q: Which of the following is a basic feature that distinguishes a capitalist economy from a socialist economy?
o: Need for economic planning
Existence of consumer wants
Scarcity of resources
Freedom of private enterprise and ownership of property
questions.e: Private enterprise and private ownership of property are the hallmark of capitalism, while socialism emphasizes collective or state ownership. Scarcity and consumer wants exist under every economic system.
questions.p: Na private property and business be the main thing wey dey show say economy na capitalist. Socialism dey talk about government or collective ownership, but scarcity and consumer wants dey happen for every system.

questions.q: In a mixed economy, price control by government on essential commodities like rice and sugar is mainly intended to:
o: Eliminate the private sector completely
Protect consumers from exploitation while still allowing market forces to operate
Transfer all means of production to the state
Abolish the use of money in transactions
questions.e: A mixed economy combines market forces with government intervention. Price control protects consumers from exploitation without removing private enterprise, unlike pure socialism which nationalises production.
questions.p: Mixed economy dey mix market forces with government work. Price control dey help protect consumers from high price without stopping private business people from making profit.

questions.q: One major weakness commonly associated with a purely capitalist economic system is that it:
o: Results in wide inequality in the distribution of income and wealth
Leads to inefficient allocation of resources due to lack of competition
Removes the profit motive from business decisions
Prevents individuals from owning private property
questions.e: Because production is driven by profit and resources go to those who can pay, capitalism tends to widen the gap between the rich and the poor. The other options describe features of socialism, not capitalism.
questions.p: Because capitalism dey focus on profit, e dey make the gap between rich and poor people too wide. The other options na things wey dey happen for socialism, no be capitalism.

questions.q: A country decides that the government will own and control key sectors such as steel production and electricity generation, while individuals are allowed to freely engage in trading, tailoring, and farming for profit. This arrangement best illustrates:
o: A pure capitalist economy
A pure socialist economy
A mixed economic system
A subsistence economy
questions.e: The combination of state ownership of major industries with private individuals freely engaging in trade and farming is the defining feature of a mixed economy. Neither pure capitalism nor pure socialism allows this dual arrangement.
questions.p: If government get some big industries but people still dey do their own private business, that one na mixed economy. E no be pure capitalism or pure socialism.

questions.q: Under a free enterprise (capitalist) economy, the question of 'what to produce' is primarily determined by:
o: Rationing of goods by government agencies
A national development plan drawn up by the government
Directives issued by a central planning authority
The interaction of consumer demand and producer supply through the price mechanism
questions.e: In capitalism, the price mechanism, driven by the forces of demand and supply, signals to producers what consumers want, thereby determining what is produced. Central planning and rationing are features of socialism, not capitalism.
questions.p: For capitalist economy, na demand and supply determine wetin dem go produce through price mechanism. Government no dey use central planning or rationing to decide wetin people go buy.

questions.q: Which of these is a genuine advantage that a mixed economy has over a purely socialist economy?
o: It allows private initiative to thrive alongside government provision of essential services
It removes the need for any form of taxation
It guarantees absolutely equal income for every citizen
It completely eliminates unemployment in the economy
questions.e: A mixed economy blends private initiative, which encourages efficiency and innovation, with government provision of essential services like health and infrastructure. Pure socialism restricts private initiative, while the other options are unrealistic claims not guaranteed by any system.
questions.p: Mixed economy dey allow private people to bring new ideas and work hard, while government still dey provide important services. Pure socialism no dey allow private initiative like that.

questions.q: A government is debating whether to fully nationalise its telecommunications industry or leave it entirely to private companies. An economist advises that a middle path, where the government regulates the sector through licensing while private firms compete for customers, would better serve the economy. This advice is rooted in the principle of:
o: Command economy
Mixed economy
Pure capitalism
Subsistence economy
questions.e: Combining government regulation with private sector competition, rather than full nationalisation or pure market freedom, is the essence of a mixed economic system. This balances efficiency from competition with public oversight to prevent exploitation.
questions.p: When government regulate sector but still allow private companies to compete, that one na mixed economy. E dey balance the efficiency of market with government oversight to stop exploitation.

questions.q: Economic systems can broadly be classified into capitalism, socialism and mixed economy mainly on the basis of which criterion?
o: The level of literacy of the citizens
The size of the country's population
The ownership and control of the means of production
The climate and natural vegetation of the country
questions.e: Economic systems are classified according to who owns and controls the factors of production, that is, land, labour and capital. This ownership pattern determines whether an economy is capitalist, socialist or mixed.
questions.p: Dem dey divide economic system based on who get and control land, labour and capital. Dis ownership pattern na im dey show whether economy na capitalist, socialist or mixed.

questions.q: In a pure capitalist economy, consumers are said to exercise 'consumer sovereignty'. This means that:
o: Government fixes the quantity of goods every household must buy
The central planning authority decides consumer preferences
Consumers, through their spending decisions, influence what producers choose to produce
Producers alone decide what consumers must buy regardless of demand
questions.e: Consumer sovereignty means buyers direct production by how they spend their money, since producers aim to make profit and will supply what consumers demand. It is a key feature of the price mechanism in capitalism.
questions.p: Consumer sovereignty mean say buyers dey direct wetypun producers go make through how dem spend dia money. Producers like to make profit, so na wetin consumers demand na im dem go supply.

questions.q: A key argument put forward by supporters of socialism in favour of state ownership of major industries is that it helps to:
o: Reduce inequality in the distribution of income and wealth
Increase competition among many private firms
Maximise profit for a few wealthy individuals
Allow prices to be determined solely by market forces
questions.e: Socialists argue that when government owns and controls major industries, wealth and income can be shared more evenly among citizens instead of concentrating profits in the hands of a few private owners. This reduces inequality.
questions.p: Socialist people dey talk say if government own major industries, money and wealth go spread well for citizens instead make profit pack for only small private owners hand. Dis one dey reduce inequality.

questions.q: Chief Adebayo argues that a mixed economy is better than a purely capitalist economy because it allows government to correct certain weaknesses of the free market. Which of the following is one such weakness that government intervention in a mixed economy specifically addresses?
o: The automatic equal distribution of income without any policy
The complete absence of private businesses in the economy
The total elimination of the price mechanism
The existence of monopolies that exploit consumers through excessive prices
questions.e: A weakness of pure capitalism is that powerful firms can form monopolies and exploit consumers with high prices. In a mixed economy, government intervenes through regulation, taxation and sometimes price control to check such exploitation.
questions.p: One bad thing about pure capitalism na say big companies fit form monopoly and use high price exploit consumers. For mixed economy, government dey put mouth through law and price control to stop dis kind exploitation.

questions.q: Which of the following is a distinguishing feature of a mixed economy as practised in countries like Nigeria?
o: Only the government owns and operates all businesses
Only private individuals own and operate all businesses without any government involvement
Both the government and private individuals own and operate businesses side by side
Production decisions are made solely by a central planning committee
questions.e: A mixed economy combines features of both capitalism and socialism, so both the public sector (government) and the private sector (individuals and companies) co-exist and carry out economic activities together.
questions.p: Mixed economy na where both government and private people dey join hand own and run business together. E carry features of capitalism and socialism join body.

questions.q: One of the basic economic problems facing every economic system, regardless of whether it is capitalist, socialist or mixed, is:
o: Deciding the religious beliefs of the citizens
Deciding what quantity of goods and services to produce with limited resources
Deciding which political party should be in power
Deciding the national language to be used in schools
questions.e: Every economic system, no matter its ideology, must solve the basic problems of what, how and for whom to produce because resources are scarce relative to human wants. This is independent of politics, religion or language.
questions.p: Every economy must solve basic problem of wetin, how and for who to produce because resources limited pass human wants. Dis one no concern politics or language.

questions.q: A particular country operates an economic system in which land and major industries are collectively owned by the state, individual profit-making is discouraged, and the central authority determines production targets and distribution of goods to citizens based on need rather than ability to pay. This description best fits:
o: A barter economic system
A laissez-faire capitalist economy
A free market economy with no government
A socialist (command) economy
questions.e: The description matches socialism, where the state owns major resources, profit motive is downplayed, and a central authority plans production and distributes goods, often according to need rather than purchasing power.
questions.p: Na socialism match dis description well well, because state dey own major resources and central authority dey plan production and share goods based on need, no be by who get money pass.

questions.q: Suppose an economy initially operates as a purely capitalist system where private firms freely set prices and output. The government later introduces minimum wage laws, consumer protection agencies, and taxes on luxury goods, while still allowing private ownership of businesses. This change best illustrates a shift towards:
o: A purely socialist economy
A mixed economy
A subsistence economy
A barter economy
questions.e: Introducing government regulation such as minimum wage laws, consumer protection and taxation while still permitting private ownership shows a blend of capitalist and socialist features, which defines a mixed economy rather than a purely capitalist or socialist one.
questions.p: If government add minimum wage, consumer protection and tax to private business ownership, e mean say government don mix capitalist and socialist style together. Dis na wetin we dey call mixed economy.

questions.q: A trader in Onitsha market recorded the number of bags of rice sold over 7 days as follows: 4, 6, 4, 9, 4, 7, 2. What is the mode of this distribution?
questions.e: The mode is the value that occurs most often. Here, 4 appears three times, more than any other value.
questions.p: Mode na that number wey dey show pass all of them for inside data. Na 4 dey appear three times, so na him be the mode.

questions.q: A class of 12 students scored the following marks in an Economics test: 30, 35, 40, 40, 45, 50, 55, 60, 60, 65, 70, 75. What is the median score?
questions.e: With 12 values arranged in order, the median is the average of the 6th and 7th values, which are 50 and 55. Adding them and dividing by 2 gives 52.5.
questions.p: Because the total number of students na 12, we go find the middle two numbers wey be 50 and 55. If you add 50 and 55 come divide am by 2, you go get 52.5.

questions.q: A researcher wants to compare the monthly output (in tonnes) of three different cassava farms over one year on a single chart, making it easy to see which farm produced more in each month. Which graphical tool is most suitable?
o: Pie chart
Histogram
Pictogram
Multiple bar chart
questions.e: A multiple bar chart allows direct comparison of several categories (farms) side by side for each time period (month). A pie chart only shows proportions of a whole, not comparisons across time.
questions.p: Multiple bar chart good well well to compare different farms side by side for each month. Pie chart na just to show part of one whole thing, e no dey good for this kind comparison.

questions.q: A frequency table of the number of children per household in a Lagos community shows: 1 child (8 households), 2 children (15 households), 3 children (10 households), 4 children (7 households). If a pie chart is drawn to represent this data, what angle (in degrees) should represent households with 2 children?
questions.e: The total number of households is 8+15+10+7 = 40. The angle for 2-children households is (15/40) x 360 = 135 degrees.
questions.p: Total household na 40. To find the angle for the 15 households wey get 2 children, just do (15/40) times 360, and you go get 135 degrees.

questions.q: In a distribution of examination scores, the mean is 60, the median is 60, and the mode is 60. What does this suggest about the shape of the distribution?
o: It is negatively skewed
It is symmetrical
It is bimodal
It is positively skewed
questions.e: When the mean, median and mode are equal, the distribution is symmetrical, with values evenly balanced around the centre. Skewed distributions have these measures pulled apart in one direction.
questions.p: If mean, median and mode join body become one number, e mean say the distribution balance well well like mirror. Na wet we dey call symmetrical distribution.

questions.q: The number of customers served daily at a POS shop in Ibadan for 9 days were: 12, 15, 12, 18, 20, 12, 25, 15, 12. What is the mode of this distribution?
questions.e: The value 12 appears four times, which is more than any other value in the data set. The mode is the value that occurs most frequently.
questions.p: Na 12 dey show pass four times for inside di numbers, so na di mode be that. Di number wey dey show pass na im be mode.

questions.q: A pie chart is used to represent the allocation of a family's monthly income of ₦60,000 into four expenditure areas. If the sector for feeding occupies 120° of the circle, how much naira was spent on feeding?
questions.e: A full circle is 360°, so the feeding sector represents 120/360 of the total income. This fraction (one-third) of ₦60,000 gives ₦20,000.
questions.p: Whole circle na 360°, so feeding dey take 120/360 of everything. If you divide ₦60,000 by three, you go get ₦20,000.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major limitation of using the mean as a measure of central tendency for a set of traders' daily sales figures?
o: It cannot be calculated unless the data is arranged in order
It is strongly affected by extremely high or low values in the data
It ignores all the actual values and depends only on frequency
It can only be used when there are an odd number of values
questions.e: The mean is calculated using every value in the data set, so one unusually large or small figure (an outlier) can pull the mean away from where most values actually lie. This makes it less reliable than the median in such cases.
questions.p: Mean dey carry every number inside calculate, so if one number too big or too small, e go scatter di average. E make am less reliable pass median for that kind matter.

questions.q: The table below shows the distribution of ages of 40 members of a cooperative society in a local government area, grouped into class intervals of 21-25, 26-30, 31-35, and 36-40 years with frequencies 6, 14, 12, and 8 respectively. What is the class mark (mid-point) of the class interval with the highest frequency?
questions.e: The class interval with the highest frequency is 26-30, which has 14 members. The class mark is found by adding the lower and upper limits and dividing by 2, giving (26+30)/2 = 28.
questions.p: Di group wey get highest frequency na 26-30 because 14 people dey inside. To find di class mark, add 26 and 30, then divide by 2 to get 28.

questions.q: A small business records its weekly revenues (in ₦'000) over eight weeks as: 50, 60, 55, 70, 65, 80, 55, 75. What is the median weekly revenue?
questions.e: Arranging the values in order gives 50, 55, 55, 60, 65, 70, 75, 80. Since there are eight values, the median is the average of the 4th and 5th values, which are 60 and 65, giving (60+65)/2 = 62.5.
questions.p: If you arrange di numbers from small to big, di fourth and fifth numbers na 60 and 65. When you add dem and divide by 2, you go get 62.5.

questions.q: When comparing the output of two palm oil processing firms over several years, a researcher wants a single chart that clearly shows both the composition (parts that make up a whole, such as different product types) and the overall trend over time. Which combination of tools would best achieve this purpose?
o: A component bar chart together with a line graph
A pie chart combined with the mode
A simple bar chart only
The mean calculated from a frequency table
questions.e: A component bar chart breaks each year's total output into its different parts, while a line graph traces how figures change over time. Using both together gives information on composition and trend that a single chart or a single average cannot provide.
questions.p: Component bar chart dey show how things join make whole, while line graph dey show how e dey move over time. If you use both, you go see composition and trend well well.

questions.q: Chidinma buys 4 tubers of yam per week when the price is ₦800 each. When the price falls to ₦600, she buys 6 tubers per week, with her income and taste unchanged. This change in quantity demanded is best described as a
o: change in the determinants of demand
shift of the demand curve to the right
movement along the demand curve
decrease in demand
questions.e: Since only the price of yam changed and quantity responded along the same curve, this is a movement along the demand curve, not a shift. A shift would require a change in a non-price factor.
questions.p: Na only yam price change, and the quantity follow am waka for the same curve. E no be shift at all.

questions.q: A survey shows that whenever households in Kano expect the price of cooking gas to rise sharply next month, they immediately buy more gas cylinders now. This behaviour illustrates the effect of which determinant of demand?
o: change in consumer taste
future price expectation
change in price of substitute goods
change in consumer income
questions.e: When buyers expect prices to rise in future, they increase current purchases to beat the expected increase. This is the effect of price expectation on demand, a known non-price determinant.
questions.p: If people dey expect say price go high tomorrow, dem go rush buy am today. Na wetin we dey call future price expectation.

questions.q: The demand for fountain pens in a school bookshop is given as Qd = 100 - 5P, where Qd is the number of pens demanded per week and P is the price in naira. If the price of a pen is ₦12, what is the quantity demanded?
o: 60 pens
48 pens
40 pens
35 pens
questions.e: Substituting P = 12 into Qd = 100 - 5P gives Qd = 100 - 60 = 40. This shows the quantity of pens demanded at that price.
questions.p: Make we put 12 inside P for the formula. E go give us 100 minus 60, wey come remain 40 pens.

questions.q: Suppose the demand for a particular brand of face cream increases sharply after a popular Nollywood actress is seen using it in public, even though its price and consumers' income remain unchanged. This change in demand is best explained by
o: an increase in consumer income
a change in consumer taste or preference
a rise in the price of complementary goods
a fall in the price of substitutes
questions.e: Since price and income are unchanged, the increase in demand must be due to a change in taste or preference caused by the endorsement. Tastes and fashion are recognised non-price determinants of demand.
questions.p: Since price and money for hand no change, na actor wey use am make people like the cream pass before. Na change in taste be that.

questions.q: A government policy reduces import duties on foreign rice, causing its price to fall from ₦1,200 to ₦900 per bag, while the price of locally produced rice remains at ₦1,000. Assuming the two are substitutes, what is the most likely effect on the demand for locally produced rice?
o: Demand for local rice will decrease
Demand for local rice will increase
Demand for local rice will remain unchanged
Quantity demanded of local rice will move along its curve
questions.e: Since foreign rice becomes cheaper than local rice, consumers are expected to substitute away from local rice towards foreign rice, causing the demand curve for local rice to shift leftward, representing a decrease in demand.
questions.p: As foreign rice come cheap pass local rice, people go leave local rice go buy foreign one. Demand for local rice go come drop.

questions.q: In a certain town, economists observe that as the price of a popular brand of bottled water rises, the quantity demanded also rises because wealthy residents now associate the higher price with higher social status. Which special type of good does this describe?
o: inferior good
normal good
Giffen good
Veblen good
questions.e: A Veblen good is a good whose quantity demanded increases as its price rises because consumers associate the high price with prestige or status. This differs from a Giffen good, which rises due to income effects on necessities.
questions.p: Veblen good na the type of thing wey people dey buy more as price dey high because of status. E dey show class.

questions.q: At a price of ₦250 per loaf, bakers in Enugu sell 300 loaves of bread daily. When the price rises to ₦300, two things happen at once: the quantity demanded falls to 250 loaves due to the price change, and separately, a rise in the price of flour causes bakers' costs to rise, shifting the supply curve, which further affects market price. Which single factor purely caused the movement from 300 to 250 loaves, ignoring the supply-side effect?
o: change in consumer taste
change in the price of bread itself
change in consumer income
change in the price of flour
questions.e: A movement along the demand curve, such as quantity falling from 300 to 250 loaves, is caused only by a change in the price of the good itself. The flour price change affects supply, not the position along the demand curve.
questions.p: Na only the price of bread itself cause the movement from 300 to 250 loaves. The flour matter na for supply side.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs of goods best illustrates complementary goods in demand theory?
o: Indomie noodles and Supreme noodles
Rice and beans sold separately in different shops with no link
Bread and butter
Tea and coffee
questions.e: Complementary goods are used together, so a rise in the price of one reduces demand for the other. Bread and butter are consumed together, unlike the other pairs which are either substitutes or unrelated.
questions.p: Complementary goods na things wey dem dey use together, so if price of one go up, demand for the other one go drop. Bread and butter dey go together well well, unlike the other ones wey be substitute or no get connection.

questions.q: A rise in the population of a town from 50,000 to 80,000 persons, with incomes and tastes unchanged, is most likely to cause which of the following in the market for garri?
o: A rightward shift of the demand curve for garri
A leftward shift of the demand curve for garri
A movement up the demand curve for garri
No change in the demand curve for garri
questions.e: Population is a determinant of demand; more people in the town means more buyers, so at every price more garri is demanded. This causes the entire demand curve to shift to the right.
questions.p: Population na one of the things wey dey determine demand, meaning say when people plenty for town, more buyers go dey. E mean say at every price, people go demand more garri, and dis one go make the whole demand curve shift go right side.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of derived demand?
o: Demand for shoes by a student for school use
Demand for bread by households for breakfast
Demand for sugar by a household for tea
Demand for flour by a bakery because bread is demanded by consumers
questions.e: Derived demand arises when a good is wanted not for its own sake but because it helps produce another good that is demanded. The bakery wants flour only because consumers demand bread, so the demand for flour is derived from the demand for bread.
questions.p: Derived demand happen when person want something not because of itself, but because e help to produce another good wey people want. Bakery dey need flour only because consumers dey demand bread, so demand for flour come from demand for bread.

questions.q: In a village market, the demand schedule for oranges shows that at ₦50 each, 200 oranges are bought, and at ₦80 each, 140 oranges are bought, with all other factors unchanged. This relationship illustrates
o: the law of diminishing marginal utility only
an exception to the law of demand
a shift in demand
the law of demand
questions.e: As price rises from 50 to 80, quantity demanded falls from 200 to 140, showing the inverse relationship between price and quantity demanded. This is exactly what the law of demand describes, with other factors held constant.
questions.p: As price dey go up from 50 to 80, quantity wey people dey buy dey fall from 200 to 140, and dis one show the opposite relationship between price and quantity demanded. Na exactly wetin the law of demand dey talk, as other things remain constant.

questions.q: Okon notices that whenever the price of beef rises, more people in his neighbourhood buy chicken instead, even though their incomes and tastes have not changed. This behaviour is best explained by which determinant of demand?
o: Price of substitute goods
Population size
Consumer's income
Consumer's taste
questions.e: Beef and chicken are substitutes, so when beef becomes more expensive, consumers switch to chicken, increasing its demand. This shift is caused by a change in the price of a related substitute good, not income or taste.
questions.p: Beef and chicken na substitute goods, so if beef price cost, people go quick change to chicken. Na change for the price of related substitute good cause dis movement, and not income or taste.

questions.q: A particular brand of designer wristwatch is priced very high deliberately, and some wealthy buyers demand more of it simply because of its high price, viewing it as a status symbol. This situation describes
o: a Giffen good
a normal good obeying the law of demand
a Veblen good (ostentatious/conspicuous consumption good)
a complementary good
questions.e: A Veblen good is bought more as its price rises because of the prestige or status it confers, which is an exception to the normal law of demand. This differs from a Giffen good, which rises in demand due to income effects on necessities, not status.
questions.p: Veblen good na item wey people dey buy more as price dey increase because of status and pride, and dis one na exception to normal law of demand. E different from Giffen good wey be say poor people dey buy am more when price rise because of poverty.

questions.q: During the rainy season in a Nigerian city, the demand for umbrellas rises sharply even though the price of umbrellas has not changed. This change in demand is best explained by
o: an increase in the price of substitute goods
a change in consumer taste caused by weather conditions
a movement along the demand curve due to price change
a fall in the price of umbrellas
questions.e: Since the price of umbrellas is unchanged but demand still increases, the cause must be a non-price factor, here a seasonal change affecting consumer taste or preference for umbrellas. This causes the whole demand curve to shift rightward rather than a movement along it.
questions.p: Since umbrella price never change but demand still high, na because weather change and people taste for umbrella don increase. Dis one dey make the whole demand curve shift go right side instead make movement happen for top the curve.

questions.q: A technological breakthrough enables palm oil processors in Imo State to extract more oil from the same quantity of palm fruits at lower cost. Holding price constant, what is the most likely effect on the supply of palm oil?
o: There is a downward movement along the same supply curve
The supply curve shifts to the left
