There is an upward movement along the same supply curve
The supply curve shifts to the right
questions.e: An improvement in technology lowers production costs and raises output at every price, so the whole supply curve shifts rightward (an increase in supply). It is a shift, not a movement, because price itself did not change.
questions.p: Better technology dey reduce how much money cost to produce things, con make production plenty for every price. Na im make the whole supply curve dey shift go the right side.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a direct determinant of the supply of a commodity?
o: Number of sellers in the market
Consumers' income
Cost of production
Government taxes and subsidies
questions.e: Consumers' income is a determinant of demand, not supply, since it affects buyers' purchasing power rather than producers' willingness or ability to supply. Cost of production, taxes/subsidies and the number of sellers all directly affect supply.
questions.p: Na demand money wey consumers get dey affect, no be supply. Cost of production, taxes, and number of sellers na direct things wey dey control supply.

questions.q: The supply schedule for bags of garri in a market is such that at a price of ₦2,000 per bag, 60 bags are supplied, and at ₦3,000 per bag, 90 bags are supplied, with all other factors held constant. This relationship illustrates
o: the law of diminishing returns
a shift in the supply curve
a direct relationship between price and quantity supplied
an inverse relationship between price and quantity supplied
questions.e: As price rises from ₦2,000 to ₦3,000, quantity supplied also rises from 60 to 90 bags, showing a direct (positive) relationship between price and quantity supplied, which is the law of supply. This is movement along a curve, not a shift.
questions.p: As price dey go up from ₦2,000 to ₦3,000, quantity supplied con join am increase from 60 to 90 bags. Dis one show say price and quantity supplied dey follow each other carry body.

questions.q: A severe flood destroys large farmlands used for tomato cultivation in Kebbi State, sharply reducing the number of farmers able to grow tomatoes. Assuming prices remain unchanged, what effect will this have on the supply curve of tomatoes?
o: It shifts leftward because the number of suppliers and their capacity has fallen
It remains the same but quantity supplied moves downward
It remains the same but quantity supplied moves upward
It shifts rightward because scarcity encourages more output
questions.e: A flood reduces productive farmland and the number of active suppliers, so less tomato can be supplied at every price level. This is captured as a leftward (decrease) shift of the entire supply curve, not a movement along it.
questions.p: Bad flood wey spoil farm land and reduce farmers mean say tomatoes go reduce for market. E dey make the supply curve shift go the left because people no get capacity again.

questions.q: A manufacturer of plastic chairs in Aba finds that the price of a key raw material, PVC resin, has doubled within a month due to import restrictions, while the selling price of plastic chairs has not changed. What is the expected immediate effect on the supply of plastic chairs?
o: Quantity supplied increases along the same curve
Supply remains totally unaffected since price of chairs is unchanged
Supply decreases as the supply curve shifts leftward
Supply increases because more resin is now available
questions.e: A rise in the cost of an essential input raises production costs, making it less profitable to supply the same quantity at the old price, so producers reduce output at every price level. This is shown as a leftward shift of the supply curve, distinct from any change in the chair's own price.
questions.p: If raw material price cost too much, production go hard for manufacturers. Na im make supply curve shift go left since profit don reduce.

questions.q: A poultry farmer in Ogun State produces both eggs and chicken meat from the same flock of birds. If the market price of chicken meat rises sharply due to festive season demand, what is the most likely effect on the supply of eggs from the same farm, assuming egg price is unchanged?
o: Egg supply rises because the birds lay more eggs when fed better
Egg supply shifts rightward because the two goods are in competitive supply
Egg supply is completely unrelated to the chicken meat market
Egg supply falls as more birds are slaughtered for meat, reducing the egg-laying flock
questions.e: Eggs and chicken meat are joint products from the same birds, so when more birds are slaughtered to meet rising demand for meat, fewer birds remain to lay eggs. This reduces the supply of eggs even though the egg price itself has not changed, illustrating joint supply effects.
questions.p: If dem sell chicken meat well and farmers go slaughter more birds, the remaining ones wey go dey lay eggs go reduce. Dis one mean say egg supply go fall join.

questions.q: In a competitive market for yam tubers, which combination of events will definitely cause the supply curve to shift to the right?
o: A new government tax on yam sales and a rise in cost of seed yams
A fall in the wages of farm labourers and discovery of a cheaper fertilizer
An increase in farmers' expectation of future price rises and higher transportation costs
A rise in the price of yam and favourable weather conditions
questions.e: A fall in wages and a cheaper fertilizer both lower the cost of producing yam, encouraging farmers to supply more at every price, which shifts the supply curve rightward. The other options either describe a movement along the curve or include at least one factor that would shift supply leftward.
questions.p: If labour wages fall and fertilizer cheap, yam production go easy and cheap for farmers. Dis one go make supply curve shift go the right.

questions.q: Given the supply function Qs = 20 + 3P for crates of soft drinks, where P is price in naira per crate, by how many crates will quantity supplied increase if price rises from ₦50 to ₦80?
questions.e: At P=50, Qs = 20+150 = 170. At P=80, Qs = 20+240 = 260. The increase is 260-170 = 90 crates.
questions.p: If P bi 50, Qs bi 170. If P bi 80, Qs bi 260. So, di increase na 260 minus 170, wey give us 90 crates.

questions.q: A farmer in Niger State grows both maize and sorghum on the same land, using the same labour and inputs, and can switch between them depending on which gives better returns. Maize and sorghum are best described, from the supply side, as:
o: joint supply
composite supply
competitive supply
derived supply
questions.e: Competitive supply occurs when the same resources can be used to produce alternative goods, so producing more of one means producing less of the other. Maize and sorghum here compete for the same land and inputs.
questions.p: Competitive supply dey happen when you fit use di same land or machine produce different things. Because maize and sorghum dey fight for di same land, dem dey compete.

questions.q: Which of the following changes would cause a leftward shift of the entire supply curve for cassava flour in a Nigerian market?
o: A fall in the price of cassava flour itself
An increase in the number of buyers of cassava flour
A fall in the price of a substitute food item
A rise in the wages paid to processing workers
questions.e: A rise in the cost of production, such as higher wages, raises the cost of supplying cassava flour, pushing the whole supply curve leftward (less supplied at every price). Changes in the price of the good itself cause movement along the curve, not a shift, and changes in buyers or substitute prices affect demand, not supply directly.
questions.p: If worker salary go up, e go cost more money to produce cassava flour. Dis one go make supply curve shift go left because producers no go fit supply as before.

questions.q: The government of a certain state removes an existing production levy that was previously charged on every bag of cement produced by local factories. Assuming no other change, the most likely effect on the supply curve of cement is that it will:
o: shift to the left, as production costs fall
shift to the right, as production costs fall
remain stationary, with a downward movement along it
remain stationary, with an upward movement along it
questions.e: Removing a per-unit levy lowers the cost of producing each bag of cement, encouraging producers to supply more at every price level. This is shown as a rightward (outward) shift of the whole supply curve, not a movement along it.
questions.p: If government remove tax, e go cost less to produce cement. Producers go come happy to supply more, so di supply curve go shift go right.

questions.q: A new government policy requires all small-scale soap manufacturers in Nigeria to obtain an expensive annual operating license before they can produce and sell soap. Holding all other factors constant, this policy will most likely cause:
o: a leftward shift of the soap supply curve
a downward movement along the existing soap supply curve
a rightward shift of the soap supply curve
an upward movement along the existing soap supply curve
questions.e: An expensive licensing requirement raises the overall cost of doing business for soap producers, which discourages supply at every price level. This is represented by a leftward shift of the entire supply curve, since it is not caused by a change in the price of soap itself.
questions.p: If license cost too much, e go make production cost high for soap makers. Dis one go make dem supply less soap, so di supply curve go shift go left.

questions.q: In a market where only yam is supplied, suppose there is simultaneously a bumper harvest (increasing the quantity of yam available) and a sharp rise in the price of yam due to high demand from neighbouring countries. On a supply-demand diagram for yam, these two events together would most likely result in:
o: only a rightward shift of the supply curve, with no movement along it
a rightward shift of the supply curve combined with an upward movement along it
a leftward shift of the supply curve combined with a downward movement along it
only an upward movement along a fixed supply curve, with no shift
questions.e: A bumper harvest increases supply at every price, shifting the whole supply curve to the right, while the rise in yam's own price due to demand causes an upward movement along that new curve. Both effects occur together, so the curve shifts right and there is also movement along it due to the price change.
questions.p: Bumper harvest go shift supply curve go right because plenty yam dey. Di price rise go come make movement happen along dat new curve.

questions.q: In economics, market equilibrium is best described as the situation where:
o: The quantity demanded equals the quantity supplied at a given price
The government fixes a price that both buyers and sellers must obey
Producers supply more goods than consumers are willing to buy
Consumers demand more goods than producers are willing to sell
questions.e: Equilibrium occurs where the demand curve and supply curve intersect, so quantity demanded exactly equals quantity supplied. At this price there is no shortage or surplus.
questions.p: Na where demand curve meet supply curve equilibrium dey happen, meaning say wetyn people wan buy equal wetyn sellers bring come market. For this price, shortage or surplus no go dey at all.

questions.q: A sudden outbreak of bird flu destroys many poultry farms in Ibadan, sharply reducing the supply of chicken while demand stays the same. What will likely happen to the equilibrium price and quantity of chicken?
o: Price rises and quantity rises
Price falls and quantity falls
Price falls and quantity rises
Price rises and quantity falls
questions.e: A fall in supply with demand unchanged shifts the supply curve leftward. This leads to a higher equilibrium price and a lower equilibrium quantity.
questions.p: If supply drop and demand remain the same, the supply curve go shift go left. Naim make the price go high up and the total quantity wey people dey sell come fall down.

questions.q: The demand for a product is said to be perfectly elastic when:
o: Quantity demanded does not change no matter how price changes, giving a vertical demand curve
A given percentage change in price causes an equal percentage change in quantity demanded
Quantity demanded changes infinitely at a particular price, giving a horizontal demand curve
Quantity demanded falls to zero regardless of price changes
questions.e: Perfectly elastic demand means buyers will buy any quantity at one fixed price but none at a higher price. This is represented by a horizontal demand curve.
questions.p: Perfectly elastic demand mean say buyers ready to buy any amount at one particular price, but dem no go buy anything if price increase small. Na horizontal demand curve dem take dey represent am.

questions.q: If the price elasticity of supply of a good is 0.6, the supply is said to be:
o: Unitary elastic
Perfectly elastic
Inelastic
Elastic
questions.e: A price elasticity of supply value less than one means quantity supplied responds proportionately less than the change in price. This makes supply inelastic.
questions.p: If price elasticity of supply value dey less than one, e mean say quantity supplied no dey move as quick as price change. That one make the supply to be inelastic.

questions.q: When the government fixes a minimum wage above the market equilibrium wage, which of the following is the most likely consequence in the labour market?
o: An automatic fall in the price of goods produced by the firms
Equilibrium is unaffected since wages are not prices
A shortage of workers as firms struggle to find enough labour
A surplus of labour as the quantity of workers willing to work exceeds the quantity firms demand
questions.e: A minimum wage set above equilibrium is a price floor for labour. It encourages more people to seek jobs while firms hire fewer workers, creating unemployment (a surplus of labour).
questions.p: Minimum wage wey high pass market equilibrium dey act like price floor for labour. E go make plenty people wan work, but companies go employ small workers, con cause surplus of labour.

questions.q: A trader in Aba notices that when she raises the price of her handbags by 20%, her total revenue falls. This shows that the demand for her handbags is:
o: Perfectly inelastic
Elastic
Inelastic
Unitary elastic
questions.e: When a price rise causes total revenue to fall, it means the percentage fall in quantity demanded exceeds the percentage rise in price. This is the defining feature of elastic demand.
questions.p: If price increase make total revenue fall, e mean say the percentage drop for quantity demanded pass the percentage increase for price. Na him be elastic demand.

questions.q: Government imposes a maximum price (price ceiling) on rice below the free market equilibrium price in order to protect consumers. One likely effect of this policy is:
o: The emergence of a black market where rice is sold above the official price
A fall in the demand for rice below the equilibrium quantity
An automatic increase in the supply of rice to meet demand
A persistent surplus of rice in the market
questions.e: A price ceiling below equilibrium causes quantity demanded to exceed quantity supplied, creating a shortage. This shortage often pushes some buyers and sellers to trade illegally at higher prices, giving rise to a black market.
questions.p: Price ceiling wey dey below equilibrium go cause shortage because demand go pass supply. This shortage go come make people start to dey sell for underground market at higher price.

questions.q: In a market for fresh pepper at Mile 12 market, Lagos, the demand function is Qd = 60 - 3P and the supply function is Qs = -10 + 2P, where P is price in naira and Q is quantity in baskets. What is the equilibrium price?
questions.e: At equilibrium Qd equals Qs, so 60 - 3P = -10 + 2P, giving 70 = 5P and P = 14. Substituting back confirms both quantities equal 18 baskets.
questions.p: If you set Qd equal to Qs, you go get 60 - 3P = -10 + 2P. When you solve am, 70 = 5P, so P = 14. Both sides go give you 18 baskets.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why the price elasticity of demand for a narrowly defined good, such as 'Peak milk brand', is usually higher than that of a broadly defined good, such as 'milk in general'?
o: Narrowly defined goods have fewer uses than broadly defined goods
Narrowly defined goods are usually necessities rather than luxuries
Narrowly defined goods take a larger share of consumer income
Narrowly defined goods have more close substitutes available to consumers
questions.e: A specific brand like Peak milk has many substitute brands of milk, so consumers can easily switch if its price rises, making demand more elastic. The broader category 'milk' has fewer substitutes, making its demand less elastic.
questions.p: Peak milk get plenty other milk wey people fit buy if price high, so demand dey elastic. But 'milk' as general category no get many substitute, so e no dey elastic like that.

questions.q: A government wants to support local rice farmers by guaranteeing them a price above the free market equilibrium price. This policy is best described as a form of
o: price ceiling, which will create a shortage of rice in the market
indirect taxation, which will reduce farmers' income
price floor, which will create a surplus of rice in the market
subsidy on consumption, which will increase demand for rice
questions.e: A price fixed above equilibrium to help producers is called a price floor or minimum price. Since the price is above equilibrium, quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded, creating a surplus.
questions.p: When government fix price pass equilibrium to help farmers, we dey call am price floor. Because price high, supply go pass demand and surplus go happen.

questions.q: The income elasticity of demand for a particular good is calculated to be -1.5. Based on this value, the good can be classified as
o: an inferior good
a good with unitary elasticity
a normal good with elastic demand
a luxury good
questions.e: A negative income elasticity means that demand for the good falls as income rises. Goods with this property are classified as inferior goods.
questions.p: If income elasticity na minus, e mean say as person money increase, e no go want buy that item again. We dey call dis kain item inferior good.

questions.q: Suppose the supply function for tomatoes in a market is Qs = 5P - 20. If the price rises from ₦20 to ₦25 per basket, what is the price elasticity of supply, using the initial price and quantity as the base?
questions.e: At P=20, Qs = 5(20)-20 = 80; at P=25, Qs = 5(25)-20 = 105. Percentage change in quantity is 25/80 = 0.3125 and percentage change in price is 5/20 = 0.25, so elasticity = 0.3125/0.25 = 1.25.
questions.p: At P=20, Qs na 80, and at P=25, Qs na 105. Percentage change for quantity na 0.3125 while for price na 0.25, so 0.3125 divide by 0.25 give you 1.25.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes a change in quantity demanded from a change in demand?
o: A change in quantity demanded is caused by a change in the price of the good itself, while a change in demand is caused by a change in a non-price factor
A change in quantity demanded is caused by a change in consumer income, while a change in demand is caused by a change in price
Both are caused only by changes in the price of the good, but they differ in magnitude
A change in quantity demanded shifts the entire demand curve, while a change in demand moves along the curve
questions.e: A change in the price of the good itself causes a movement along the demand curve, known as a change in quantity demanded. A change in demand refers to a shift of the entire curve caused by non-price factors like income or tastes.
questions.p: If price of the item change, na movement along the curve we dey see, wey be change in quantity demanded. But if other things like income change, the whole curve go shift, wey be change in demand.

questions.q: In the market for exercise books in a Nigerian town, equilibrium price is ₦150 per book. If the government fixes a maximum price of ₦100 per book, which of the following is the most likely consequence?
o: No change in the market since price controls do not affect quantity
An increase in the equilibrium price as demand falls
A shortage of exercise books as quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied
A surplus of exercise books as sellers produce more at the lower price
questions.e: Setting a maximum price below the equilibrium price means producers supply less while consumers demand more at the lower price. This gap between quantity demanded and quantity supplied creates a shortage.
questions.p: If government fix price lower pass equilibrium, sellers no go wan produce plenty, but buyers go want buy more. Dis one go cause shortage for market.

questions.q: Which of the following is the best example of entrepreneurship as a factor of production in a Nigerian context?
o: A landlord who receives rent for a warehouse used for storing cement
A bank that charges interest on a loan given to a trader
A worker who is paid ₦35,000 monthly to arrange goods on shelves in a supermarket
A woman who borrows ₦2 million, rents a shop in Onitsha, hires workers and bears the risk of running a provisions store
questions.e: Entrepreneurship involves organising other factors of production and bearing business risk for profit. The woman who initiates, finances, and manages the business while bearing risk fits this role, unlike the worker, landlord, or bank.
questions.p: Entrepreneurship mean say person go arrange other factor of production and carry the risk to make profit. Na the woman wey borrow ₦2 million, rent shop for Onitsha, and bear business risk fit this description well well.

questions.q: In the theory of production, the law of diminishing returns states that as more units of a variable factor are added to a fixed factor, output will eventually
o: increase but at a diminishing rate
rise at an increasing rate indefinitely
remain constant regardless of the number of workers added
fall to zero immediately after the second worker is employed
questions.e: The law of diminishing returns says that beyond a certain point, each additional unit of a variable factor added to a fixed factor yields less extra output than the previous one. This means total output still rises, but more slowly.
questions.p: Law of diminishing returns talk say if you dey add variable factor join fixed factor, the extra output wey you go dey get go start to dey reduce. Total output still dey go up, but e dey increase slowly.

questions.q: A garment factory in Kano has a fixed workshop and machines. As it employs the 1st to 4th tailor, total output rises sharply. From the 5th tailor onward, total output still rises but by smaller amounts each time, until the 9th tailor is added and total output stops rising. The stage from the 5th to the 8th tailor best illustrates
o: the stage of increasing returns
the point of maximum total product only
the stage of diminishing returns
the stage of negative returns
questions.e: When total output keeps rising but each extra worker adds less than the one before, production is in the stage of diminishing returns. This is different from increasing returns (output rising faster) or negative returns (output falling).
questions.p: If total output dey still rise but each extra worker dey add small small quantity, dat one na the stage of diminishing returns. E no be increasing returns or negative returns.

questions.q: A cassava processing mill in Kogi has 5 workers producing a total of 250 bags of garri per week. When a 6th worker is employed, total output rises to 270 bags. What is the marginal product of the 6th worker?
o: 50 bags
20 bags
45 bags
270 bags
questions.e: Marginal product is the change in total output from employing one more worker, calculated as 270 minus 250, which equals 20 bags. The other options either use the wrong figures or confuse marginal with total or average product.
questions.p: Marginal product na the extra output wey one extra worker dey bring, wey you go get if you minus the old total output from the new total output. If you minus 250 from 270, you go get 20 bags.

questions.q: Which of the following is a key difference between division of labour and specialization as used in production theory?
o: Division of labour reduces output while specialization increases output
Specialization only occurs in agriculture, while division of labour only occurs in industry
Division of labour applies only to machines, while specialization applies only to workers
Division of labour refers to breaking a production process into separate tasks, while specialization refers to a worker, firm or region focusing on a particular task or product
questions.e: Division of labour is the splitting of a job into smaller tasks done by different people, while specialization is the broader concept of focusing on one task, trade, or product for efficiency. Both work together but are not identical.
questions.p: Division of labour na to break work into small small part make different people do am, while specialization na when person or place focus on only one particular work or product. Dem two different, even though dem dey work hand in hand.

questions.q: A vulcanizer in Minna rents a workshop for ₦8,000 per month. Whether he repairs 0 tyres or 100 tyres in a month, he still pays this same ₦8,000 rent. This ₦8,000 is best described as his:
o: Variable cost
Marginal cost
Fixed cost
Average revenue
questions.e: A cost that does not change with the level of output, such as rent, is a fixed cost. It is paid even when output is zero.
questions.p: Cost wey no dey change as production dey increase, like house rent, na fixed cost. You must pay am even if you no produce anything at all.

questions.q: A plantain chips producer in Akure has total variable cost of ₦60,000 when she produces 300 packs. What is her average variable cost per pack?
questions.e: Average variable cost equals total variable cost divided by output, which is 60,000 divided by 300, giving 200 per pack.
questions.p: To find average variable cost, just divide total variable cost by output. If you divide 60,000 by 300, e go give you ₦200 per pack.

questions.q: A bottled drinks firm in Kaduna has the total cost function TC = 20,000 + 40Q, where Q is the number of crates produced. What is the firm's total variable cost when it produces 150 crates?
questions.e: Variable cost is the part of total cost that depends on output, which is 40Q. At Q = 150, this gives 40 multiplied by 150, equal to 6,000.
questions.p: Na only the part wey follow production, wey be 40Q, be variable cost. When you multiply 40 by 150, you go get ₦6,000.

questions.q: A tailor in Owerri finds that when he sews 10 clothes, his total cost is ₦45,000, and when he sews 11 clothes, his total cost rises to ₦48,500. What is his marginal cost of the 11th cloth?
questions.e: Marginal cost is the change in total cost from producing one more unit, which is 48,500 minus 45,000, equal to 3,500.
questions.p: Marginal cost na the extra money wey you spend to produce one more cloth. If you minus 45,000 from 48,500, you go get ₦3,500.

questions.q: A printing press in Jos has average total cost of ₦250 per flyer when it prints 400 flyers, and its average fixed cost at this output is ₦70. What is its average variable cost per flyer?
questions.e: Average total cost equals average fixed cost plus average variable cost, so average variable cost is 250 minus 70, which equals 180.
questions.p: Average total cost na the sum of average fixed cost and average variable cost. If you minus 70 from 250, you go remain with ₦180.

questions.q: A rice milling company in Kebbi observes that as it increases output in the short run, its average variable cost first falls, reaches a minimum, and then begins to rise. This pattern mainly occurs because of:
o: The law of diminishing returns to the variable factor of production
A constant rise in fixed cost per unit as output increases
An increase in the number of competing firms in the industry
A permanent fall in the market price of rice
questions.e: As more variable input is added to fixed capital, output per unit of input first rises then falls due to diminishing returns, causing average variable cost to first fall then rise. This is a short-run production phenomenon, not a market price or competition effect.
questions.p: As worker dem plenty join machine for short run, the law of diminishing returns go make output drop after time. E make average variable cost first fall, come later begin rise.

questions.q: A palm oil seller in Abia State pays ₦12,000 monthly as shop rent and ₦3,000 monthly for a trade licence, regardless of how many litres of oil she sells. These two amounts together represent her:
o: Marginal cost
Average variable cost
Total fixed cost
Total variable cost
questions.e: Costs that remain the same no matter the level of output, such as rent and licence fees, are fixed costs. They do not change whether she sells little or much oil.
questions.p: Shop rent and trade licence money wey person dey pay every month no dey change even if she sell plenty oil or small. Na total fixed cost be that because dem no dey depend on how many things she sell.

questions.q: Which of the following is the best example of a variable cost for a bread bakery in Ilorin?
o: Monthly salary of the permanent manager
Annual rent paid for the bakery building
Depreciation charge on the baking oven
Cost of flour and yeast used in baking
questions.e: Flour and yeast are raw materials whose quantity used rises and falls directly with the amount of bread baked, so their cost is variable. Rent, salary and depreciation stay fixed in the short run.
questions.p: Flour and yeast na raw materials wey quantity dey increase or reduce as bread production dey go up or down, so na variable cost. Rent, salary and depreciation na fixed cost for short run.

questions.q: A phone accessories dealer in Computer Village, Lagos, has the following short-run figures: total fixed cost is ₦20,000, and total variable cost at 100 units is ₦30,000. What is the total cost of producing 100 units?
questions.e: Total cost equals total fixed cost plus total variable cost. Adding ₦20,000 and ₦30,000 gives ₦50,000.
questions.p: Total cost na total fixed cost join total variable cost. If you add ₦20,000 and ₦30,000 together, wetin you go get na ₦50,000.

questions.q: A poultry farmer in Oyo State produces 80 crates of eggs at a total cost of ₦96,000, giving an average total cost of ₦1,200 per crate. If his average fixed cost per crate is ₦400, what is his average variable cost per crate?
questions.e: Average total cost equals average fixed cost plus average variable cost. Subtracting ₦400 from ₦1,200 leaves ₦800 as the average variable cost per crate.
questions.p: Average total cost na average fixed cost join average variable cost. When you minus ₦400 from ₦1,200, wetin remain na ₦800 per crate.

questions.q: A shoe exporter in Aba sells 50 pairs of shoes at ₦4,000 each, then sells an additional 10 pairs which raises her total revenue to ₦260,000. What is her marginal revenue per pair for the additional 10 pairs?
questions.e: Initial revenue from 50 pairs is 50 times 4,000, which equals ₦200,000. The extra revenue from the 10 additional pairs is 260,000 minus 200,000, giving ₦60,000, so marginal revenue per pair is 60,000 divided by 10, which is ₦6,000.
questions.p: Initial revenue for 50 pairs na ₦200,000, and extra revenue for the 10 extra pairs na ₦60,000. If you divide ₦60,000 by 10, you go get ₦6,000 as marginal revenue per pair.

questions.q: A grinding mill operator in Sokoto notices that as he grinds more grain beyond a certain point, each extra bag of grain ground adds more to total cost than the previous bag did, even though his machine and shop rent have not changed. This situation best illustrates:
o: Diminishing marginal returns leading to rising marginal cost
A fall in average fixed cost
Rising fixed cost
Constant returns to scale
questions.e: When extra units of a variable input add less and less extra output, the cost of producing each additional unit rises, which is diminishing marginal returns pushing marginal cost upward. Fixed cost is unaffected since rent and machine cost stay constant.
questions.p: When extra input dey give smaller output, the cost to produce extra one dey go up because of diminishing marginal returns. Fixed cost still dey remain the same since rent and machine no change.

questions.q: A furniture workshop in Ogun State produces wooden tables. At 20 tables, total variable cost is ₦140,000; at 21 tables, total variable cost rises to ₦152,000; and at 22 tables, it further rises to ₦166,000. Over this range, what is happening to marginal cost as output increases from 20 to 22 tables?
o: Marginal cost is falling from ₦12,000 to ₦10,000
Marginal cost is falling from ₦14,000 to ₦12,000
Marginal cost is constant at ₦12,000
Marginal cost is rising from ₦12,000 to ₦14,000
questions.e: The change from 20 to 21 tables adds ₦12,000 to cost, while the change from 21 to 22 tables adds ₦14,000. Since each extra table costs more than the one before it, marginal cost is rising.
questions.p: From 20 to 21 tables, the cost increase na ₦12,000, but from 21 to 22 tables, the increase na ₦14,000. Because every extra table dey cost pass the previous one, marginal cost dey rise.

questions.q: Which of the following is a basic assumption of the perfect competition model concerning buyers and sellers?
o: Buyers and sellers have perfect knowledge of market prices
New firms face high barriers before entering the industry
Firms produce differentiated goods to attract customers
A few large firms dominate total output
questions.e: Perfect competition assumes perfect knowledge, so buyers and sellers know prevailing prices and no one can be cheated. The other options describe oligopoly or monopolistic competition, not perfect competition.
questions.p: Perfect competition mean say everybody sabi market price well-well so nobody fit cheat. Other options na for different market like oligopoly or monopolistic competition.

questions.q: A pure monopolist is best described as a firm that:
o: Competes with many small firms selling identical products
Shares the market with three or four other large firms
Sells a product with no close substitute and is the sole supplier in the industry
Produces a slightly different version of a product sold by rivals
questions.e: A pure monopoly exists where one firm is the sole producer of a good that has no close substitute, giving it full control of supply. The other descriptions fit perfect competition, monopolistic competition and oligopoly respectively.
questions.p: Pure monopoly mean only one person dey produce wetin no get close substitute. Na only one person get control of supply for that market.

questions.q: Which of these is the most important barrier that allows a monopoly to persist in an industry?
o: Large number of competing sellers
Exclusive control of a key raw material or legal patent rights
Identical products sold by all firms
Free entry and exit of firms
questions.e: Monopolies survive because of barriers such as sole ownership of resources, patents, or licences that stop other firms from entering. Free entry, many sellers, and identical products are instead features of competitive markets.
questions.p: Monopoly dey stay strong because of barriers like patent or control of raw material. If entry dey free or sellers plenty, na competitive market be that.

questions.q: A key feature that distinguishes oligopoly from monopolistic competition is that oligopoly firms are:
o: Completely independent price takers with no influence on market price
Producers of identical, undifferentiated products only
Free from all barriers to entry into the industry
Mutually interdependent, so each firm's pricing decision affects and is affected by rivals
questions.e: Under oligopoly, few large firms dominate the market, so each firm must consider how rivals will react to its price or output changes, making them mutually interdependent. Monopolistic competition has many firms acting more independently.
questions.p: For oligopoly, few big firms dey so wetin one do go affect the other one. Dem dey mutually interdependent unlike for monopolistic competition.

questions.q: Suppose three firms, Ade Bakery, Bola Foods and Chidi Bread, each produce exactly one-third of all bread sold in a town, and no other firm can enter because of high start-up costs. This market structure is best classified as:
o: Pure monopoly
Oligopoly
Perfect competition
Monopolistic competition
questions.e: A few firms (three) controlling the whole market with entry barriers is the classic description of oligopoly. It is not perfect competition because there are only three sellers, not pure monopoly since there is more than one firm, and not monopolistic competition since entry is blocked.
questions.p: If only three firms dey control market and new ones no fit enter, na oligopoly be that. E no fit be monopoly because dem be three, and e no fit be perfect competition.

questions.q: A monopolist faces the demand function P = 200 - 2Q and has a marginal cost of ₦40 per unit which is constant at all output levels. Given that marginal revenue is MR = 200 - 4Q, what output level maximises the monopolist's profit?
o: 40 units
80 units
50 units
20 units
questions.e: Profit is maximised where marginal revenue equals marginal cost: 200 - 4Q = 40, so 4Q = 160, giving Q = 40 units. Substituting other values into the MR = MC condition does not satisfy the equation.
questions.p: To get maximum profit, you must make sure say MR equal MC. If you solve 200 - 4Q = 40, you go get Q = 40 units.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly compares long-run equilibrium under perfect competition and monopoly?
o: A perfectly competitive firm earns only normal profit in the long run, while a monopolist can continue to earn abnormal profit
Both market structures guarantee zero economic profit in the long run
A monopolist always earns normal profit because entry is free
A perfectly competitive firm can permanently earn abnormal profit due to product differentiation
questions.e: Free entry in perfect competition erodes abnormal profits until only normal profit remains, but barriers to entry allow a monopolist to keep earning abnormal profit indefinitely. The other statements wrongly describe entry conditions or profit outcomes.
questions.p: For perfect competition, free entry dey kill abnormal profit for long run. But for monopoly, barriers dey help them continue to make abnormal profit.

questions.q: A trader in Onitsha buys garri from a farmer for ₦2,000 and sells it to a wholesaler for ₦3,500. The wholesaler then sells it to a retailer for ₦5,000. Which method of calculating national income focuses on summing only the value added at each of these stages?
o: Expenditure method
Income method
Output (value added) method
Residual method
questions.e: The output method adds up the value added at each stage of production to avoid counting the full value of goods more than once. This is different from the income or expenditure approaches, which use wages, profits or spending data instead.
questions.p: Na output method wey dem dey call value added method we dey take add up value for every stage of production so dat we no go count goods twice. E different from income or expenditure method wey dey use wages, profits abi spending.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes Gross National Product (GNP)?
o: The value of goods and services produced within a country's borders by both citizens and foreigners
The value of final goods and services produced by a country's citizens and firms, both at home and abroad
The value of goods and services produced within a country's borders only
The total consumer spending on final goods and services in a country
questions.e: GNP measures output produced by the citizens and firms of a country, whether they are located at home or abroad. GDP, by contrast, measures output produced within the country's borders regardless of who produces it.
questions.p: GNP na di value of goods and services wey citizen and company of one country produce, whether dem dey house abi for foreign land. GDP na just di one wey dem produce inside di country border.

questions.q: Using the income approach, national income is obtained by summing which of the following?
o: The value added at each stage of production
Transfer payments, pensions and subsidies received by households
Consumption, investment, government spending and net exports
Wages, rent, interest and profit earned by factors of production
questions.e: The income method adds up all factor incomes earned in producing goods and services, namely wages, rent, interest and profit. The expenditure method, not the income method, sums consumption, investment, government spending and net exports.
questions.p: Income method dey add all di money wey factors of production earn, like wages, rent, interest, and profit. Na expenditure method dey add consumption, investment, government spending, and net export.

questions.q: A country's Gross National Product is ₦680 billion. If capital consumption (depreciation) for the year is ₦45 billion, what is the Net National Product (NNP)?
o: ₦725 billion
₦45 billion
₦635 billion
₦680 billion
questions.e: Net National Product is obtained by subtracting depreciation from Gross National Product. Therefore 680 billion minus 45 billion gives 635 billion naira.
questions.p: To get Net National Product, you go minus depreciation from Gross National Product. So, if you minus 45 billion naira from 680 billion naira, you go get 635 billion naira.

questions.q: In Economics, national income at factor cost differs from national income at market price mainly because market price figures include which of the following?
o: Depreciation of capital assets
Transfer payments from government
Indirect taxes and subsidies
Net factor income from abroad
questions.e: Market prices include indirect taxes (which raise prices) and subsidies (which lower prices), while factor cost reflects only the payments to factors of production. To move from market price to factor cost, indirect taxes are subtracted and subsidies are added back.
questions.p: Market price dey carry indirect taxes wey dey make price high and subsidies wey dey reduce am, but factor cost na just payment for factors of production. To change market price to factor cost, you must remove indirect taxes and add subsidy.

questions.q: Mr. Danjuma, a retired civil servant in Jos, receives a monthly pension from the government. When economists compute national income using the income method, why is this pension excluded?
o: Because pensions are already counted under government expenditure
Because pensions are a transfer payment and not a payment for current production
Because retired workers are not citizens for national income purposes
Because pensions are taxed at a lower rate than wages
questions.e: Transfer payments like pensions, scholarships and unemployment benefits are not payments for producing goods or services in the current period, so they must be excluded to avoid overstating national income. Only earnings tied to current factor services are counted.
questions.p: Dem no dey count pension inside national income because e be transfer payment and no be payment for work wey person do for dat year. Na only money wey come from current work dem dey count.

questions.q: An economy recorded the following for a given year: Consumption ₦120 billion, Investment ₦40 billion, Government spending ₦60 billion, Exports ₦25 billion, Imports ₦15 billion. Using the expenditure approach, what is the Gross Domestic Product?
o: ₦220 billion
₦260 billion
₦245 billion
₦230 billion
questions.e: GDP by expenditure equals consumption plus investment plus government spending plus net exports (exports minus imports). Adding 120 + 40 + 60 + (25 - 15) gives 230 billion naira.
questions.p: For expenditure approach, you go add consumption, investment, government spending, and net exports where exports minus imports. If you add 120 + 40 + 60 + (25 - 15), your answer na 230 billion naira.

questions.q: A country's Gross Domestic Product is ₦900 billion, net factor income from abroad is negative ₦30 billion, and depreciation is ₦60 billion. What is the Net National Product (NNP) at market price?
o: ₦810 billion
₦930 billion
₦990 billion
₦870 billion
questions.e: First find GNP by adding net factor income from abroad to GDP: 900 + (-30) = 870 billion. Then subtract depreciation to get NNP: 870 - 60 = 810 billion naira.
questions.p: First, find GNP by adding net factor income from abroad to GDP, wey give 870 billion. Den minus depreciation from am to get 810 billion naira as your Net National Product.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the standard functions of money as taught in economics?
o: A store of value
A generator of economic growth
A unit of account
A medium of exchange
questions.e: Money functions as a medium of exchange, a store of value, a unit of account and a standard for deferred payment. Generating economic growth is not a direct function of money itself.
questions.p: Money dey serve as medium of exchange, store of value, and unit of account. But to generate economic growth no be direct function of money itself.

questions.q: A trader prefers to hold cash to take advantage of an expected fall in bond prices so she can buy bonds cheaply later. This illustrates the demand for money for the
o: precautionary motive
transactions motive
speculative motive
unit of account motive
questions.e: Holding money to take advantage of expected future changes in asset prices, such as bond prices or interest rates, is the speculative motive in Keynesian liquidity preference theory. Transactions and precautionary motives relate to everyday spending and emergencies, not speculation.
questions.p: When person hold money sake of say e wan wait make bond price fall so e go fit buy am cheap, na speculative motive be dat. Na Keynesian theory explain say dis one dey different from daily spending or emergency money.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the precautionary demand for money?
o: Money held to meet unforeseen expenses such as sudden hospital bills
Money held purely as a measure of the value of goods
Money held to profit from expected changes in interest rates
Money held to pay for daily purchases like food and transport
questions.e: The precautionary motive refers to holding money to cover unexpected or emergency expenses. The transactions motive covers planned daily spending, while the speculative motive relates to taking advantage of interest rate or bond price changes.
questions.p: Precautionary motive na when you keep money for emergency wey you no plan for, like sudden sickness. E no be for daily chop or to take gamble for interest rate.

questions.q: A country experiences a continuous rise in the general price level mainly because government spends heavily on infrastructure using newly created money without a matching rise in output. This situation best illustrates
o: imported inflation
cost-push inflation
structural inflation
demand-pull inflation
questions.e: When aggregate spending, fueled by excess money creation, rises faster than the economy's output, prices are pulled upward by demand. This is demand-pull inflation, unlike cost-push inflation which arises from rising production costs.
questions.p: If government print too much money and spend am pass wetin the country fit produce, demand go high pass supply. Dis one na demand-pull inflation because the demand dey pull price go up.

questions.q: During a prolonged deflation in an economy, which of the following outcomes is most likely?
o: Erosion of the purchasing power of wages
Consumers delaying purchases in expectation of further price falls
Falling real value of fixed savings held in cash
Rising business profits as prices increase faster than costs
questions.e: Deflation means prices keep falling, so consumers often postpone buying goods hoping prices will drop further, which worsens the economic slowdown. Cash savings actually gain real value and wages gain purchasing power during deflation, so those outcomes are wrong.
questions.p: If price dey fall every time, people go wait make e fall more before dem buy anything. Dis one dey make business slow down because nobody wan spend money quick.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major cause of cost-push inflation in a developing economy like Nigeria?
o: A sharp rise in consumer demand for locally made goods
An increase in government subsidies on fuel
A sudden rise in the price of imported raw materials used by local manufacturers
A reduction in the cash reserve ratio by the central bank
questions.e: Cost-push inflation arises when production costs rise, forcing firms to increase prices. A rise in the cost of imported raw materials directly raises production costs and pushes prices upward, unlike changes in demand or monetary policy which cause demand-pull effects.
questions.p: Cost-push inflation dey happen when the cost to produce goods come high. If raw materials wey dem dey import come cost, company go increase price of goods to cover the cost.

questions.q: Money is generally described as a 'store of value'. This means that money enables its holder to:
o: Exchange goods without the need for a common unit of account
Measure the worth of different goods using one common unit
Settle debts that are due immediately
Transfer purchasing power from the present to the future
questions.e: Store of value means money can be kept and used later without losing all its purchasing power, allowing wealth to be carried forward in time. Measuring worth describes the unit of account function, not store of value.
questions.p: Store of value mean say you fit keep money for future use without e lose value. E allow you carry your wealth go front. Measuring worth na unit of account function, no be store of value.

questions.q: Which of the following is a basic qualitative characteristic that good money must possess so that it does not spoil or lose value while being kept?
o: Durability
Divisibility
Scarcity
Portability
questions.e: Durability means money must be able to last and withstand wear and tear without deteriorating in quality or value over time. Divisibility, portability and scarcity are other desirable qualities but do not specifically address not spoiling while stored.
questions.p: Durability mean say money must fit last long without spoil or tear. If money no durable, e go lose value quick. Other qualities like divisibility or scarcity no mean say money no go spoil.

questions.q: A market woman in Onitsha keeps a fixed amount of cash daily, separate from her trading capital, purely to pay for an emergency such as sudden transport breakdown or unexpected medical treatment. This holding of money illustrates the:
o: Precautionary motive
Store of value motive
Speculative motive
Transaction motive
questions.e: Holding money to meet unforeseen emergencies or unexpected expenses is the precautionary motive for demanding money. It is different from the transaction motive, which covers planned day-to-day spending.
questions.p: When you keep money for emergency wey you no expect, na precautionary motive be dat. E different from transaction motive wey be for your daily market spending. You dey prepare for bad belle things wey fit happen.

questions.q: A galloping inflation that is left unchecked and keeps accelerating until money loses almost all its value, forcing people to resort to trading goods for goods, is best described as:
o: Creeping inflation
Stagflation
Hyperinflation
Reflation
questions.e: Hyperinflation is an extremely rapid and uncontrollable rise in prices that destroys the value of money, often leading to a return to barter. Creeping inflation is mild, while stagflation combines inflation with stagnant output.
questions.p: Hyperinflation na when price of things dey rise too fast until money no get value again. People go come start to dey swap goods for goods. E different from creeping inflation wey dey slow.

questions.q: Suppose the Central Bank of Nigeria reduces the Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) sharply to encourage borrowing, while government also increases spending on infrastructure using newly created money, without any matching rise in output. Based on monetary theory, the most likely combined effect on the general price level is that it will:
o: Fall sharply due to reduced velocity of circulation
Rise, because increased money supply and spending push demand beyond available output
Remain stable, since government spending balances money supply growth
Fall, because lower interest rates reduce money demand
questions.e: Cutting interest rates encourages more borrowing and spending, while new money financing government expenditure further raises aggregate demand. With output unchanged, too much money chasing few goods leads to demand-pull inflation, so prices rise.
questions.p: If interest rate low and government dey spend plenty new money, demand go pass supply. When too much money dey chase few goods, price must go up. Na demand-pull inflation be dis.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why barter trade became inconvenient and eventually led to the invention of money as a medium of exchange?
o: Barter trade was banned by early governments for security reasons
Goods in a barter system could not be measured in any unit at all
Goods exchanged under barter always had equal value
Barter required a double coincidence of wants between trading parties
questions.e: Under barter, a person wanting to exchange goods had to find someone who both had what they wanted and wanted what they had, which was difficult. Money solved this problem by serving as a common medium accepted by everyone.
questions.p: Barter trade hard because you must find person wey get wetin you want, and wey also want wetin you get. We call am double coincidence of wants. Money come solve dis wahala because everybody dey accept am.

questions.q: A commercial bank in Lagos has total deposits of ₦20,000,000 and the Central Bank of Nigeria fixes the required reserve ratio at 25%. What is the maximum amount the bank can give out as loans?
questions.e: Required reserve is 25% of 20,000,000 = 5,000,000. The bank must keep this as reserve, so it can lend out the balance of 15,000,000.
questions.p: If you calculate 25% of 20,000,000, you go get 5,000,000 as reserve. The bank must keep that one, so dem fit lend out the remaining 15,000,000.

questions.q: Which of the following is a function of the Central Bank of Nigeria but NOT a function of commercial banks?
o: Providing safe custody for valuables
Granting loans and overdrafts
Issuing legal tender currency
Accepting deposits from customers
questions.e: Only the Central Bank has the sole right to print and issue the national currency. Commercial banks accept deposits, grant loans and keep valuables safe for customers.
questions.p: Na only Central Bank get power to print and issue money for Nigeria. Commercial banks dey only collect deposit and give loan to people.

questions.q: In the Nigerian financial system, which of the following best distinguishes the capital market from the money market?
o: The capital market deals in instruments of less than one year, while the money market deals in long-term instruments
The capital market deals in long-term instruments like shares and debentures, while the money market deals in short-term instruments
The capital market is regulated by the Central Bank while the money market is unregulated
The capital market only operates in Lagos while the money market operates nationwide
questions.e: The capital market trades long-term financial instruments such as shares, bonds and debentures with maturities of more than one year. The money market, on the other hand, deals in short-term instruments like treasury bills and commercial papers.
questions.p: Capital market dey handle long-term things like shares wey go last pass one year. Money market na for short-term things like treasury bills.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why the Central Bank of Nigeria is described as the 'banker's bank'?
o: It prints currency notes for use by commercial banks
It sets the prices of goods sold by commercial banks
It accepts deposits directly from the general public
It keeps the accounts of commercial banks and lends to them in times of need
questions.e: The Central Bank is called the banker's bank because commercial banks keep their reserves with it and can borrow from it when they are short of funds. It does not deal directly with the general public the way commercial banks do.
questions.p: Dem dey call Central Bank banker's bank because commercial banks dey keep their money there. If commercial banks need help, na Central Bank dem dey run go meet.

questions.q: A company wishes to raise long-term capital by selling new shares directly to the investing public for the first time. Which capital market institution would it primarily make use of?
o: The discount house
The secondary market
The money market
The primary market
questions.e: New securities are sold for the first time in the primary market, where companies raise fresh long-term capital directly from investors. The secondary market only allows trading of already-issued securities among investors.
questions.p: If company wan sell new shares for the first time, na primary market dem dey go. Secondary market na only for shares wey people don already buy before.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major function of the Nigerian Stock Exchange (now Nigerian Exchange Group) in the capital market?
o: Facilitating the buying and selling of existing shares and bonds
Fixing the minimum rediscount rate for treasury bills
Providing short-term loans to commercial banks
Printing and issuing the national currency
questions.e: The stock exchange is a secondary market where already-issued shares and bonds are bought and sold by investors. Issuing currency and setting rediscount rates are functions of the Central Bank, not the stock exchange.
questions.p: Stock exchange na secondary market where people dey buy and sell shares wey don dey exist before. Na Central Bank dey print money and fix rate, no be stock exchange.

questions.q: A commercial bank's major source of income is the
o: profit from printing new currency notes for circulation
difference between interest charged on loans and interest paid on deposits
fees collected from the Central Bank for keeping reserves
commission earned on cheque clearing services
questions.e: Commercial banks earn most of their income from the interest rate spread, that is, charging a higher interest on loans than they pay on customers' deposits. Printing currency is solely a Central Bank function.
questions.p: Commercial bank dey make their main money from interest rate difference, wey mean say dem charge higher interest on loans pass wetin dem dey pay depositor. Na Central Bank dey print currency.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a treasury bill as a money market instrument?
o: A certificate representing part-ownership of a public limited company
A long-term bond issued by state governments to fund infrastructure projects
A short-term, low-risk debt instrument issued by government to finance temporary budget shortfalls
A document used by banks to transfer ownership of fixed assets
questions.e: A treasury bill is a short-term government security, usually maturing within a year, used to bridge short-term financing gaps. It is a debt instrument, not an ownership share like equity.
questions.p: Treasury bill na short-term government debt instrument wey dey mature within one year to cover small budget gap. E no be company equity share.

questions.q: A commercial bank in Enugu has total deposits of ₦45,000,000. If the Central Bank of Nigeria sets the required reserve ratio at 15%, what is the maximum amount the bank can give out as loans, assuming it keeps exactly the required reserve and lends out the rest?
questions.e: The required reserve is 15% of 45,000,000, which equals 6,750,000. Subtracting this from total deposits leaves 38,250,000 available for loans.
questions.p: Required reserve na 15% of ₦45,000,000, wey be ₦6,750,000. When you subtract am from total deposit, you go get ₦38,250,000 wey bank fit give out as loan.

questions.q: The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) in Nigeria performs which of the following roles in the capital market?
o: Regulating and supervising the issuance and trading of securities to protect investors
Granting short-term overdrafts to deposit money banks
Setting the exchange rate between the naira and foreign currencies
Collecting company income tax on behalf of the Federal Government
questions.e: The SEC regulates the Nigerian capital market, approving new securities and supervising operators to protect investors from fraud. Exchange rate management and tax collection are not its functions.
questions.p: SEC na him dey regulate capital market and protect investors from fraud. Na different agency dey collect tax and manage foreign exchange rate.

questions.q: A key difference between the money market and the capital market is that the money market deals in instruments with maturity periods of
o: more than ten years, while the capital market deals in instruments of less than one year
less than one year, while the capital market deals in instruments of more than one year
exactly five years, while the capital market has no fixed maturity period
more than one year, while the capital market deals in instruments of less than one year
questions.e: The money market trades short-term instruments such as treasury bills that mature within a year, while the capital market trades long-term instruments like shares and debentures with maturities exceeding one year.
questions.p: Money market dey deal with short-term instruments like treasury bills wey dey mature under one year, while capital market dey handle long-term instruments like shares.

questions.q: If the Central Bank of Nigeria raises the minimum rediscount rate (monetary policy rate), the most likely effect on commercial banks' lending rates and the volume of credit in the economy is that
o: lending rates fall and credit expands
lending rates remain unchanged while credit expands
lending rates rise but credit remains unchanged
lending rates rise and credit contracts
questions.e: A higher monetary policy rate raises the cost at which banks borrow from the Central Bank, so banks in turn raise their own lending rates, making loans more expensive and reducing the volume of credit demanded. This is a standard tool for tightening monetary policy.
questions.p: If Central Bank increase monetary policy rate, loan interest go high and people go borrow less money. Na way to control inflation.

questions.q: A bank has deposits of ₦60,000,000 and the Central Bank operates a required reserve ratio of 10%. If the Central Bank unexpectedly raises the ratio to 20%, by how much must the bank increase its reserves to comply, assuming deposits remain the same?
questions.e: At 10% the bank needed 6,000,000 in reserves, and at 20% it needs 12,000,000. The additional reserve required is the difference, which is 6,000,000.
questions.p: At 10% reserve, bank need ₦6,000,000, but at 20% reserve, dem need ₦12,000,000. The extra money wey dem must add na ₦6,000,000.

questions.q: A medium-term development plan in Nigeria typically covers a period of:
o: 3 to 5 years
20 to 25 years
1 year
10 to 15 years
questions.e: Medium-term plans usually run for 3 to 5 years, long enough to execute specific projects but short enough to review progress regularly. Short-term plans are annual, while long-term plans (perspective plans) run for 10 years or more.
questions.p: Medium-term plan dey usually last for 3 to 5 years. E long reach to finish project but e short enough make dem review am. Short-term plan na one year, while long-term plan dey pass 10 years.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major pre-requisite for successful economic planning in a developing country like Nigeria?
o: Absence of a planning body
Complete elimination of the private sector
Total dependence on foreign aid
Availability of reliable statistical data
questions.e: Accurate and reliable data on population, resources and past performance are needed to set realistic targets and allocate resources properly. Without good data, planners cannot forecast correctly or evaluate outcomes.
questions.p: To plan well, you need correct data about population and resources. Without better data, planners no fit forecast well or know if dem dey succeed. Na why reliable statistics dey very important.

questions.q: One major way in which planning helps a developing economy is by:
o: Making prices rise uncontrollably to attract investment
Preventing the government from participating in any economic activity
Channelling scarce resources into priority sectors to achieve set national goals
Allowing resources to be allocated purely by market forces without direction
questions.e: Planning enables a country to direct its limited resources deliberately towards sectors considered most important for growth, such as agriculture, education or infrastructure. This directed allocation helps achieve specific national objectives within a set period.
questions.p: Planning help country direct im scarce resources go where e dey important, like agriculture or school. Dis one help government achieve national goals quick. E no be just market forces dey decide everything.

questions.q: A country's Gross National Income was ₦45 trillion when its population was 150 million people. If the population rises to 180 million while the Gross National Income stays the same, what happens to income per capita?
o: It rises because the national income is constant
It falls from ₦300,000 to ₦250,000 per person
It remains unchanged at ₦300,000
It falls from ₦300,000 to ₦200,000 per person
questions.e: Income per capita before is 45 trillion divided by 150 million, which equals ₦300,000. After the population rises to 180 million, it becomes 45 trillion divided by 180 million, which equals ₦250,000, showing a fall in living standards despite constant national income.
questions.p: Before, ₦45 trillion divided by 150 million give ₦300,000 per person. When population reach 180 million, the same ₦45 trillion come divide by 180 million, e come drop to ₦250,000. So, income per capita don fall.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why rapid economic growth may NOT automatically lead to economic development in a country?
o: Development requires that national income fall over time
Growth figures are always inaccurate and cannot be trusted
Growth can occur alongside worsening income inequality and poor living standards for the majority
Growth only happens in developed countries, not developing ones
questions.e: A country's output and income can rise significantly, yet if the benefits are concentrated among a few people while poverty, unemployment and inequality persist for the majority, genuine development has not occurred. This is why growth is necessary but not sufficient for development.
questions.p: Economic growth fit happen but development no go follow if poverty and inequality still dey. If only small people dey enjoy the money while majority dey suffer, that one no be development. Growth alone no be enough.

questions.q: A key reason why many national development plans in Nigeria have failed to achieve their targets is:
o: Inadequate implementation due to corruption, policy inconsistency and shortage of funds
Excessive involvement of the private sector in all planning decisions
Overabundance of skilled manpower for plan execution
Too much emphasis on long-term perspective planning alone
questions.e: Even well-designed plans often fail because of corruption, frequent changes in government policy, insufficient funding and poor implementation strategies. These challenges prevent set targets from being met regardless of how good the plan looks on paper.
questions.p: Many plans for Nigeria dey fail because of corruption and lack of money. Sometimes government policy dey change anyhow, so implementation come hard. Even if the plan fine for paper, these problems dey stop am from working.

questions.q: A country's per capita income is ₦280,000. If its Gross National Product is ₦56 trillion, what is the population of the country?
o: 250 million
150 million
220 million
200 million
questions.e: Per capita income equals GNP divided by population, so population equals GNP divided by per capita income. 56,000,000,000,000 divided by 280,000 gives 200,000,000.
questions.p: To get population, you divide GNP by per capita income. If you divide 56 trillion by 280,000, you go get 200 million people.

questions.q: In Rostow's stages of economic growth, the stage in which a society invests heavily in a few leading sectors and experiences rapid, self-sustaining growth driven by technological change is called the:
o: Traditional society stage
Take-off stage
Pre-condition for take-off stage
Age of high mass consumption
questions.e: The take-off stage is marked by rapid growth concentrated in a few leading sectors, supported by rising investment rates and technological advancement. This stage leads the economy into self-sustained growth.
questions.p: Take-off stage na when economy start to grow fast because of new technology and big investment. Na this stage dey make growth continue by itself.

questions.q: One of the major functions of the National Planning Commission (now Ministry of Budget and National Planning) in Nigeria is to:
o: Collect personal income tax from workers directly
Fix the prices of all goods sold in the market
Print and issue the national currency
Coordinate and monitor the implementation of national development plans
questions.e: The planning body is responsible for designing, coordinating and monitoring development plans across the country. Printing currency and collecting personal tax are duties of other agencies like the Central Bank and tax authorities.
questions.p: The main work of the planning body na to arrange and watch how national development plans dey work. Other agencies like Central Bank dey handle money matter, no be them.

questions.q: A major difference between economic growth and economic development is that economic development:
o: Involves qualitative improvements in welfare, in addition to quantitative increase in output
Is measured only in monetary terms while growth is not
Can occur without any increase in national output whatsoever
Refers strictly to a rise in capital goods production
questions.e: Economic development goes beyond a rise in output to include improvements in living standards, health, education and overall welfare. Growth alone focuses only on the quantitative increase in output or income.
questions.p: Economic development no be just to get more money, e include better life for people like good health and school. Economic growth na just to see say output increase.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes 'perspective planning' as used in economic planning?
o: A plan drawn up only for a single sector of the economy
A plan that is reviewed and extended by one year after every year
A long-term plan, usually 15 to 25 years, that sets broad goals guiding shorter plans
A plan lasting less than one year designed for emergency spending
questions.e: Perspective planning is a long-term framework, often spanning 15 to 25 years, which sets out broad development goals within which shorter and medium-term plans are formulated. It is not an annual or rolling plan, which are shorter in scope.
questions.p: Perspective planning na long-term plan wey fit last for 15 to 25 years. E dey show the big goals wey go guide the short-term plans.

questions.q: One major obstacle to effective economic planning in many West African countries is:
o: Excessive availability of reliable statistical data
Too much political stability disrupting plan continuity
Overabundance of trained manpower for plan implementation
Inadequate and unreliable data for accurate plan formulation
questions.e: Many West African countries struggle with poor data collection systems, making it difficult to formulate and evaluate development plans accurately. A shortage, not excess, of reliable data and trained manpower is the real challenge.
questions.p: Many countries for West Africa no get correct data to plan well. Because the data no dey reliable, e dey hard to make good plans.

questions.q: Agriculture contributes to the Nigerian economy in several ways. Which of the following is NOT a recognized contribution of agriculture to national development?
o: Direct provision of crude oil revenue to the government
Generation of foreign exchange through export of cash crops
Provision of employment for the rural population
Provision of raw materials for agro-based industries
questions.e: Crude oil revenue comes from the petroleum sector, not agriculture. Agriculture instead supplies raw materials, employment, and export earnings.
questions.p: Na petroleum sector dey bring crude oil money, no be agriculture. Agriculture dey provide food, raw materials for factory, and work for people.

questions.q: A farming system in Nigeria in which crops like maize, cassava and melon are planted together on the same plot at the same time is known as
o: Crop rotation
Bush fallowing
Mixed cropping
Shifting cultivation
questions.e: Mixed cropping involves growing two or more different crops on the same piece of land simultaneously to maximize land use and reduce risk of total crop failure.
questions.p: Mixed cropping na when farmer plant different crops for one land at the same time. E dey help make land use dey effective and reduce risk if one crop fail.

questions.q: One major problem of agricultural marketing in Nigeria is the activity of middlemen. This problem mainly leads to
o: Improved storage facilities at the farm level
Lower prices paid to farmers and higher prices paid by final consumers
Reduction in the bulk of produce available for export
Increased income for farmers due to competition among buyers
questions.e: Middlemen buy cheaply from farmers and sell at a markup to consumers, so farmers earn less while consumers pay more, widening the marketing margin.
questions.p: Middlemen dey buy farm produce cheap from farmer, come sell am high to consumer. This one dey make farmer gain small money while consumer dey pay too much.

questions.q: The Nigerian government established commodity marketing boards in the past mainly to
o: Construct feeder roads linking farms to urban markets
Provide free farm inputs such as fertilizer to all farmers
Train extension workers to teach modern farming methods
Fix and stabilize producer prices of export crops and pay farmers afterwards
questions.e: Marketing boards were set up to buy export crops from farmers at fixed prices, sell them abroad, and stabilize farmers' incomes against price fluctuations.
questions.p: Marketing boards bin dey fix price so farmer go know wetin dem go get. Dem dey buy export crops from farmer and sell am outside to keep price stable.

questions.q: A key reason why mechanized farming has remained low in many parts of rural Nigeria is that
o: Landholdings are mostly small and fragmented, making machine use difficult
The government has banned the use of tractors nationwide
Nigerian soils are too fertile for machines to be used
Farmers prefer importing finished food products instead
questions.e: Due to the land tenure system, farm plots are often small, scattered and fragmented, making it uneconomical and difficult to deploy large machinery effectively.
questions.p: Small and scattered land no dey allow big machine like tractor to work well. Because the land no dey big, e no dey easy to use modern machine for farm.

questions.q: A cooperative society of maize farmers in Kaduna recorded a total farm output worth ₦5,400,000 in a season. If labour and input costs took up 3/5 of this value, what was the net value (profit) realised by the cooperative?
questions.e: Costs equal 3/5 of 5,400,000 which is 3,240,000. Subtracting this from total output gives 5,400,000 minus 3,240,000 equals 2,160,000 as net value.
questions.p: If cost na 3/5 of ₦5,400,000, e mean say cost na ₦3,240,000. When you remove that cost from the total ₦5,400,000, you go get ₦2,160,000 as profit.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why the agricultural sector's share of Nigeria's GDP has generally declined relative to the services sector over recent decades, even though agriculture still employs many people?
o: All farmers have moved permanently into manufacturing jobs
The services and oil sectors have grown faster in value, reducing agriculture's relative share
Government has stopped collecting agricultural statistics
Agricultural output has fallen to zero across the country
questions.e: A sector's share of GDP can fall simply because other sectors like services and oil grow faster in monetary value, even if agricultural output itself is rising in absolute terms.
questions.p: Even if agriculture dey grow, other sectors like oil and services dey grow pass am for money. That one dey make agriculture share for GDP look small.

questions.q: The 'River Basin Development Authorities' were established in Nigeria mainly to
o: Develop irrigation facilities and water resources for agricultural use
Supervise the stock exchange activities of agro-allied companies
Issue import licences for agricultural machinery
Regulate the exchange rate of the naira
questions.e: River Basin Development Authorities were created to harness water resources, provide irrigation, and support all-year-round farming in different parts of Nigeria.
questions.p: River Basin Development Authorities dey help manage water for farm. Dem dey provide irrigation so say farmer fit plant crop even when rain no fall.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes 'industrialisation' as used in economics?
o: The movement of people from urban areas to rural areas in search of farmland
The process of increasing agricultural output through mechanised farming
The process by which an economy transforms from being primarily agrarian to one dominated by manufacturing and allied activities
The process of exporting raw materials to earn foreign exchange
questions.e: Industrialisation refers to the structural shift of an economy from reliance on agriculture and raw materials towards manufacturing, processing and related industrial activities. The other options describe unrelated or opposite processes.
questions.p: Industrialisation na wen economy move from farming go enter manufacturing and factory work. E mean say country dey shift focus from raw materials go produce finished goods.

questions.q: A footwear manufacturing company in Aba decides to also set up its own tannery to process raw hides into leather, instead of buying leather from other suppliers. This type of business expansion is called:
o: Lateral integration
Forward vertical integration
Horizontal integration
Backward vertical integration
