questions.e: Backward vertical integration occurs when a firm expands towards an earlier stage of production, such as a footwear maker owning a tannery that supplies its raw material. Forward integration would instead move towards the final consumer, such as owning retail shops.
questions.p: Backward vertical integration happen wen company go back to control wetin dem dey use work, like shoe maker wey come get tannery. If dem move go front to sell direct to people, na forward integration be dat.

questions.q: Okonkwo and three friends want to start a business that requires huge capital for machinery, and they wish to limit their personal risk so that their private houses and cars cannot be seized to pay business debts beyond what they invested. Which form of business organisation best suits their need?
o: Cooperative thrift society
Private limited liability company
Sole proprietorship
Partnership with unlimited liability
questions.e: A private limited liability company gives owners limited liability, meaning they can only lose the amount they invested as shares, protecting their personal property. Sole proprietorship and ordinary partnership typically carry unlimited liability.
questions.p: Private limited liability company dey protect person property if business get debt. You go only lose wetin you put inside the business as share, your personal house no go dey for risk.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major contribution of small-scale industries to the Nigerian economy?
o: They are mainly owned and controlled by foreign investors
They generate substantial employment and make use of local raw materials
They require very large amounts of capital before they can start operating
They produce mostly for export markets and ignore local demand
questions.e: Small-scale industries are valued because they create jobs for many Nigerians and often use locally sourced raw materials, promoting grassroots economic development. They usually need relatively low capital and serve local markets.
questions.p: Small-scale industries dey help Nigeria economy well well because dem dey give plenty people work. Dem also dey use local materials wey dey ground for inside country.

questions.q: A furniture-making company situated in Benin City finds that most of its skilled carpenters, timber suppliers and furniture buyers are already clustered in that same city, making it easier and cheaper to operate there than elsewhere. This advantage of the location is best described as:
o: Economies of large scale production
Diseconomies of scale
External economies of localisation
Economies of scale
questions.e: External economies of localisation arise when firms in the same industry cluster together in one area and jointly benefit from shared skilled labour, suppliers and markets, even though each firm remains independent. This differs from economies of scale, which relate to a single firm's internal size of operation.
questions.p: External economies of localisation happen wen companies for same line of work gather for one place. Dem all dey benefit from shared skilled workers and suppliers wey dey near dem.

questions.q: A cooperative society in a farming community in Benue State pools money from its members and uses it to grant loans to members at low interest rates for buying farm inputs. This type of cooperative is best classified as a:
o: Consumers' cooperative society
Producers' cooperative society
Marketing cooperative society
Thrift and credit cooperative society
questions.e: A thrift and credit cooperative mainly collects savings from members and gives out loans to them at favourable rates. Producers' and marketing cooperatives instead focus on joint production and selling of goods respectively.
questions.p: Thrift and credit cooperative na group wey members dey save money come borrow am for low interest. Na dis one dey help farmers get money to buy wetin dem need for farm.

questions.q: Which of the following is an essential feature that distinguishes a public corporation from a private limited liability company in Nigeria?
o: A public corporation is established by an Act of government and is usually owned and financed by the state
A public corporation's profits are shared only among a few private shareholders
A public corporation must have at least two but not more than fifty shareholders
A public corporation sells its shares freely to members of the public on the stock exchange
questions.e: Public corporations like the Nigerian Ports Authority are created by government legislation, owned by the state and run for public interest, unlike private limited companies which are privately owned by shareholders. Selling shares on the stock exchange is instead a feature of public limited companies, not public corporations.
questions.p: Public corporation na government setup am through law and na state dey own am. Private limited company na private people get am, so dem no be the same.

questions.q: An iron and steel company requires 5000 tonnes of iron ore to produce 1000 tonnes of finished steel products in a month, because a large proportion of the ore's weight is lost as waste during processing. Based purely on this weight-loss consideration, the company should ideally locate its factory:
o: Near the source of the iron ore deposits
At the capital city where government offices are located
Near the market where the steel products will be sold
At the seaport used for importing machinery
questions.e: Since the raw material loses a lot of weight during processing, it is cheaper to transport the lighter finished product to the market than to transport the heavier raw material over long distances. This is why weight-losing, bulky raw materials pull industries towards the source of the raw material rather than the market.
questions.p: If raw material heavy well well and e go lose weight during production, e better make you build factory near where you dey get the material. E go cost you less money to carry the finished product go market.

questions.q: Nigeria's crude oil is generally classified as 'light' and 'sweet'. What does the term 'sweet' refer to in this classification?
o: A high specific gravity of the crude oil
A high wax content that solidifies at room temperature
A low sulphur content in the crude oil
A high viscosity that makes refining difficult
questions.e: Sweet crude oil contains a low percentage of sulphur, which makes it easier and cheaper to refine into petroleum products. Light refers to its low density, a separate property from sweetness.
questions.p: Sweet crude oil get small small sulphur inside am, wey dey make am easy and cheap to refine to petroleum products. 'Light' mean say e get low density, wey be another thing entirely from sweetness.

questions.q: Which of these is the main reason the petroleum industry, unlike agriculture, has not created widespread direct employment for Nigerians?
o: Oil exploration sites are located only in densely populated areas
The government restricts the number of workers allowed in the industry
Petroleum products are mainly consumed locally and not exported
The industry is capital-intensive and highly mechanized rather than labour-intensive
questions.e: Petroleum extraction and refining rely heavily on machinery, technology and skilled technical staff rather than large numbers of workers. This makes the sector capital-intensive, unlike labour-intensive agriculture which employs many more people.
questions.p: Petroleum work dey rely well well on heavy machines, technology and skilled workers instead of plenty people. E make the sector capital-intensive, unlike agriculture wey dey employ plenty labour.

questions.q: A barrel of crude oil sold by Nigeria is priced at $80. If the naira-dollar exchange rate is ₦1500 to $1, what is the naira value of 5,000 barrels exported in a day?
questions.e: Total dollar value is 5000 multiplied by 80, giving 400,000 dollars. Converting at ₦1500 per dollar gives 400,000 times 1500, which equals ₦600,000,000.
questions.p: Total dollar value na 5000 times 80, wey give 400,000 dollars. When you change am at ₦1500 per dollar, e go give 400,000 times 1500, wey come equal ₦600,000,000.

questions.q: In the Nigerian petroleum industry value chain, which of the following activities belongs to the 'midstream' sector?
o: Retailing of petrol at filling stations to consumers
Transportation, refining, and storage of petroleum products
Exploration and drilling of crude oil wells
Prospecting for new oil fields using seismic surveys
questions.e: The midstream sector covers processing, refining, transportation and storage of crude oil and its products. Exploration belongs to upstream, while retail sale to final consumers belongs to downstream.
questions.p: Midstream sector cover how dem dey process, refine, transport and keep crude oil and im products. Exploration na upstream, while selling petrol for filling station na downstream.

questions.q: One major reason successive Nigerian governments have found it difficult to fully deregulate the downstream petroleum sector is that
o: Private investors are legally barred from owning refineries in Nigeria
Deregulation would reduce the price of crude oil on the international market
Deregulation would immediately increase the volume of crude oil reserves
Removing fuel subsidies tends to raise transport costs and general prices, causing public resistance
questions.e: Subsidy removal usually leads to higher pump prices for petrol, which raises transportation costs and the general price level. This often triggers strong public opposition, making full deregulation politically difficult.
questions.p: When dem remove subsidy, transport fare and market prices go high up. This one dey vex people plenty,y wey make am hard for government to fully deregulate the sector.

questions.q: Which international organisation does Nigeria belong to that coordinates production quotas among major crude oil exporting countries to influence world oil prices?
o: Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC)
Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS)
World Trade Organisation (WTO)
African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA)
questions.e: Nigeria is a member of OPEC, a group of oil-exporting nations that agree on production quotas to regulate supply and stabilise international oil prices. The other bodies deal with regional integration or general trade, not oil quotas.
questions.p: Nigeria join OPEC, na him be the group of oil countries wey dey control how much oil dem dey produce to help balance world oil price. The other organisations no dey control oil quota.

questions.q: A Nigerian state government depends on crude oil revenue for 90% of its budget. If world oil prices suddenly fall sharply, which of the following best describes the most likely immediate effect on the state's economy?
o: A proportional increase in the state's non-oil tax revenue to cover the gap
An automatic rise in the state's agricultural output to compensate for the loss
A significant shortfall in revenue leading to difficulty funding planned projects and salaries
An immediate increase in the state's foreign exchange reserves
questions.e: Since the state depends heavily on oil revenue, a sharp fall in oil prices directly reduces its income, making it hard to meet budgeted spending such as salaries and projects. The other outcomes do not happen automatically just because oil prices fall.
questions.p: Because the state dey rely well well on oil money, if oil price fall, money no go enter again to pay salary and build projects. The other options no dey happen just like that because oil price fall.

questions.q: Nigeria's continued dependence on imported refined petroleum products, despite being a major crude oil producer, best illustrates which of the following economic problems?
o: Excess refining capacity leading to surplus petrol for export
Strong forward linkages from crude oil into local manufacturing
Overdependence on primary exports with weak domestic value addition
A permanent shortage of crude oil reserves within the country
questions.e: Nigeria exports mostly crude oil, a raw primary product, while importing refined products because local refining capacity is insufficient. This shows weak value addition and overdependence on exporting unprocessed resources.
questions.p: Nigeria dey export raw crude oil but dey import refined fuel back because our refineries no strong. E show say we overdepend on primary export without processing our things well for house.

questions.q: The petroleum industry in Nigeria is often described as an 'enclave' industry because it
o: is located only in the Niger Delta region
is wholly owned by foreign multinational companies
produces only crude oil for export and nothing else
has very weak linkages with other sectors of the domestic economy
questions.e: An enclave industry operates almost independently of the rest of the economy, buying few local inputs and creating few jobs outside itself. The Nigerian oil industry is capital-intensive and imports most of its equipment, so it has weak backward and forward linkages with agriculture and manufacturing.
questions.p: Enclave industry dey operate like say e no send other sectors of economy, and e no dey buy many local things or create plenty jobs. Nigeria oil industry dey import most of im equipment, so e get weak backward and forward connection with agriculture and manufacturing.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes 'bitumen' as a natural resource found in Nigeria?
o: A solid mineral used mainly for road construction and roofing materials
A precious metal mined for jewellery making
A type of agricultural raw material processed into fuel
A gaseous resource flared alongside crude oil production
questions.e: Bitumen is a thick, sticky, semi-solid form of petroleum found in commercial quantities in Ondo State, Nigeria. It is mainly used in road construction (asphalt) and waterproofing materials.
questions.p: Bitumen na thick, sticky petroleum wey dem dey see plenty for Ondo State. Dem dey use am mainly to make road, like asphalt, and for waterproofing materials.

questions.q: A country is said to have 'proven reserves' of crude oil when the quantity of oil
o: is locked permanently underground and can never be recovered
can be extracted profitably with current technology and existing economic conditions
has already been pumped out and sold in the world market
is estimated to exist but cannot yet be confirmed by any survey
questions.e: Proven reserves refer to the amount of oil that geological and engineering data show can be recovered with reasonable certainty under current technology and prices. This is different from oil already extracted or merely speculated to exist.
questions.p: Proven reserves na that oil amount wey science and machine show say dem fit pack out well well with current technology and price. E different from oil wey dem don already bring out or the one wey dem just dey guess say dey ground.

questions.q: A Nigerian oil exploration company estimates that an oil field contains 500 million barrels of crude oil, but only 60% of this amount can be economically recovered using current drilling technology. What is the recoverable quantity, in million barrels?
questions.e: Recoverable quantity equals 60% of 500 million barrels, which is 0.6 multiplied by 500 giving 300 million barrels. This shows how proven reserves differ from total estimated deposits.
questions.p: To find the recoverable quantity, you go calculate 60% of 500 million barrels, which mean 0.6 times 500. Dat one give you 300 million barrels.

questions.q: Which of the following is the main reason crude oil is referred to as a 'wasting asset' in economic analysis?
o: It spoils quickly in storage tanks before it can be refined
It generates no revenue for the government that owns it
Its price falls continuously every year without exception
It is a non-renewable resource that depletes permanently once extracted and used
questions.e: A wasting asset is one whose stock diminishes as it is used, since nature does not replace it within a human timescale. Crude oil fits this description because every barrel extracted reduces the fixed total reserve permanently.
questions.p: Wasting asset mean something wey dey finish as people dey use am, because nature no dey quick replace am. Crude oil be like dat because once dem pack one barrel komot, that particular reserve don reduce forever.

questions.q: During the global oil boom of the 1970s, large revenues flowed into Nigeria, but agriculture was neglected and the economy became overly dependent on oil exports. Economists refer to this general phenomenon as
o: trade liberalisation
the multiplier effect
the Dutch disease
a balance of payments surplus
questions.e: Dutch disease describes a situation where a resource boom in one sector (like oil) causes neglect and decline of other productive sectors (like agriculture) due to currency appreciation and resource shift. Nigeria's oil boom years are a classic example of this phenomenon.
questions.p: Dutch disease mean when plenty money from one natural resource like oil make government forget agriculture and other sector. Nigeria experience dis kind thing for the 1970s oil boom time.

questions.q: The Petroleum Industry Act (PIA) was enacted in Nigeria primarily to
o: ban all foreign companies from operating in the Nigerian oil sector
provide a modern legal, regulatory, fiscal and governance framework for the petroleum industry
transfer ownership of all oil wells directly to host communities
fix the pump price of petrol permanently across the country
questions.e: The Petroleum Industry Act was designed to overhaul outdated laws governing the sector, creating clearer rules on licensing, taxation, host community benefits, and institutional oversight. It did not ban foreign firms or fix pump prices permanently, but rather modernised governance of the whole industry.
questions.p: The Petroleum Industry Act na law wey dem bring to clean up and update how oil business suppose run for Nigeria. E clear rules for tax, license, and how government go manage the whole petroleum sector well.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a 'census' as distinct from general population estimates used in national planning?
o: A complete and official count of every person in a country carried out at regular intervals
An estimate of population based only on birth registration records
A sample survey of a small fraction of households used to project national figures
A record of only the working-age citizens registered for tax purposes
questions.e: A census is a complete, official enumeration of every person in a country, usually conducted periodically. Estimates or sample surveys are different from a full head count.
questions.p: Census na proper counting of everybody for inside country wey dem dey do every time. E different from sample survey wey dem dey use small people take guess.

questions.q: According to the Malthusian theory of population, which situation results when population growth outstrips food supply growth?
o: Permanent rise in standard of living for all citizens
Population is naturally checked by famine, disease and war
Food production automatically doubles to match population
Government subsidies always restore balance immediately
questions.e: Malthus argued that when population grows faster than food supply, positive checks such as famine, disease and war reduce population back to a sustainable level. He did not believe technology would automatically solve the imbalance.
questions.p: Malthus talk say if population pass food, wahala like famine, sickness and war go come reduce them. E no believe say food go just double on its own.

questions.q: In the demographic transition model, a country in the third (late expanding) stage is typically characterised by which combination of birth and death rates?
o: High birth rate and high death rate
Low birth rate and rising death rate
Falling birth rate and already low death rate
High birth rate and rapidly falling death rate
questions.e: In the late expanding stage, death rates have already fallen to a low level while birth rates begin to decline as well, slowing population growth. This is different from the early expanding stage where death rates are still falling rapidly.
questions.p: For the third stage, death rate don already low, and birth rate con dey fall down too. This one dey slow down how population take dey grow.

questions.q: A population pyramid for a typical developing Nigerian community shows a wide base that narrows sharply towards the top. What does this shape indicate?
o: A high proportion of elderly dependents and low birth rate
A declining total population with negative growth rate
A fairly even distribution of population across all age groups
A high birth rate with a large young dependent population
questions.e: A wide base on a population pyramid shows many young people born recently, indicating a high birth rate, while the narrowing top shows fewer people surviving to old age. This pattern is typical of developing countries with high fertility.
questions.p: Wide base for population pyramid mean say plenty pikin dey born, so birth rate high. As e dey narrow go top, naim show say old people no plenty.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major reason why population census figures are often politically sensitive in a federation like Nigeria?
o: Census figures determine the number of years a government stays in office
Census results are used to allocate revenue and political representation among states
Only census figures are used to fix the national minimum wage
Census data decides the exchange rate of the national currency
questions.e: In federations, population figures influence how revenue allocation, constituency boundaries and political representation are shared among states, making census exercises highly sensitive. The other listed uses are not the direct purpose of census data.
questions.p: For Nigeria, census sensitive because na im dem dey use share money and political seat for states. Na that reason make people dey eye census.

questions.q: The theory of optimum population states that for a given level of technology and resources, population growth beyond a certain point leads to which outcome?
o: No effect at all on output per head
Continuous rise in output per head without limit
An automatic increase in available natural resources
A decline in output per head due to diminishing returns
questions.e: Beyond the optimum point, additional population causes output per head to fall because resources and capital are spread more thinly, reflecting diminishing returns. This is the central idea behind the optimum population theory.
questions.p: If population pass where e suppose reach, output per head go begin fall because of diminishing returns. Resources go con small for everybody body.

questions.q: A country has a population density of 180 persons per square kilometre and a total land area of 600,000 square kilometres. What is the total population of the country?
o: 600,180 persons
10,800,000 persons
3,333 persons
questions.e: Population equals density multiplied by land area. Multiplying 180 by 600,000 gives 108,000,000 persons.
questions.p: To find the total population, you just multiply population density by land area. When you multiply 180 by 600,000, you go get 108,000,000 persons.

questions.q: In the demographic transition model, the stage characterised by a high but rapidly falling birth rate alongside a low and stable death rate, leading to a slowing rate of natural increase, is best described as the
o: late expanding stage
low stationary stage
early expanding stage
high stationary stage
questions.e: In the late expanding stage, death rates are already low while birth rates begin to fall rapidly due to social and economic changes, which narrows the gap between births and deaths. This slows population growth compared to the earlier expanding stage.
questions.p: For this stage, death rate dey low already while birth rate dey fall quick quick because of social and economic changes. This one dey make the population growth slow down small compare to before.

questions.q: A state government wants to classify its population into economically active and dependent groups for planning school enrolment and old-age support schemes. Which concept should the planners primarily rely on?
o: Age-sex structure of the population
Net migration rate
Crude birth rate
Population density
questions.e: The age-sex structure shows how many people fall into the young, working, and elderly age groups, which helps planners estimate dependents versus workers. Birth rate, density, and migration do not directly show this grouping.
questions.p: Na the age-sex structure dey show how many people dey young, working class, or old age. E dey help planners know people wey dey work versus those wey dey depend on them.

questions.q: A region has a working population of 450,000 persons, while the number of dependents (children and elderly) is 300,000. What is the dependency ratio of the region, expressed as a ratio of dependents to workers in simplest form?
questions.e: Dependency ratio is dependents divided by workers, which is 300,000 to 450,000, simplifying to 2:3. This means for every 3 working people, there are 2 dependents.
questions.p: Dependency ratio na dependents divide by workers, wey mean 300,000 over 450,000. When you simplify am, e go give you 2:3.

questions.q: According to the theory of optimum population, which of the following statements correctly describes a situation of UNDER-population?
o: Population size is exactly matched with resources so that output per head is at its maximum
Population is so large that output per head is falling as more people are added
Population is too small relative to available resources, so output per head could rise if more people were added
Population growth has stopped completely and the birth rate equals the death rate
questions.e: Under-population occurs when there are too few people to fully exploit a country's resources, meaning adding more workers would raise output per head rather than lower it. This is different from optimum population, where output per head is already maximised, or overpopulation, where adding more people reduces output per head.
questions.p: Under-population happen when people small too much compared to the resources wey dey ground. If more workers join, output per head go even increase instead of to fall.

questions.q: A Nigerian town recorded 2,400 live births and 900 deaths in a particular year out of a mid-year population of 60,000 people. What was the rate of natural increase of the population for that year, expressed as a percentage?
questions.e: Crude birth rate is 2400 divided by 60000 multiplied by 1000, giving 40 per 1000, and crude death rate is 900 divided by 60000 multiplied by 1000, giving 15 per 1000. The natural increase rate is 40 minus 15, which is 25 per 1000, equal to 2.5 percent.
questions.p: Crude birth rate na 40 per 1,000 while crude death rate na 15 per 1,000. When you subtract death rate from birth rate, you go get 25 per 1,000, wey be 2.5 percent.

questions.q: Two farmers, Musa and Ibe, can each produce yam and maize. Musa produces 8 tonnes of yam or 4 tonnes of maize with his resources, while Ibe produces 6 tonnes of yam or 6 tonnes of maize with his. Which statement is correct according to the law of comparative advantage?
o: Musa has comparative advantage in yam while Ibe has comparative advantage in maize
Ibe has comparative advantage in both yam and maize
Musa has comparative advantage in both yam and maize
Musa and Ibe should both specialize in yam only
questions.e: Musa's opportunity cost of 1 tonne yam is 0.5 maize, lower than Ibe's 1 maize, so Musa should specialize in yam. Ibe's opportunity cost of 1 tonne maize is 1 yam, lower than Musa's 2 yams, so Ibe specializes in maize.
questions.p: Musa get comparative advantage for yam because e cost am small to produce am. Ibe get comparative advantage for maize because e cost am small to produce am pass Musa.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a 'fixed exchange rate' system as used in international trade?
o: A system where traders set exchange rates individually for each transaction without central bank involvement
A system where exchange rates are determined solely by the volume of exports a country records
A system where the value of a currency is allowed to fluctuate freely according to market forces of demand and supply
A system where the government or central bank pegs the value of the local currency to another currency or a basket of currencies at an official rate
questions.e: Under a fixed exchange rate system, the monetary authority officially pegs the currency's value to another currency and intervenes to maintain that rate. This contrasts with a floating rate determined by market forces.
questions.p: Fixed exchange rate mean say government or central bank go fix the price of money. Dem no dey allow market forces to just change the rate anyhow.

questions.q: Which of the following is a non-price measure a government can use to correct a persistent balance of payments deficit?
o: Devaluation of the national currency
Raising the exchange rate to make the currency stronger
Imposition of import quotas restricting the quantity of certain goods allowed into the country
Increasing the money supply through the central bank
questions.e: Import quotas are a direct, non-price control that physically limits the quantity of imports, unlike devaluation which works through price changes. This helps reduce spending on foreign goods.
questions.p: Import quota na way to limit the amount of goods wey dey enter country. E no be price change, na direct control to stop too much import.

questions.q: Nigeria exports mainly primary agricultural and mineral products while importing mostly manufactured goods and machinery. Which problem commonly associated with the terms of trade is this pattern likely to cause for Nigeria in the long run?
o: Automatic balance of payments surplus regardless of world prices
A tendency for terms of trade to deteriorate since primary product prices often rise slower than manufactured goods prices
Complete immunity from exchange rate fluctuations
A tendency for terms of trade to improve steadily over time
questions.e: Primary products often face slower price growth and more volatile demand than manufactured goods, so countries exporting primary goods and importing manufactures tend to experience deteriorating terms of trade over time.
questions.p: If country dey export raw materials and dey import finished goods, the terms of trade go spoil with time. The price of raw materials no dey rise like the price of machines and finished goods.

questions.q: In a particular year, Ghana records the following: exports of goods and services worth $900 million, imports of goods and services worth $1,050 million, net income received from abroad of $40 million, and net current transfers received of $30 million. What is the current account balance?
o: -$200 million
-$80 million
$70 million
-$150 million
questions.e: Current account balance equals exports minus imports plus net income plus net transfers: 900 minus 1050 plus 40 plus 30 equals -80. This shows a current account deficit of $80 million.
questions.p: To get current account balance, you go subtract import from export, then add net income and transfers. If you calculate 900 minus 1050 plus 40 plus 30, you go get -80 million.

questions.q: Which of the following best distinguishes the African Development Bank (AfDB) from the World Bank?
o: The AfDB lends exclusively to private commercial banks in Africa
The AfDB focuses mainly on regulating international trade disputes
The AfDB is regionally focused on financing development projects within Africa, while the World Bank operates globally
The AfDB sets production quotas for African oil-exporting countries
questions.e: The AfDB was created specifically to finance economic and social development projects across African countries, unlike the World Bank, which lends to developing countries worldwide. The other options describe functions of different organisations.
questions.p: AfDB get focus for Africa development projects only. World Bank dey work for all over the world. Na why dem different.

questions.q: A member country of OPEC decides, along with other members, to cut its daily crude oil production quota. The most likely immediate effect on the world oil market, all things being equal, is a:
o: Rise in world oil prices due to reduced supply
Rise in world oil prices due to increased supply
Fall in world oil prices due to reduced supply
Fall in world oil prices due to increased demand
questions.e: When OPEC members cut production, total global supply of crude oil falls while demand remains roughly unchanged, so the price tends to rise. This follows the basic law of supply and demand.
questions.p: If supply of oil reduce but demand still dey, price go go up. Na simple law of supply and demand be dat.

questions.q: Under the World Trade Organization's dispute settlement framework, when a member country is found to have violated a trade agreement, the WTO's main role is to:
o: Impose direct military sanctions on the offending country
Automatically expel the offending country from the organisation
Nationalise the assets of companies involved in the dispute
Provide a structured process for resolving the dispute and authorise proportionate trade remedies if needed
questions.e: The WTO dispute settlement system allows aggrieved members to bring complaints, have them adjudicated by panels, and if a violation is confirmed and not corrected, authorises proportionate countermeasures. It does not use military force or expulsion as remedies.
questions.p: WTO dey help settle trade fight between countries. If country break rule, dem fit allow trade punishment but no be military force.

questions.q: A small West African country wants to borrow from the IMF because its foreign reserves can barely cover one month of imports. Which condition is the IMF most likely to attach to such a loan?
o: A requirement to withdraw permanently from international trade agreements
A requirement to adopt macroeconomic reforms such as reducing budget deficits and reforming exchange rate policy
A requirement to increase government subsidies on all consumer goods
A requirement to nationalise all foreign-owned businesses in the country
questions.e: IMF loans to countries facing balance of payments problems usually come with conditions aimed at restoring macroeconomic stability, such as cutting deficits and adjusting exchange rate policy. The other options are not typical IMF loan conditions.
questions.p: IMF dey give loan with condition to fix economy. Dem go ask country to reduce budget deficit and fix exchange rate.

questions.q: A regional trade bloc like ECOWAS aims to deepen integration beyond a simple free trade area by adopting a common external tariff on goods imported from non-member countries. This arrangement, where internal trade is free but external tariffs are harmonised, best describes a:
o: Free trade area
Monetary union
Common market with free labour mobility only
Customs union
questions.e: A customs union combines free trade among members with a common external tariff applied uniformly to non-members, which is more advanced than a plain free trade area that lacks a common tariff. Monetary union involves a shared currency, which is a separate and deeper stage of integration.
questions.p: Customs union mean say members no dey pay tariff among dem, but dem get one common tariff for outside countries. Dis one different from free trade area.

questions.q: In a certain labour market, the equilibrium wage is ₦45 per hour. The government fixes a minimum wage of ₦60 per hour. At this minimum wage, 2,000 workers are willing to work but only 1,400 are demanded by employers. What is the size of the resulting unemployment (labour surplus)?
o: 3,400 workers
1,400 workers
600 workers
2,000 workers
questions.e: Unemployment caused by a minimum wage above equilibrium equals quantity supplied minus quantity demanded, that is 2000 - 1400 = 600. This surplus of labour represents those willing to work but unable to find jobs at that wage.
questions.p: If government put minimum wage high pass where market balance, plenty people go wan work. Na to minus the 1,400 people wey employers want from the 2,000 workers wey ready to work, e come give us 600 workers surplus.

questions.q: A business owned and controlled by one person, who provides the capital, bears all the risks and takes all the profits, is best described as a
o: sole proprietorship
cooperative society
partnership
private limited company
questions.e: A sole proprietorship is a one-man business where a single individual supplies the capital, makes all decisions, bears all risks and keeps all the profit. The other forms involve two or more people sharing ownership.
questions.p: Sole proprietorship na one man business where na only one person dey bring money, make decision, carry all the risk, and pack all the profit. Other business types dey involve two or more people.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major disadvantage of a sole proprietorship as a form of business organisation?
o: Double taxation of profits
Difficulty in reaching quick decisions
Separation of ownership from control
Unlimited liability of the owner
questions.e: In a sole proprietorship, the owner has unlimited liability, meaning personal property can be seized to pay business debts. The other options apply more to partnerships or companies, not sole proprietorships.
questions.p: For sole proprietorship, person get unlimited liability, meaning if business owe debt, dem fit sell your personal property to pay am. Na company and partnership other things dey happen, no be sole proprietorship.

questions.q: In a partnership business, a 'sleeping partner' is one who
o: is liable only for debts incurred during his own transactions
has unlimited liability and manages the firm actively
contributes capital but does not take part in the day-to-day management
manages the business but contributes no capital
questions.e: A sleeping (silent) partner invests money in the business and shares in the profits or losses but does not take part in the active running of the firm. Active or general partners are the ones who manage the business daily.
questions.p: Sleeping partner na person wey put money for business and dey share profit or loss, but e no dey join hand run the business everyday. Na active partners dey manage the business daily.

questions.q: A public limited liability company is best distinguished from a private limited liability company by the fact that the public company
o: can invite members of the public to subscribe for its shares through the stock exchange
must have only two shareholders at formation
is owned and financed entirely by the government
cannot be sued in a law court
questions.e: A public limited company can offer its shares to the general public and list them on the stock exchange, unlike a private limited company whose shares are restricted to a few members. It is not necessarily government owned.
questions.p: Public limited company get power to sell shares to anybody for stock exchange market, unlike private limited company wey members limited. Government no suppose own am by force.

questions.q: The document that states the relationship of a registered company with the outside world, including its name, objectives and registered address, is called the
o: Articles of Association
Memorandum of Association
Certificate of Incorporation
Prospectus
questions.e: The Memorandum of Association governs the company's external relations, stating its name, objectives, registered office and share capital. The Articles of Association, by contrast, deal with the internal rules of the company.
questions.p: Memorandum of Association na the paper wey dey show how company take dey relate with outsiders, including company name and objective. Articles of Association na for internal rules.

questions.q: One key advantage a joint stock company has over a sole proprietorship in raising long-term finance is that the company can
o: obtain unlimited personal loans from its single owner
avoid paying company income tax completely
sell shares and debentures to a large number of investors
operate without keeping any financial records
questions.e: A joint stock company can raise large amounts of capital by issuing shares and debentures to many investors, something a sole proprietor cannot easily do. Companies still pay tax and must keep proper accounts.
questions.p: Joint stock company fit raise plenty money by selling shares and debentures to many investors, wey sole proprietor no fit easily do. Company still dey pay tax and keep account.

questions.q: A cooperative society in Nigeria mainly exists to
o: maximize profit for a few wealthy shareholders
promote the mutual economic welfare of its members through joint effort
replace the role of commercial banks in the economy
operate solely as an agent of the Federal Government
questions.e: Cooperative societies are formed by people with common interests who pool resources together to improve their economic welfare, such as through savings, credit or bulk buying. They are not profit-maximising ventures for a few owners.
questions.p: Cooperative society na people wey join hand together to help themselves economically through savings and bulk buying. E no be business wey dey find excess profit for only few rich people.

questions.q: Adaeze and three friends want to start a transport business. Adaeze contributes ₦2,000,000 and insists on unlimited liability and full control, but her friends want all four of them to share ownership, profits and liability without the cost and complex registration procedure of forming a company. Based on these conditions, the most suitable form of business organisation for them is a
o: statutory corporation
sole proprietorship
public limited company
partnership
questions.e: Since four people want to jointly own, manage and share profits and liabilities without the heavy legal requirements of registering a company, a partnership fits best, as it allows two or more persons to combine capital and skills under simpler rules than a company. A sole proprietorship suits only one owner, while a public company and statutory corporation involve far more formal and extensive registration.
questions.p: Since four people wan join hand business without stress of heavy company registration, partnership fit dem well because e allow people pull resources together under simple rule. Sole proprietorship na for only one person.

questions.q: Distributive trade refers to the activities involved in moving goods from the point of production to the:
o: Point of final consumption
Point of raw material extraction
Point of storage only
Port of export only
questions.e: Distributive trade covers all activities, such as transport, storage and selling, that take goods from producers to final consumers. Storage and extraction are only parts of this chain, not the whole process.
questions.p: Distributive trade na all di work wey dem dey do to carry goods from where dem produce am reach di final person wey go use am. Dis one include transport, storage, and selling.

questions.q: A middleman in commodity marketing is best described as a person who:
o: Links producers and consumers by buying and reselling goods
Manufactures goods for export only
Fixes government prices for farm produce
Regulates the quality standard of exported goods
questions.e: Middlemen are intermediaries who buy from producers and sell to consumers or other middlemen, bridging the gap between the two groups. They do not manufacture goods or fix government prices.
questions.p: Middleman na person wey stand between di person wey produce goods and di person wey go buy am. Dem dey buy and resell to make di work easy for everybody.

questions.q: Chidinma buys bags of garri directly from farmers in Nnewi and sells them in large quantities to retailers in Onitsha market. Chidinma is best classified as a:
o: Commission agent
Wholesaler
Retailer
Broker
questions.e: A wholesaler buys in bulk from producers and sells in fairly large quantities to retailers rather than directly to final consumers. She does not sell in small units to the final consumer like a retailer, nor merely negotiate deals without owning goods like a broker.
questions.p: Wholesaler na person wey dey buy plenty goods from farmer and come sell am for big quantity to retailers. Because Chidinma dey buy plenty and sell to retailers, she be wholesaler.

questions.q: One major advantage of using middlemen in the marketing of farm produce such as tomatoes and pepper in Nigeria is that they:
o: Guarantee that farmers receive the highest possible profit
Eliminate the need for transportation of goods
Help in bulk-breaking and distributing goods to scattered consumers
Always reduce the final price paid by consumers
questions.e: Middlemen break bulk purchases into smaller units and distribute them to widely scattered consumers, which producers alone often cannot do efficiently. They do not automatically lower prices or guarantee farmers maximum profit; in fact they add a margin that can raise consumer prices.
questions.p: Middlemen dey help break big bulk into small-small units so that e go reach people wey dey scattered everywhere. Na true say dem dey help distribute goods well-well.

questions.q: A key difference between a broker and a commission agent in commodity marketing is that the broker:
o: Takes physical possession of the goods being traded
Is always a government-appointed official
Buys goods outright and resells at a personal profit
Does not take possession of goods but only negotiates sales between buyer and seller
questions.e: A broker merely brings buyers and sellers together and negotiates terms without ever owning or holding the goods. A commission agent, however, usually takes possession of goods on behalf of the owner before selling them.
questions.p: Broker no dey touch or keep di goods at all, e just dey help buyer and seller agree on price. Commission agent own different because e fit hold di goods for di owner before e sell am.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major problem associated with the activities of middlemen in the distribution of agricultural produce in Nigeria?
o: They reduce the number of market days available to farmers
They increase the final price of goods to consumers through multiple profit margins
They are legally barred from operating in rural markets
They prevent goods from reaching urban markets entirely
questions.e: Because goods often pass through several middlemen before reaching the final consumer, each one adds a profit margin, which raises the final price. Middlemen do not stop goods from reaching urban areas; rather, they help distribute them.
questions.p: As goods dey pass from one middleman to another, each person go add im own profit. Dis one come make di final price wey consumer go pay come high too much.

questions.q: A commodity board set up by a government mainly performs which function in marketing?
o: Buying farm produce from farmers at fixed prices and organising export or resale
Manufacturing finished goods from raw materials for local consumption
Setting retail prices for all imported manufactured goods
Producing the commodity directly on large plantations
questions.e: A commodity board typically purchases produce such as cocoa or groundnuts from farmers at a set price, then handles grading, storage and export or resale, acting as a stabilising middleman. It does not itself produce or manufacture goods; its role is organisational and regulatory in marketing.
questions.p: Commodity board na government body wey dey buy farm produce from farmers for fixed price. Dem dey handle export and storage to make sure say market price no scatter.

questions.q: Mr. Bello, a wholesaler, buys 500 crates of eggs from a farm at ₦1,200 per crate and sells all of them to retailers at ₦1,450 per crate. If he also pays a total of ₦25,000 as transport and storage cost for the whole consignment, what is his net profit?
questions.e: Total selling price is 500 times 1450 equals 725,000 naira, and total cost price is 500 times 1200 equals 600,000 naira, giving a gross profit of 125,000 naira. Subtracting the 25,000 naira expenses leaves a net profit of 100,000 naira.
questions.p: Total sales na 725,000 naira, while total cost na 600,000 naira plus 25,000 naira for transport. If you remove 625,000 naira from 725,000 naira, you go get 100,000 naira profit.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the main function of a wholesaler in the chain of distributive trade?
o: Setting the final retail price of goods by law
Manufacturing goods for direct sale to final consumers
Buying in bulk from producers and selling in smaller quantities to retailers
Advertising goods on behalf of the government
questions.e: A wholesaler buys goods in large quantities from producers and breaks them into smaller lots for retailers. This bridges the gap between producers and retailers in distributive trade.
questions.p: Wholesaler dey buy plenty goods from producer come break am small-small for retailer. Na so dem dey bridge the gap between producer and retailer for trade.

questions.q: A retailer is best defined as a trader who:
o: Transports goods in bulk from one country to another
Negotiates prices between two wholesalers without taking ownership of goods
Buys raw materials and processes them into finished goods
Sells goods in small quantities directly to final consumers
questions.e: Retailers are the last link in distributive trade, buying from wholesalers or producers and selling in small units to final consumers. This makes goods accessible for everyday household purchase.
questions.p: Retailer na the last person for the chain, e dey buy from wholesaler come sell small-small to final consumer. Na dem dey make goods easy for people to buy for house.

questions.q: Which of these is a major function performed by commodity marketing boards in Nigeria for export crops such as cocoa and groundnut?
o: Printing new currency notes for farmers
Granting university scholarships to traders
Stabilising producer prices paid to farmers
Fixing exchange rates for the naira
questions.e: Commodity marketing boards buy produce from farmers at guaranteed prices to protect them from sharp price fluctuations in world markets. This stabilises farmers' incomes and encourages continued production.
questions.p: Marketing board dey buy crop from farmer for fixed price so say price no go just dey jump up and down. This one dey help farmer get steady money and continue their work.

questions.q: One of the following is a disadvantage associated with the operation of commodity marketing boards on farmers:
o: Farmers may be paid prices below the prevailing world market price
Farmers are forced to relocate to urban areas
Farmers automatically receive higher prices than the world market
Farmers lose the right to grow their own crops
questions.e: Marketing boards sometimes pay farmers less than the actual world price and keep the difference as surplus, which discourages some producers. This is a commonly cited weakness of such boards.
questions.p: Sometimes marketing board dey pay farmer money wey small pass wetin dem for get for world market. This one dey make some farmer vex and stop to produce.

questions.q: In distributive trade, a chain store differs from a departmental store mainly because a chain store:
o: Exists only to export goods to other countries
Operates many branches of similar shops in different locations under one ownership
Sells only one type of product in a single large building
Is owned jointly by farmers in a cooperative society
questions.e: A chain store consists of several branch shops in different towns or areas, all owned and controlled by the same company, selling similar goods. A departmental store, by contrast, is usually one large building with different sections under one roof.
questions.p: Chain store get many branches for different place but na one person get all of dem. Departmental store na just one big building wey get different sections inside.

questions.q: Alhaji Musa buys 2000 tubers of yam from farmers in Benue at ₦250 each and transports them to Lagos, where he sells all the tubers to retailers at ₦340 each. If his total transport and handling cost for the whole consignment was ₦60,000, what is his net profit?
questions.e: Total cost of buying is 2000 times 250 equals 500,000, and revenue from selling is 2000 times 340 equals 680,000, giving a gross profit of 180,000. Subtracting the 60,000 transport cost leaves a net profit of 120,000 naira.
questions.p: Total cost na 500,000 naira, and total sales na 680,000 naira. If you remove 60,000 naira for transport, the profit wey remain na 120,000 naira.

questions.q: A major problem facing distributive trade in rural parts of Nigeria is poor road networks. Which of the following is the most direct effect of this problem on commodity marketing?
o: Permanent closure of all rural markets
Automatic reduction in the price of farm produce
Increased cost of transporting goods and higher spoilage of perishable produce
Elimination of the need for middlemen in trade
questions.e: Poor roads make it difficult and costly to move goods, especially perishables like tomatoes, from farms to markets, leading to higher transport costs and spoilage. This ultimately raises the final price paid by consumers.
questions.p: Bad road dey make transport cost high and e dey make perishable goods spoil quick. This one dey make price of food come high for market.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why hawkers are considered an important part of the distributive trade system in many Nigerian towns, despite having no fixed business premises?
o: They control the supply of foreign exchange to traders
They fix the national price of goods sold in the country
They are licensed to issue import permits to wholesalers
They bring goods close to consumers in areas not easily reached by shops
questions.e: Hawkers move goods directly to where consumers live and work, reaching remote streets and areas without shops. This convenience makes them a useful, if small-scale, link in the distributive trade chain despite lacking a permanent shop.
questions.p: Hawker dey carry goods reach where shop no dey, so e dey easy for consumer to buy. Even though dem no get shop, dem dey help move goods well-well.
